# docserver L1 — rules and corpus Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking. The programme's coordinator dispatches this wave as one run (see "How this wave runs" below). The worker carries it out under the `ccrc-worker` skill.

**Goal:** Ship the first layer of `@synapsium-labs/docserver`. That is a pure `render()` and `scanRefs()` whose HTML matches the reference renderer's, apart from eight ruled departures, PD1-PD8 (PD8 is a set of bounds only hostile documents reach). It also includes a conformance corpus that any consumer can run against its own render function.

**Architecture:** One package sits at the repo root and has two ESM entries:
- `./render` is pure. It is markdown-it with ported rules for the raw-HTML allowlist, details balancing, heading ids, `data-line`, fences, Mermaid figures and captions, alerts, tables, task lists and front matter, plus `meta` and `scanRefs`.
- `./conformance` is Node-only. It holds `loadCorpus`, `runCorpus`, the output-safety oracle and verdicts.

The corpus has 77 cases: 37 golden, 15 hostile with goldens and 25 generated. Its goldens come from the reference renderer and are normalised only for code highlighting. CI runs both typechecks, the tests and the build, then the verdict ratchet, then a smoke test that installs the packed tarball as a consumer would.

**Tech Stack:**
- Node `>=22`. CI runs Node 22 and 24. The plan was measured on Node 24.14.1 with npm 11.11.0.
- Dependencies, exact pins:
  - `markdown-it` 14.3.2;
  - `markdown-it-footnote` 4.0.0;
  - `js-yaml` 4.3.2;
  - `highlight.js` 11.12.0.
- Dev dependencies, exact pins:
  - `typescript` 6.0.3;
  - `vitest` 4.1.11;
  - `@types/node` 22.20.4;
  - `@types/js-yaml` 4.0.9;
  - `@types/markdown-it` 14.2.0;
  - `esbuild` 0.28.2.
- Every pin is installed with `--before=2026-09-28T00:00:00Z` (rulings C6 and C7).
- CI uses `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/setup-node@v4`.
- The dev-only reference is Python 3.12.3 with markdown-it-py 4.2.0, mdit-py-plugins 0.6.1, Pygments 2.20.0 and PyYAML 6.0.3. The renderer's sha256 is `26a04a16547a657aa56653b6aa4a23a833ebede47b061b1156010ae66fc9ad06`.

**Spec:** [Rich Docs reader and a shared renderer](https://github.com/Synapsium-Labs/ccrc-pwa/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-rich-docs-reader-and-shared-renderer-design.md). §3 covers the library and §8 covers sequencing.

## Global Constraints

- **Public-ready from the first commit.** This covers code, tests, fixtures, corpus prose, CI, package metadata and commit messages. None of them may hold a host, user, private path, project list, issue-tracker workspace, private product name or operator default. Corpus prose is invented, and e-mail addresses use reserved example domains only. T12's `public-ready.test.ts` scans the tree. `docs/` is outside the scan and is scrubbed before L3.
- **The reference renderer is passed by argument only (C5).**
  - Run `"$REFERENCE_PYTHON" -I scripts/golden/generate.py --renderer "$REFERENCE_RENDERER" …`. The coordinator supplies both on the worker's command lines.
  - No tracked file, task text or commit holds either path.
  - If a version or the renderer hash differs from the pins above, the task stops and asks.
  - `PROVENANCE.json` holds versions and hashes only.
  - Once the reference retires, `reference/` is frozen provenance and `expected/` is the contract.
- **`./render` is pure (C18).**
  - No network, storage, git, clock, randomness or environment variables, and no globals beyond JS intrinsics. Output is deterministic for each input and set of options.
  - Per-render state lives in `RenderEnv`.
  - `tsconfig.render.json` (lib ES2022, `types: []`) loads no `lib.dom`. Its `paths` map highlight.js to `src/types/purity/*.d.ts` from T1 on (C18).
  - Only `./conformance` touches `node:*`.
- **There is one allowlist.** It holds `<br>` forms, bare `sup`, `sub` and `kbd`, `details` and `summary` lines, and `<!-- id:X -->` with X matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}`.
  - The same code runs in Node, browsers and workers, with no environment branch.
  - Tag names fold ASCII letters only (C9, PD5).
- **Cost is bounded, not only input.** `maxBytes` caps the input. Inside it, the comment searches are linear (T5: a document-wide index, and memories per inline text and per closing line), highlighting is bounded per fence line and per document (T6), the empty cells tables add are bounded per document (T8), `maxHtmlBytes` caps the html (T3, C20) and the four allowlisted tags nest at most 64 deep (T5, C21). Each bound has a generated case in T11. The last three are departure PD8 (C19).
- **There is no raw-HTML path.**
  - The engine is `new MarkdownIt('commonmark', { html: false, xhtmlOut: true, … })`, with `maxNesting` 20. `validateLink` and `normalizeLink` are untouched.
  - A failure renders `<p class="page-subtitle">This document could not be rendered; its source follows.</p><pre>`, then the escaped source, then `</pre>`.
- **Escaping follows the reference.** `escapeHtml` is used wherever markdown-it uses it. `pyEscape` (which also turns `'` into `&#x27;`) is used wherever Python used `html.escape`: summary text, Mermaid source, front-matter `dt` and `dd`, and the failure fallback.
- **Python text semantics go through `pyText.ts` only (C8, C10).**
  - `PY_WS`, `pyStrip`, `cpLength`, `cpSlice` and `utf8Length` live there.
  - `pyLower` is whole-string `toLowerCase()`, so `ΟΔΟΣ` becomes `οδος`, as in CPython.
  - `block_strip` (T4) strips heading, setext and paragraph text.
  - The table block rule is ported with `pyStrip` (T8).
  - No raw `\s`, `.`, `trim`, `toLowerCase` or `.slice` where Python semantics apply.
- **Engine chains (C7, C8), pinned by `test/engine.test.ts`:**
  - Core: `normalize, block, block_strip, inline, footnote_tail, task_lists, text_join, anchors, balance_details, alerts, figcaption, table_code, line_attrs`.
  - Block: `front_matter` first, with alternatives `paragraph, reference, blockquote, list`. `safe_block_html` comes before `html_block`, with alternatives `paragraph, reference, blockquote`.
  - Inline: `safe_inline_html` comes before `html_inline`.
- **API (C2, C3):**
  - `render(md, { maxBytes?, maxHtmlBytes?, lineAttrs? })` returns `{ html, outcome: 'rendered' | 'over-limit' | 'output-over-limit' | 'failed', bytes, meta }`. `maxHtmlBytes` defaults to 16777216 (16 MiB, four times `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES`); past it the render stops with `'output-over-limit'` and the escaped-source fallback, cut to the bound (C20).
  - `meta` is `{ front, frontList, title, headings, figures, tables, mermaidKinds }`. It is frozen `EMPTY_META` unless the outcome is `rendered`.
  - `scanRefs(md, { maxBytes?, maxImages? })` returns `{ outcome: 'scanned' | 'over-limit', images, imagesTruncated, mermaid }`.
  - `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` is 4194304 and `DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES` is 512. An invalid limit (`maxHtmlBytes` included) throws `RangeError`.
  - Ids are not unique across kinds (C22): heading ids keep the reference's de-duplication, `<!-- id:X -->` anchors are emitted as written, and the footnotes' `fn1`/`fnref1` are unprefixed. The README tells hosts never to look an element up by a document id.
- **The corpus is the contract (C1, C14).**
  - Every change under `conformance/expected/` carries a `Goldens-moved: <id>, <id>` trailer naming exactly the changed ids, new goldens included.
  - A hostile verdict only ever tightens.
  - `node scripts/ratchet.mjs --base <ref>` enforces both rules.
  - `UPDATE_EXPECTED=1` writes only cases that have no departure, and CI never sets it.
- **Mutation discipline.**
  - Each task lists its rows, `L1-T<n>-M<k>` (`file`, `old`, `new`, `tests`, `red`), in one JSON fence.
  - Rows are measured with Task 1's `mutate.mjs`, each in its own throwaway copy outside the checkout.
  - A row that does not go red is rewritten with a case that does, or reported. It is never dropped.
  - When a later task re-spells a row's anchor, it re-anchors that row. Rows that print `NOT APPLIED` at a later state are reported; the final state's list is under "How this wave runs".
- **Exact pins (C6, C7).**
  - `.npmrc` sets `save-exact=true` and `engine-strict=true`.
  - The lockfile is committed and CI uses `npm ci`.
  - Every version is at least 14 days old. Installs use `--before=<a cutoff at least 14 days back>`, so transitive dependencies obey the rule too.
- **No network in tests.** `test/setup/no-network.ts` makes `fetch` and every socket connect throw. Only `npm ci` and CI's consumer-smoke install reach the registry.
- **Node.** `engines.node` is `>=22`, `@types/node` is 22.x, and no API newer than Node 22.0 is used.
- **Tests (C11).**
  - Run `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run [file]` in the foreground, never a bare `npx vitest`.
  - `npm run typecheck` runs both tsconfigs.
  - The vitest projects `unit`, `browser` and `pack` run in that order.
  - `maxMs` is `max(1000, 10 × the median of 5 runs)`, rounded up to 100.
  - The comment-scan tests keep their 5 s backstops.
  - A timing red on a loaded box is re-run in isolation. `timeScale` loosens a run, never `hostile.json`.
- **CI and the repository (C4).**
  - `ci.yml` runs on pull requests, on pushes to `main` and by hand, with `contents: read`. Its checks are `test (22)` and `test (24)`.
  - L1 changes no repository setting, branch protection, ruleset or `delete_branch_on_merge`.
- **Commits.** One commit per task, with files staged by name. The subject is `<area>: <what> (docserver L1)`. The trailer is the `Co-Authored-By:` of the model that wrote the commit. Commits go on the workspace branch, and no task pushes.
- **Edits are located by content.** Each task's Step 0 checks the state the previous task left. If a check or a Find block fails, stop and ask the coordinator; never guess.
- **Escapes.** Test files hold `\uXXXX` escapes literally. If an editor decodes them, write the file with a heredoc. Each task's grep checks this.
- **Docker:** none.
- **Deferred to L2 and L3:** CSS, fonts, the Mermaid bundle and its options, `enhance`, `frameDocument`, `host`, `assets.json`, publishing, provenance and the public flip.

## Departures from the reference renderer

| ID | What differs | Why | Ruling | Pinned by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PD1 | Code highlighting. highlight.js replaces Pygments. `normaliseForCompare` replaces the inner HTML of each `div.codehilite > pre` with its escaped text. The wrapper, its `data-line` and everything outside it stay byte-exact. | The two tokenisers differ, and no class map reaches byte equality. L2 remaps the CSS to `hljs-*`. | C1 | T2 `test/normalise.test.ts` (M2.1 scope, M2.2 text); T3's `runCorpus` compares normalised HTML. No file moves. |
| PD2 | Front-matter scalars. `null`, `~` and an empty value render `''`. `true`/`True`/`TRUE` and `false`/`False`/`FALSE` render `true` and `false`. Every other scalar renders its source text, for example `1.50`, `.inf`, `017`, `0o17`, a 20-digit integer, `yes`, `on` and dates. The schema is js-yaml's `FAILSAFE_SCHEMA` plus null, bool and merge, in JSON mode. Under C17 it also covers: (a) array-index keys listed first; (b) a last block scalar keeps its trailing `\n`; (c) a sequence key loads as joined text; (d) nesting deeper than 100 renders nothing; (e) a late `<<` puts the merged keys last. Tags outside the schema, `!!int` and `!!float` among them, fail the load. U+0085 is not a line break. A null list item renders `''`. | A public library should not print Python's `None` or `True`. A display library shows what the author wrote, and JS numbers would lose precision. | C1, C15, C16, C17 | T9 `test/frontmatter.test.ts` (the PD2 block, with one case for each of C17's items); rows L1-T9-M12, M13, M35 and M43-M48. `DEPARTURES.json`: `frontmatter-types` (html, meta). |
| PD3 | `meta.front` and `meta.frontList` come from the same block the strip renders. CRLF files, `----`, `...` closers and `--- x` openers now get a list where the reference gave `null`. | With one parser, the strip and `meta` cannot disagree. | C1 | T9 `test/frontmatter.test.ts` (the PD3 block). `DEPARTURES.json`: the meta of `frontmatter-openers/{dashes4,dots,space-open}` and `line-endings/crlf`. |
| PD4 | One leading U+FEFF is removed before parsing (`bytes` still counts it). | Otherwise a BOM file's front matter rendered as a setext heading. | C1 | T9 `test/frontmatter.test.ts` (the PD4 block); `stripBom` in T10's `render.ts`. `DEPARTURES.json`: `line-endings/bom` (html, meta). |
| PD5 | Allowlisted tag names fold ASCII letters only. U+0130, U+0131, U+212A and U+017F stay escaped text. | The reference's `re.I` emitted raw tags outside the allowlist and misread a `summary` line. | C9 | T5 `test/allowlist.test.ts` "look-alike letters are text" (rows L1-T5-M13, M14); T12's README row and `readme.test.ts`. No file moves. |
| PD6 | Reference labels. markdown-it normalises a link's reference label with JavaScript's `trim()` and `\s`, the reference with Python's, so a label holding `\x1c`-`\x1f`, `\u0085` or `\ufeff` matches a different definition, or none. Measured for all six characters in three shapes (between two words, at the end of a definition's label, as the whole label): all 18 differ. PD6 stays authorised only for whitespace that markdown-it trims before any hook can run; tables need none (T8 ports the table rule with `pyStrip`, and T4's `block_strip` covers headings and paragraphs). | Parity first; a departure only for a residue no hook can recover. A key-mapping hook on `env.references` could recover two of the three shapes for five characters and none for U+FEFF, so PD6 would stand anyway; porting markdown-it's `reference`, `link` and `image` rules is not worth the risk. | C10, C23 | T4 `test/blockstrip.test.ts` (18 unit cases, each pinning both outputs; no mutation row, since no code of this library makes the difference); T8 `test/tables.test.ts`; T12's README row and `readme.test.ts` (row L1-T12-M33). No file moves. |
| PD7 | A figure caption never comes from a hidden (tight-list) paragraph and never reaches past the block after its figure, so the HTML stays balanced. The reference's caption pattern pulled `</em></li></ul><p><em>y` into the `figcaption`. | Parity would mean emitting unbalanced HTML. | C12 | T7 `test/figcaption.test.ts` "where this library differs from the reference", which pins both outputs; row L1-T7-M3; T12's README row and `readme.test.ts` (row L1-T12-M32). No file moves. |
| PD8 | Bounds that only hostile documents reach. (a) The limit of 65536 empty cells that short table rows may add holds for the whole document as well as for each table (T8): markdown-it and the reference count per table only, and 64 tables of 1807 bytes exhausted the heap, a fatal error `render()` cannot catch. (b) The html is capped at `maxHtmlBytes`, default 16 MiB (T3, C20): a 304 KB input that rendered 200 MB of html now stops with outcome `'output-over-limit'` and the escaped-source fallback, cut to the bound. (c) `details`, `sup`, `sub` and `kbd` nest at most 64 open levels each (T5, C21); an opener past the cap, and the closer that pairs with it, stay escaped text, so the output stays balanced. | Bounded cost and output for any input under `maxBytes`, and no fragment deep enough to overflow a consumer's recursive walk. No golden case reaches any of the three bounds, so every golden stays unchanged. | C19, C20, C21 | (a) T8 `test/tables.test.ts` (row L1-T8-M28); T11 `x-tables/many-ragged` (row L1-T11-M40). (b) T3 `test/render-shell.test.ts` (rows L1-T3-M32-M42); T11 `x-limits/html-expansion` (rows L1-T11-M46, M47). (c) T5 `test/allowlist.test.ts` (rows L1-T5-M28-M35); T11 `x-details-10000-unclosed` and `x-inline-unclosed/sup-100000` (row L1-T11-M48). T12's README row and `readme.test.ts` (rows L1-T12-M34, M35). No file moves. |

**The rule.** The list above is closed. Any other difference from the reference is a parity bug to fix, not a departure. A new departure needs a coordinator ruling (the next is C24), recorded in the ledger before any file moves. It then needs a `DEPARTURES.json` entry if a file moves, a README row and a test that pins both outputs.

## Coordinator rulings

The full text of each ruling, with its reason and what it costs if wrong, goes into the programme ledger, `docs/superpowers/programs/docserver.md`, under "Decisions & deviations", in the same pull request that merges this plan (see "How this wave runs"). Until then the coordinator's rulings file is the record.

- **C1:** PD1-PD4 are accepted as the closed departure list (T2, T9).
- **C2:** API shape. `render()` returns `{html, outcome, bytes, meta}`, with `meta` holding front, frontList, title, headings, figures, tables and mermaidKinds. `scanRefs` gains `outcome` and `imagesTruncated` (T1, T3, T10).
- **C3:** `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` is 4 MiB and `DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES` is 512; hosts pass their own (T1).
- **C4:** No change to repository settings. CI runs on pull requests and on `main`. Actions minutes are unmeasured, and the operator is told. The coordinator merges with `gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit <sha>`, giving `--body` one `Goldens-moved:` trailer block (see "How this wave runs"; T1, T12).
- **C5:** The generator takes the reference interpreter and renderer as arguments only, and no tracked file names a path (T2).
- **C6:** Every pin is at least 14 days old. markdown-it 15 is used only if gate D1 passes, otherwise 14.3.2 (T1, T3).
- **C7:** The pins are js-yaml 4.3.2, markdown-it 14.3.2 with `@types/markdown-it` 14.2.0 (D1 fired because 15.0.2 changed img alt text), typescript 6.0.3, vitest 4.1.11, `@types/node` 22.20.4 and esbuild 0.28.2. Installs use `--before` (T1, T3).
- **C8:** `line_attrs` lands in T3 and `block_strip` in T4. The core chain is as given in Global Constraints. `pyLower` is whole-string lower-casing (T3, T4).
- **C9:** PD5, tag names fold ASCII letters only (T5).
- **C10:** PD6 is authorised only for a residue no hook can restore, and a hook is tried first. Tables needed none (T8); reference labels are PD6 under C23.
- **C11:** The 5 s comment-scan backstops stay. `x-comments/block-20000` and `x-comments/inline-40000` are added with verdicts (T5, T11).
- **C12:** PD7, captions never cross a tight list's end (T7; its README row in T12).
- **C13:** The anchor after a blockquote that a details line ends. The comment index spans the document (`state.bMarks.length - 1`) from Task 5 on, with two unit cases and row L1-T5-M25; the corpus case `h-anchor-after-summary-nested` arrives with the other hostile cases in T11 (rows L1-T11-M37-M39).
- **C14:** The `nest_list` probe is last in `lists-tasks` from Task 2 on, so `ordered_start` and `tasklist_nested` render and M8.5 goes red through them (T2; row L1-T8-M5).
- **C15:** The YAML merge key is accepted (T9).
- **C16:** Front-matter scalars render their source text. The schema is FAILSAFE plus null, bool and merge, and PD2 is restated (T9).
- **C17:** PD2 also covers the loader differences (a)-(e), failing tags, U+0085 and null list items. Each is pinned by a unit case in T9's PD2 block; they come from js-yaml and JavaScript's object order, not from a guard here, so they have no mutation row.
- **C18:** The `lib.dom` leak through highlight.js's `/// <reference lib="dom" />` is closed by `paths` in `tsconfig.render.json` from Task 1 on (it breaks none of Tasks 1-5's reds, measured), pinned there by row L1-T1-M15 and checked by T12's purity test (rows L1-T12-M6, M27). It is a finding against T1 and T6, recorded in the ledger with the rulings.
- **C19:** PD8, resource bounds that only hostile documents reach, is accepted as one departure category. It covers the document-wide empty-cell limit (`env.emptyCells`, 65536; T8) and the bounds of C20 and C21. Each bound has a generated hostile case and a mutation row; no golden moves (T8, T11, T12's README).
- **C20:** The html is bounded. `RenderOptions` gains `maxHtmlBytes`, default 16 MiB (four times `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES`), stated in the type and the README. When the html would pass it, `render()` stops and returns its failure shape with the distinct outcome `'output-over-limit'`, never folded into `'rendered'` or `'over-limit'`; the html is the escaped-source fallback, cut so it too stays within the bound. Placed in `render()`'s shell (T3, rows L1-T3-M32-M42), with the generated case `x-limits/html-expansion` (T11, rows L1-T11-M46, M47). Part of PD8.
- **C21:** Allowlisted tags nest at most 64 open levels per kind (`details`, `sup`, `sub`, `kbd`). An opener past the cap renders as escaped text, and so does the closer that pairs with it, so the output stays balanced. The verdicts of `x-details-10000-unclosed` and `x-inline-unclosed/sup-100000` require that bound (T5, rows L1-T5-M28-M35; T11, row L1-T11-M48). Part of PD8.
- **C22:** Ids keep parity in L1: no prefix and no de-duplication across kinds. Heading slugs keep the reference's de-duplication and comment-anchor ids are emitted as written. The README and `types.ts` state that ids may collide and that hosts must never look an element up by a document id (T12, row L1-T12-M36); L2's `enhance` rule says the same, and L2 revisits this if the layout needs unique ids.
- **C23:** Reference labels: the residue is recorded as PD6, as C10 authorised, and markdown-it's three rules are not ported. Each measured difference (`\x1c`-`\x1f`, `\u0085`, `\ufeff`) is pinned by a unit case, not a golden (T4, 18 cases). A key-mapping hook was allowed if cheap; none is added, because it would leave PD6 standing (T4, decision 9).

**Open at planning: ruled.** The five items this plan left open were ruled on 2026-10-13 and are applied in the tasks that own them:
1. The document-wide empty-cell limit is departure PD8 (C19; T8).
2. The html is bounded by `maxHtmlBytes` with the outcome `'output-over-limit'` (C20; T3, T11).
3. Allowlisted tags nest at most 64 deep (C21; T5, T11).
4. Ids keep parity, and the README warns that they may collide (C22; T12).
5. Reference labels are PD6, pinned by unit cases (C23; T4).

Nothing is left open.

## Review Focus

These are the five inputs most likely to bite a user that no single task fully covers:

1. **Hostile HTML, links and attributes in a document.**
   - Inputs: `<script>` in any case, `<img onerror>`, `javascript:` in any spelling, attributes smuggled onto `sup`, `kbd` or `br`, fence info strings and Mermaid source that close their `<pre>`, and look-alike tag letters.
   - Each stays escaped text or an unlinked reference, and every output passes the oracle.
   - Pinned by T3 (`oracle.test.ts`, M3.1-M3.3), T5 (`allowlist.test.ts`, L1-T5-M13 and M14), T6 (`fence.test.ts`) and T11 (the `h-*` verdicts).
2. **Anchor comments and details lines inside quotes, lists and tables.**
   - Inputs: `> - x` / `> <!-- id:a -->` / `<summary>s</summary>` / `<!-- id:b -->`, multi-line comments, a stray `</details>`, and 10 000 unclosed `<details>`.
   - Every valid anchor renders as a `doc-anchor` span, no empty `<p>` appears, `details` stays balanced, and it nests at most 64 deep (C21).
   - Pinned by T5 (`allowlist.test.ts`, ruling C13's two unit cases among them), T8 (`comment-anchors` with tables) and T11 (`h-anchor-after-summary-nested`).
3. **Front matter as authors write it.**
   - Inputs: `version: 1.0`, `017`, `.inf`, `yes`, null, booleans, dates, merge keys, alias bombs, unknown tags, `__proto__` keys, 41 keys, astral characters at the 500-code-point cut, CRLF files and BOM files.
   - The strip and `meta` agree, keep the author's text, and `front` has a null prototype.
   - Pinned by T9 (`frontmatter.test.ts`, one case for each of C17's items) and T11 (the `h-frontmatter-hostile/*` verdicts).
4. **Very large or pathological documents.**
   - Inputs: 10 000 nested `>`, 4096-character delimiter runs, 90 000 `***` lines, 20 000 identical headings, 20 000 unterminated `<!--` lines, images whose alt text opens a comment, thousands of `<!--` lines that reach one long closing line, 2000-column tables and many tables that each reach the empty-cell limit, 200 KB of hostile code, 30000-character lines in the slow grammars, 1 MiB of code, 100 000 unclosed `<sup>`, 304 KB whose html would be 200 MB, and an input one byte over the cap.
   - Each renders within its structural and time bounds, returns `over-limit` with `html === ''`, or returns `output-over-limit` with the escaped fallback within `maxHtmlBytes`.
   - Pinned by T11 (the corpus verdicts and `hostile-input.test.ts`), on top of the linear rewrites and bounds in T4 (the slug uniquifier), T5 (the comment search and its memories), T6 (the highlighting bounds) and T8 (the task-list parent search and the document-wide empty-cell limit). `maxMs` can flake on a loaded box: re-run in isolation and never loosen `hostile.json`. T3's html bound and T5's nesting cap (PD8) bound the output.
5. **The same document in a browser, a worker and through the packed package.**
   - The esbuild bundle runs in an empty VM context and gives JSON-identical `render()` and `scanRefs()` results to Node.
   - No DOM or host global is reachable.
   - A deep import is refused with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`.
   - The consumer's own `runCorpus(render, { scanRefs })` passes from the tarball.
   - Pinned by T12 (`browser-parity`, `purity`, `pack` and `scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs`).

## How this wave runs (coordinator)

- **The plan reaches `main` first.** This plan merges to the docserver repo's `main`, under `docs/superpowers/plans/`, before the run opens.
- **One run, one fresh workspace.** The programme's coordinator opens one run row for docserver wave L1 (`ccrc-coordinator` skill). That mints a fresh child workspace in the docserver repo from `main`, after this plan has merged. Task 1's Step 0 checks for the seed state: no `package.json`, `src`, `test` or `.github`, and a clean tree.
- **The brief carries wave specifics only:** this plan's path, Tasks 1-12, the base commit, the branch-discipline sentence, and that the reference interpreter and renderer are supplied as `$REFERENCE_PYTHON` and `$REFERENCE_RENDERER` on command lines. Tasks 2 and 11 run the generator.
- **Commit on the workspace branch.** The worker commits on the workspace's own branch, never on a separate feature branch.
- **Routing.**
  - The worker runs Tasks 1-12 in order.
  - The main loop is Opus. Implementers are native `sonnet` subagents, and each task's diff is reviewed by an `opus` task reviewer before the next task starts.
  - Never Fable, and workflows are off.
  - Questions go to the coordinator as structured asks. A failed Step 0 or Find block stops the task.
- **Held-out whole-branch review.** After Task 12 and before the close, an `opus` whole-branch review reads the branch against this plan, the Global Constraints, the departure list and the Review Focus. Its fixes are separate commits ending `(docserver L1 review)`. Task 12's final gate is then run again, along with the whole mutation table.
  - **Rows that print `NOT APPLIED` at the final state.** Measured at Task 12's state, the whole table of 357 rows gives 338 red and these 19 `NOT APPLIED` (their `old` occurs 0 times), each expected. They are reported, not rewritten; any other `NOT APPLIED`, and any `NOT RED`, is a finding.
    - `L1-T1-M1`: Task 3 pins markdown-it 14.3.2 (decision gate D1), so `"markdown-it": "15.0.2"` is gone. The exact-pin tests it reds still hold: the same edit on `"14.3.2"` is red, `3 failed | 7 passed (10)`.
    - `L1-T2-M6` and `L1-T2-M7`: their `old` is the empty `conformance/DEPARTURES.json` (`[]`), which Task 9 fills. The same edits on the filled list (a stale `headings` entry first; `frontmatter-types` filed under `PD9`) are red in `test/expected.test.ts`.
    - `L1-T3-M33`: Task 10 re-spells the `maxHtmlBytes` check as `checkLimit('render', 'maxHtmlBytes', ...)`, and row `L1-T10-M21` re-anchors it.
    - `L1-T4-M9`: Task 5 re-spells `createEnv`'s return (it gains `comments`, and later tasks add a field per line), and row `L1-T5-M36` re-anchors it on the function's first line.
    - `L1-T6-M11`: Task 7 re-spells `lineAttr`'s test as `env.lineAttrs && lined(token)`, and row `L1-T7-M28` re-anchors it.
    - `L1-T9-M21` and `L1-T9-M22`: Task 10 moves the BOM line into `stripBom`, and row `L1-T10-M19` stands in for both.
    - The eleven pending-list rows `L1-T3-M26`, `L1-T4-M17`, `L1-T4-M18`, `L1-T5-M23`, `L1-T5-M24`, `L1-T6-M23`, `L1-T6-M24`, `L1-T7-M26`, `L1-T7-M27`, `L1-T8-M26` and `L1-T8-M27`: each anchors `test/corpus-pending.json` as it stood after its own task (an opening `{` followed by entries, or an entry a later task removes), and the file is `{}` from Task 9 on. Pending honesty at the final state is measured by the rows on `{}`: `L1-T9-M41`, `L1-T9-M42`, `L1-T10-M18`, `L1-T11-M30` and `L1-T12-M24`.
- **The close.**
  1. The worker pushes the workspace branch and opens ONE pull request.
  2. The PR body links this plan's `blob/main` URL, the `npm view` record for each pin, and the mutation table's results.
  3. CI runs on that PR. Actions minutes on the private repo are unmeasured (C4).
  4. The worker lists mail, measures the fingerprint (the handoff commit is the branch tip, with the PR's number and phase `open`) and sends the wave-done.
- **Review.** On a verified wave-done, the coordinator dispatches one `ccrc-reviewer` run, which reads the branch at one measured tip in its own worktree and mails one report. The coordinator rules on it.
- **Merge.** The merge is the coordinator's act, after review and a green CI: `gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit <sha> --body "$BODY"`. Nobody changes repository settings, branch protection, rulesets or `delete_branch_on_merge` (C4).
  - **Why `--body`.** A squash merge leaves one commit, and CI's ratchet on the push to `main` reads trailers from the commits that push adds, here that one. GitHub's default squash body joins the branch's messages, and git reads only the last paragraph as trailers, so Task 2's 51-id, Task 9's six-id and Task 11's one-id `Goldens-moved:` trailers would be lost while every file under `conformance/expected/` shows as changed, and the first run on `main` would go red.
  - **The body.** `BODY` is a short summary, a blank line, then one trailer block: `Goldens-moved: <ids>` and the `Co-Authored-By:` line. The ids are every case whose expected files the branch adds or changes: `git diff --name-only origin/main...<sha> -- conformance/expected/ | sed -e 's#^conformance/expected/##' -e 's#\.meta\.json$##' -e 's#\.html$##' | sort -u | paste -sd, - | sed 's/,/, /g'`.
  - **The check.** Before merging, the coordinator squashes locally on a throwaway branch from `origin/main` (`git merge --squash <sha>`, then `git commit -F` a file holding `$BODY`) and runs `node scripts/ratchet.mjs --base origin/main` there: exit 0, every verdict kept and every moved golden named.
- **The rulings reach the ledger.** The pull request that merges this plan to `main` ("The plan reaches `main` first") also appends rulings C1-C23 to the ledger's "Decisions & deviations", in public-ready wording, each with its what, its why and what it costs if wrong; C18's entry records the finding against Tasks 1 and 6. A later ruling (C24 on) goes there before any file moves.
- **Departures found while executing.** This repo has no D-numbers. A departure found during execution goes to the coordinator as a question and becomes a `C<n>` ruling in the ledger (the next is C24) before any file moves.

### Task 1: Scaffold and first CI

**Model routing:** `sonnet`, effort `high` — a new package with no code to read first, but every byte is a contract later tasks build on: exact pins resolved under a date cutoff, a lockfile whose hash is given below, three tsconfig projects (one of them the first purity wall), a test setup that refuses the network, the public types of `./render`, and a workflow whose check names branch protection would match. Every number below was measured on the shared scratch tree at the seed commit; the mutations were measured each in its own throwaway copy.

**Architecture rows:** section F, T1 (files, `package.test.ts`, `no-network.test.ts`, CI, the `npm view` record, M1.1-M1.3); section B (layout, `package.json`, the three tsconfigs, `vitest.config.ts`); section C (the types); rulings C2 (API shape), C3 (defaults), C4 (CI on PRs and `main`, no repository settings touched), C6 (every pin at least 14 days old), C18 (the purity project never loads `lib.dom`). Global constraints 1, 2, 9, 10, 11 and 12.

**Files:**
- Create: `package.json` — 56 lines: name, `private`, MIT, ESM, `sideEffects:false`, `engines`, `repository`, the three-key `exports`, `files`, four scripts, four dependencies and five devDependencies, all exact.
- Create: `package-lock.json` — generated by Step 1's `npm install` (lockfileVersion 3, 112 package entries); never hand-edited.
- Create: `.npmrc` — 2 lines: `save-exact=true`, `engine-strict=true`.
- Create: `tsconfig.json` — 20 lines: the shared strict base, typecheck of `src`, `test` and `vitest.config.ts`, `noEmit`.
- Create: `tsconfig.build.json` — 11 lines: emits `dist/` from `src/` with declarations.
- Create: `tsconfig.render.json` — 13 lines: the purity typecheck of `src/render` (lib ES2022, `types: []`, and `paths` mapping highlight.js to the two declarations below, decision 8).
- Create: `src/types/purity/highlight-core.d.ts` (26 lines) and `src/types/purity/highlight-language.d.ts` (5 lines) — the slice of highlight.js's API that Task 6's `highlight.ts` uses, with no DOM library (ruling C18).
- Create: `vitest.config.ts` — 12 lines: node environment, `test/**/*.test.ts`, the no-network setup file, 60 s timeout.
- Create: `test/setup/no-network.ts` — 24 lines: `fetch` and `net.Socket.prototype.connect` throw.
- Create: `src/render/types.ts` — 73 lines: every public type of section C, plus `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` and `DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES`.

- Test: `test/package.test.ts` (108 lines, 10 cases), `test/no-network.test.ts` (37 lines, 6 cases), `test/api.test.ts` (75 lines, 7 cases), `test/ci-workflow.test.ts` (85 lines, 8 cases), `test/render-tsconfig.test.ts` (126 lines, 3 cases).

- Produces, in `src/render/types.ts` (imports nothing):

  - `export interface RenderResult { html: string; outcome: RenderOutcome; bytes: number; meta: RenderMeta }`

- Produces, for every later task:

  - `npm run typecheck` = `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.render.json`; `npm run build` = `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`; `npm run check` runs typecheck, test and build.
  - Installed and pinned: `markdown-it@15.0.2`, `markdown-it-footnote@4.0.0`, `js-yaml@4.3.2`, `highlight.js@11.12.0`; dev `typescript@6.0.3`, `vitest@4.1.11`, `@types/node@22.20.4`, `@types/js-yaml@4.0.9`, `esbuild@0.28.2`. Each typechecks under `tsconfig.render.json` by explicit import (measured: `import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it'`, `hljs from 'highlight.js/lib/core'`, a `highlight.js/lib/languages/python` registration and `load(s, { schema: CORE_SCHEMA, json: true })` from `js-yaml` all compile clean). `markdown-it-footnote` has no types; Task 8 adds `src/types/markdown-it-footnote.d.ts`, which `tsconfig.render.json`'s `include` already covers.
  - A later task that changes a dependency edits `package.json` and re-runs Step 1's install command with the same `--before` cutoff (or a later one at least 14 days back), then re-runs `test/package.test.ts`; if Task 3's gate D1 swaps to `markdown-it@14.3.2`, its types are `@types/markdown-it@14.2.0` (published 2026-08-17).
  - `test/ci-workflow.test.ts` pins the step list; Task 12 appends its ratchet and consumer-smoke steps to that list and to `ci.yml` together. It already asserts that `ci.yml` never contains `UPDATE_EXPECTED` or a bare `npx vitest`.

**Decisions this task makes:**
1. **Pins, all measured with `npm view <pkg> time --json` on 2026-10-12 and resolved under a date cutoff.** Step 1 installs with `--before=2026-09-28T00:00:00Z` (14 days before planning), so npm refuses any exact pin younger than that and resolves every transitive range to a version published before it (ruling C6 covers the direct pins; the cutoff extends it to the whole tree). The cutoff also makes the lock reproducible: two independent resolutions (a full install and a `--package-lock-only` run in an empty directory) produced the same file, sha256 given in Step 1. Choices against section B's placeholders: `typescript@6.0.3`, the version ccrc's PWA lock holds (7.0.2 is the newer line and was not chosen); `vitest@4.1.11`, the newest 4.1.x (5.x exists and was not chosen); `@types/node@22.20.4`, the newest 22.x old enough (22.20.5 was published 2026-10-01); `esbuild@0.28.2` (Task 12's bundle); `@types/js-yaml@4.0.9`.
2. **`js-yaml@4.3.2`, not "4.1.x".** Section B wrote "4.1.x"; the 4.x line is now the `v4-legacy` dist-tag with 4.3.2 its newest release (2026-08-26), and `latest` is 5.4.3. 5.x changed the API (CORE is the default schema, schemas compose with `withTags`, it ships its own types), while Task 9 is written against 4.x's `load(content, { schema: CORE_SCHEMA, json: true })`, which 4.3.2 keeps. 4.3.x also adds two loader defaults, `maxDepth: 100` and `maxTotalMergeKeys: 10000`, that throw beyond them; Task 9 should know that a YAML block nested deeper than 100 renders nothing here, where PyYAML would render it.
3. **Three test files beyond section F's two, one per guard this task ships.** `api.test.ts` pins rulings C2 and C3 (the runtime exports, the two defaults, and the signatures as type-level assertions that `npm run typecheck` checks). `ci-workflow.test.ts` reads `ci.yml` as data with `js-yaml` and pins the read-only token, the triggers, the matrix and the steps. `render-tsconfig.test.ts` proves the purity wall has teeth: a probe of thirteen host globals plus `globalThis.localStorage` must fail under `tsconfig.render.json` line by line, and a probe of JS intrinsics must pass. Global constraint 8 (every guard ships with a case that goes red when it is removed) is the reason.
4. **The no-network setup patches `net.Socket.prototype.connect`, not only `net.connect`.** Every TCP client in Node (`net`, `tls`, the `http`/`https` agents, undici's `fetch` and `WebSocket`) reaches a socket through it, so one patch closes them all; `fetch` is also replaced outright, so its refusal is synchronous and names `fetch`. The cases call real APIs at `127.0.0.1:9`; with a stub removed the call goes no further than loopback (the discard port, which refuses), and `fetch` refuses port 9 itself as a blocked port.
5. **The constants live in `types.ts`.** `render.ts` (Task 3) and `scan.ts` (Task 10) import them from there, so nothing imports the public entry from inside `src/render` and there is no cycle.
6. **`tsconfig.render.json` also includes `src/types/**/*.d.ts`**, so Task 8's local module declaration is visible to the purity typecheck without a second edit here.
7. **CI beyond section F's list:** an explicit job name `test (${{ matrix.node }})`, so the check names are `test (22)` and `test (24)` whatever the matrix's other keys become; `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`; and a `concurrency` group that cancels a superseded pull-request run (never a `main` run), because Actions minutes on the private repo are unmeasured (ruling C4). No repository setting, branch protection, ruleset or `delete_branch_on_merge` is touched (C4).
8. **The purity project maps highlight.js to DOM-free declarations from the start (ruling C18).** highlight.js's own declarations begin with `/// <reference lib="dom" />`, so the first `src/render` file that imports `highlight.js/lib/core` (Task 6's `highlight.ts`) would bring every DOM global into `tsconfig.render.json`'s typecheck, and `typeof document` there would compile. `paths` in `tsconfig.render.json` only maps `highlight.js/lib/core` and `highlight.js/lib/languages/*` to `src/types/purity/`, two files declaring the slice of the API `highlight.ts` uses (`newInstance`, `registerLanguage`, `highlight`); `tsconfig.json` still checks every file against highlight.js's real declarations, so a call that drifts from them fails there. Nothing imports highlight.js before Task 6, so no red of Tasks 1-5 moves (measured: every row of Tasks 1-5 is red with the mapping in place). `render-tsconfig.test.ts` pins the mapping (row M15); Task 12's purity test checks the effect, that the purity typecheck loads no `lib.dom` at all.

```ts
// The package manifest, the lockfile's root and the npm settings (docserver L1, Task 1).
// A consumer pins one exact version of this package; the package pins exact versions of its own dependencies,
// so the same corpus input always meets the same parser. The exports map is the whole public surface.
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

const ROOT = new URL('../', import.meta.url);
const readText = (rel: string): string => readFileSync(new URL(rel, ROOT), 'utf8');
const readJson = (rel: string): unknown => JSON.parse(readText(rel));

type Deps = Record<string, string>;
interface Manifest {
  name: string;
  private: boolean;
  type: string;
  license: string;
  sideEffects: boolean;
  engines: { node: string };
  exports: Record<string, unknown>;
  scripts: Record<string, string>;
  dependencies: Deps;
  devDependencies: Deps;
}
interface Lock {
  lockfileVersion: number;
  packages: Record<string, { version?: string; dependencies?: Deps; devDependencies?: Deps }>;
}

const pkg = readJson('package.json') as Manifest;
const lock = readJson('package-lock.json') as Lock;
const EXACT = /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/;

describe('package.json: exact pins', () => {
  it('every dependency and devDependency is an exact x.y.z version', () => {
    const all = { ...pkg.dependencies, ...pkg.devDependencies };
    expect(Object.keys(pkg.dependencies).length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(Object.keys(pkg.devDependencies).length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    const loose = Object.entries(all).filter(([, v]) => !EXACT.test(v));
    expect(loose).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("the lockfile's root records the same exact pins", () => {
    const root = lock.packages[''];
    expect(root?.dependencies).toEqual(pkg.dependencies);
    expect(root?.devDependencies).toEqual(pkg.devDependencies);
  });

  it('the lockfile resolves each direct dependency to its pinned version', () => {
    const all = { ...pkg.dependencies, ...pkg.devDependencies };
    const resolved = Object.fromEntries(
      Object.keys(all).map((name) => [name, lock.packages[`node_modules/${name}`]?.version]),
    );
    expect(resolved).toEqual(all);
  });
});

describe('package.json: exports keys', () => {
  it('exposes exactly ./render, ./conformance and ./package.json', () => {
    expect(Object.keys(pkg.exports).sort()).toEqual(['./conformance', './package.json', './render']);
  });

  it('each code entry names its types first and its ESM build second', () => {
    expect(pkg.exports['./render']).toEqual({
      types: './dist/render/index.d.ts',
      import: './dist/render/index.js',
    });
    expect(pkg.exports['./conformance']).toEqual({
      types: './dist/conformance/index.d.ts',
      import: './dist/conformance/index.js',
    });
    expect(pkg.exports['./package.json']).toBe('./package.json');
  });
});

describe('package.json: identity', () => {
  it('is the private, MIT, ESM package @synapsium-labs/docserver', () => {
    expect(pkg.name).toBe('@synapsium-labs/docserver');
    expect(pkg.private).toBe(true);
    expect(pkg.type).toBe('module');
    expect(pkg.license).toBe('MIT');
    expect(pkg.sideEffects).toBe(false);
  });

  it('engines.node is >=22', () => {
    expect(pkg.engines.node).toBe('>=22');
  });

  it('typecheck runs both the whole-tree and the render-purity projects', () => {
    expect(pkg.scripts['typecheck']).toBe(
      'tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.render.json',
    );
  });
});

describe('.npmrc', () => {
  const lines = readText('.npmrc')
    .split('\n')
    .map((l) => l.trim())
    .filter((l) => l !== '' && !l.startsWith('#'));

  it('has save-exact=true', () => {
    expect(lines).toContain('save-exact=true');
  });

  it('has engine-strict=true', () => {
    expect(lines).toContain('engine-strict=true');

});
```

`test/no-network.test.ts`:

```ts
// No test reaches a network (docserver L1, Task 1; global constraint 10). The setup file
// test/setup/no-network.ts replaces `fetch` and `net.Socket.prototype.connect` before any test file loads,
// so every TCP path (net, tls, http, https, undici's fetch, WebSocket) throws before a socket opens.
// Each case below calls a real API at the discard port on loopback, so a missing stub is a red, never a hang.
import http from 'node:http';
import net from 'node:net';
import tls from 'node:tls';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

const REFUSED = /network access is refused in tests/;
const LOOPBACK = { host: '127.0.0.1', port: 9 } as const;

describe('no network in tests', () => {
  it('fetch() throws synchronously from the setup stub', () => {
    expect(() => fetch(`http://${LOOPBACK.host}:${LOOPBACK.port}/`)).toThrow(REFUSED);
  });

  it('net.connect() throws', () => {
    expect(() => net.connect(LOOPBACK)).toThrow(REFUSED);
  });

  it('net.createConnection() throws', () => {
    expect(() => net.createConnection(LOOPBACK)).toThrow(REFUSED);
  });

  it('a bare net.Socket cannot connect', () => {
    expect(() => new net.Socket().connect(LOOPBACK)).toThrow(REFUSED);
  });

  it('tls.connect() throws', () => {
    expect(() => tls.connect(LOOPBACK)).toThrow(REFUSED);
  });

  it('http.get() throws', () => {
    expect(() => http.get(`http://${LOOPBACK.host}:${LOOPBACK.port}/`)).toThrow(REFUSED);
  });
});
```

`test/render-tsconfig.test.ts`:

```ts
// The first purity wall of `./render` (docserver L1, Task 1; architecture section B): tsconfig.render.json
// typechecks src/render with lib ES2022 and no ambient types, so a host global (network, storage, DOM, Node)
// referenced there is a type error. A probe file is checked under that exact project, extended from a temporary
// directory: host globals must fail, JS intrinsics must pass. Task 12's purity test adds the import-graph scan.
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('../', import.meta.url));
const TSC = path.join(ROOT, 'node_modules', 'typescript', 'bin', 'tsc');
const RENDER_PROJECT = path.join(ROOT, 'tsconfig.render.json');
const TYPE_ROOTS = path.join(ROOT, 'node_modules', '@types');

interface Checked {
  status: number | null;
  out: string;
}

/** Typecheck probe modules under tsconfig.render.json's compiler options, from a temporary directory. */
function checkProbes(files: Readonly<Record<string, string>>): Checked {
  const dir = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), 'docserver-render-probe-'));
  try {
    for (const [name, source] of Object.entries(files)) writeFileSync(path.join(dir, name), source);
    writeFileSync(
      path.join(dir, 'tsconfig.json'),
      // typeRoots points at this repo's @types, so a `types` entry added to the project would resolve here
      // exactly as it does for src/render, and the probe would see what src/render would see.
      JSON.stringify({
        extends: RENDER_PROJECT,
        compilerOptions: { typeRoots: [TYPE_ROOTS] },
        include: Object.keys(files),
      }),
    );
    const r = spawnSync(
      process.execPath,
      [TSC, '--noEmit', '--pretty', 'false', '-p', path.join(dir, 'tsconfig.json')],
      { cwd: dir, encoding: 'utf8' }, // diagnostics then name the probe files relative to `dir`
    );
    return { status: r.status, out: `${r.stdout}${r.stderr}` };
  } finally {
    rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

/** The 1-based lines of `file` that carry at least one type error in `out`. */
function errorLines(out: string, file: string): number[] {
  const re = new RegExp(`^${file.replace('.', '\\.')}\\((\\d+),\\d+\\): error TS\\d+:`, 'gm');
  return [...new Set([...out.matchAll(re)].map((m) => Number(m[1])))].sort((a, b) => a - b);
}

/** Host globals that must not typecheck in src/render: one per line, so each error names its own line. */
const HOST_GLOBALS = [
  'fetch',
  'document',
  'window',
  'self',
  'navigator',
  'localStorage',
  'sessionStorage',
  'process',
  'Buffer',
  'require',
  'TextEncoder',
  'setTimeout',
  'structuredClone',
] as const;

/** JS intrinsics only: every line must typecheck. */
const CLEAN = [
  'export const ok = [',
  '  Math.max(1, 2),',
  '  JSON.stringify({ a: 1 }),',
  '  new Map<string, number>().size,',
  "  'x'.codePointAt(0),",
  '  [1, 2].at(-1),',
  "  Object.hasOwn({}, 'a'),",
  "  /a/u.test('a'),",
  '  globalThis === globalThis,',
  '];',
  '',

describe('tsconfig.render.json', () => {
  let checked: Checked = { status: null, out: '' };

  });

  it('names no ambient types, only lib ES2022, and covers src/render', () => {
    const project = JSON.parse(readFileSync(RENDER_PROJECT, 'utf8')) as {

      include?: unknown;

    expect(project.compilerOptions?.types).toEqual([]);
    expect(project.compilerOptions?.lib).toEqual(['ES2022']);
    // highlight.js's own declarations reference lib.dom; the purity project reads a DOM-free slice instead
    // (ruling C18; Task 12's purity test checks that no lib.dom is loaded).
    expect(project.compilerOptions?.paths).toEqual({
      'highlight.js/lib/core': ['./src/types/purity/highlight-core.d.ts'],
      'highlight.js/lib/languages/*': ['./src/types/purity/highlight-language.d.ts'],
    });
    expect(project.include).toEqual(['src/render/**/*.ts', 'src/types/**/*.d.ts']);
  });

  it('accepts a probe that uses only JS intrinsics', () => {
    expect(checked.out).toMatch(/^leak\.mts\(/m); // the checker ran over the probes
    expect(checked.out).not.toMatch(/error TS5\d\d\d:/); // and read the project without a config error
    expect(errorLines(checked.out, 'clean.mts')).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('rejects every host global, and a host property read through globalThis', () => {
    expect(checked.status).not.toBe(0);
    expect(errorLines(checked.out, 'leak.mts')).toEqual(LEAK_LINES.map((_, i) => i + 1));
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 4: The no-network setup, then see the per-file reds.** Create `test/setup/no-network.ts` with exactly this content:

```ts
// Runs before every test file (vitest.config.ts `setupFiles`). Tests never reach a network (global constraint
// 10): `fetch` is replaced by a function that throws, and so is `net.Socket.prototype.connect`, which every
// TCP client in Node goes through (net.connect, tls.connect, http and https agents, undici's fetch and
// WebSocket). The throw is synchronous and happens before a socket opens. Only `npm ci` in CI touches the
// registry; the tests themselves never do.
import net from 'node:net';

const MESSAGE = 'network access is refused in tests (test/setup/no-network.ts)';

function refuse(what: string): never {
  throw new Error(`${MESSAGE}: ${what}`);
}

Object.defineProperty(globalThis, 'fetch', {
  configurable: true,
  writable: true,
  value: function fetch(): never {
    return refuse('fetch');
  },
});

net.Socket.prototype.connect = function connect(): never {
  return refuse('net.Socket.prototype.connect');
};
```

```ts
// The part of highlight.js's core API that src/render/highlight.ts (Task 6) uses, declared for
// tsconfig.render.json only, from the first task on (ruling C18). highlight.js's own declarations start with
// `/// <reference lib="dom" />`, which would bring every DOM global into the purity typecheck of src/render.
// tsconfig.render.json's `paths` maps `highlight.js/lib/core` here and `highlight.js/lib/languages/*` to
// ./highlight-language.d.ts; tsconfig.json still checks src/render against highlight.js's real declarations,
// so a call that does not match them fails there.
export interface HighlightOptions {
  language: string;
  ignoreIllegals?: boolean;
}

export interface HighlightResult {
  value: string;
}

/** A language definition: a function of the instance it is registered on. */
export type LanguageFn = (hljs: HLJSApi) => object;

export interface HLJSApi {
  newInstance(): HLJSApi;
  registerLanguage(languageName: string, language: LanguageFn): void;
  highlight(code: string, options: HighlightOptions): HighlightResult;
}

declare const hljs: HLJSApi;
export default hljs;
```

```ts
// The public types of `./render` and its two default limits (docserver L1; architecture section C as amended
// by rulings C2 and C3). Imports nothing, so every module of src/render can import it without a cycle.

/** What `render()` did: parsed and rendered, refused by the byte gate, or fell back after an internal error. */
export type RenderOutcome = 'rendered' | 'over-limit' | 'failed';

export interface RenderOptions {
  /** UTF-8 byte cap on the input; above it nothing is parsed. Default DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES. */
  maxBytes?: number;
  /** Emit data-line="a-b" on block elements. Default true. */
  lineAttrs?: boolean;
}

export interface Heading {
  level: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6;
  id: string;
  text: string;
}

/** One front-matter key, in source order. Same shape as the standalone server's meta.front. */
export interface FrontEntry {
  key: string;
  list: boolean;
  vals: string[];
}

export interface RenderMeta {
  /** null-prototype record derived from frontList: list ? vals : vals[0]. null when there is no front-matter mapping. */
  front: Readonly<Record<string, string | readonly string[]>> | null;
  frontList: readonly FrontEntry[] | null;
  /** text of the first level-1 heading in document order, else null */
  title: string | null;
  headings: readonly Heading[];
  /** count of figure.mermaid-figure emitted */
  figures: number;
  /** count of tables emitted */
  tables: number;
  /** distinct diagram keywords of rendered mermaid fences, document order, max 32 */
  mermaidKinds: readonly string[];
}

export interface RenderResult {
  /** '' when over-limit; the escaped fallback block when failed */
  html: string;
  outcome: RenderOutcome;
  /** measured UTF-8 length (when over-limit: the cap + 1 at which counting stopped) */
  bytes: number;
  /** the frozen empty meta unless outcome === 'rendered' */
  meta: RenderMeta;
}

export interface ScanRefsOptions {
  /** UTF-8 byte cap on the input, as for render(). Default DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES. */
  maxBytes?: number;
  /** most distinct image sources returned. Default DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES. */
  maxImages?: number;
}

export interface ScanRefsResult {
  outcome: 'scanned' | 'over-limit';
  /** distinct img src values exactly as render() emits them (post normalizeLink), document order */
  images: string[];
  /** true when more than maxImages distinct images exist */
  imagesTruncated: boolean;
  /** only fences render() turns into figures; UTF-8 bytes of their content */
  mermaid: { fences: number; largestBytes: number; totalBytes: number };
}

/** Default UTF-8 byte cap for render() and scanRefs(): 4 MiB (ruling C3). Hosts pass their own. */
export const DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES = 4_194_304;

/** Default cap on distinct images returned by scanRefs() (ruling C3). Hosts pass their own. */
export const DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES = 512;
```

- [ ] **Step 8: The mutation rows, each measured red in its own copy.** Each row is one exact `old` → `new` replacement (each `old` occurs exactly once in its file at this task's state), the tests that must go red, and the red measured while planning. Every row is applied to its own throwaway copy of the working tree (tracked and untracked files, never ignored ones, with `node_modules` symlinked from the checkout), its tests run from the copy, and the copy is deleted; the checkout is never edited. Rows M6 and M7 call real socket APIs once their stub is gone; they reach only loopback's discard port, and only inside the copy.

(a) Outside the checkout, make a scratch directory: `WORK=$(mktemp -d)`. Save the JSON fence below as `"$WORK/rows.json"`, and save this script as `"$WORK/mutate.mjs"`:

```js
// Measures mutation rows, each in its own throwaway copy of the checkout's working tree.
// usage: node mutate.mjs <checkout> <rows.json> <work-dir>
import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, symlinkSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const [checkout, rowsFile, work] = process.argv.slice(2).map((p) => path.resolve(p));
const rows = JSON.parse(readFileSync(rowsFile, 'utf8'));
let bad = 0;
for (const row of rows) {
  const copy = path.join(work, row.id);
  rmSync(copy, { recursive: true, force: true });
  mkdirSync(copy, { recursive: true });
  // Tracked and untracked, never ignored: the task's files as they stand, without node_modules or dist.
  const list = execFileSync('git', ['-C', checkout, 'ls-files', '-z', '--cached', '--others', '--exclude-standard']);
  execFileSync('tar', ['--null', '-C', checkout, '-T', '-', '-cf', path.join(work, `${row.id}.tar`)], { input: list });
  execFileSync('tar', ['-xf', path.join(work, `${row.id}.tar`), '-C', copy]);
  rmSync(path.join(work, `${row.id}.tar`));
  symlinkSync(path.join(checkout, 'node_modules'), path.join(copy, 'node_modules'));
  const file = path.join(copy, row.file);
  const src = readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
  const hits = src.split(row.old).length - 1;
  if (hits !== 1) {
    console.log(`=== ${row.id} NOT APPLIED: old occurs ${hits} times in ${row.file}`);
    bad += 1;
    rmSync(copy, { recursive: true, force: true });
    continue;
  }
  writeFileSync(file, src.replace(row.old, row.new));
  const cmd = row.tests.startsWith('npm ') ? row.tests : `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run ${row.tests}`;
  const r = spawnSync('bash', ['-c', `${cmd} 2>&1`], { cwd: copy, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 600_000 });
  const lines = `${r.stdout ?? ''}`.split('\n');
  const keep = lines.filter((l) => /^ FAIL | × |Tests  |error TS\d+|AssertionError/.test(l));
  console.log(`=== ${row.id} rc=${r.status} ${r.status === 0 ? 'NOT RED' : 'red'}`);
  // The count line always prints, whatever the number of failing lines before it.
  const count = keep.filter((l) => /Tests  /.test(l));
  console.log([...keep.filter((l) => !/Tests  /.test(l)).slice(0, 20), ...count].join('\n'));
  if (r.status === 0) bad += 1;
  rmSync(copy, { recursive: true, force: true });
}
process.exitCode = bad === 0 ? 0 : 1;
```

### Task 2: Corpus inputs, the generator, references, the normaliser and departures

**Model routing:** `sonnet`, effort `high` — no engine code yet, but this task writes the contract every later task is measured against: 51 corpus inputs whose bytes are exact (control characters, CRLF, a BOM, astral characters at slicing boundaries), a dev-only generator that runs the reference renderer by path, 102 reference files and 102 expected files derived from them, the comparison normaliser, and the bookkeeping tests that keep inputs, references, expected files and departures in step. Every number below was measured on the shared scratch tree at Task 1's commit; the mutations were measured each in its own throwaway copy.

**Architecture rows:** section F, T2 (files, `normaliseForCompare`, the normalise, manifest and expected tests, the twice-run diff, M2.1-M2.5); section D (three tiers, the generator's command and behaviour, deriving `expected/`, the normalisation decision, the departure categories); section E (the corpus, 24 golden and 9 small hostile entries); rulings C1 (PD1-PD4 closed list), C2 (the meta shape the reference meta files carry) and C5 (the reference renderer only as arguments; no path in a tracked file). Global constraints 1, 5, 7, 8, 10 and 12.

**Files:**
- Create: `conformance/corpus/**.md` — 51 inputs (37 golden, 14 small hostile) for the 33 entries of section E; written byte-exact in Step 3 from a JSON line map and a writer for the four computed inputs (both pasted below), checked by sha256.
- Create: `conformance/manifest.json` — 308 lines: one entry per case id, in section E's order.
- Create: `conformance/probes.txt` — 168 lines: the scout's probe names, sorted.
- Create: `conformance/DEPARTURES.json` — 1 line, `[]`. Task 9 adds the PD2-PD4 entries and hand-edits those expected files.
- Create: `scripts/golden/generate.py` — 192 lines: the dev-only reference generator (never run by tests or CI).
- Create (generated by Step 4's command, not pasted): `conformance/reference/<id>.html` and `<id>.meta.json` for every case (102 files) and `conformance/reference/PROVENANCE.json`.
- Create (generated by Step 5's command, not pasted): `conformance/expected/<id>.html` and `<id>.meta.json` (102 files).
- Create: `src/conformance/normalise.ts` — 44 lines: `normaliseForCompare`.
- Test: `test/normalise.test.ts` (104 lines, 11 cases), `test/manifest.test.ts` (136 lines, 12 cases), `test/expected.test.ts` (95 lines, 104 cases: one per derived file plus two).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 1's runner (`./node_modules/.bin/vitest run`, the no-network setup), `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build`; no dependency is added. At dev time only: the reference renderer and its interpreter, given as `"$REFERENCE_PYTHON"` and `"$REFERENCE_RENDERER"` (ruling C5; the coordinator supplies both values; they are never written into a file).
- Produces, in `src/conformance/normalise.ts` (imports nothing; Node-free, so Task 3's `./conformance` entry re-exports it):
  - `export function normaliseForCompare(html: string): string` — every `<div class="codehilite"{ data-line="…"}><pre>…</pre></div>` becomes the same wrapper around the block's text (tags removed, the entities `&lt; &gt; &amp; &quot; &#39; &#x27;` decoded in one pass, then escaped as markdown-it's `escapeHtml` does: `& < > "`). Everything else is returned unchanged; idempotent. Task 3's `runCorpus` compares `normaliseForCompare(actual.html) === expected.html`.
- Produces, as data for Task 3's `loadCorpus` and every later task:
  - `conformance/manifest.json`: `Array<{ id: string; kind: 'golden' | 'hostile' | 'generated'; pins: string; probes: string[]; options?: Record<string, unknown> }>`. Ids match `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*(?:\/[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*)?$`; a golden or hostile case has `conformance/corpus/<id>.md`; a `generated` case (Task 11) has none and keeps its input spec in `conformance/hostile.json`. No case uses `options` yet.
  - `conformance/expected/<id>.html`: `normaliseForCompare(reference html)`; `conformance/expected/<id>.meta.json`: a `RenderMeta` as JSON, keys in the order `front, frontList, title, headings, figures, tables, mermaidKinds`, formatted exactly as `JSON.stringify(meta, null, 2) + '\n'` (measured: that expression reproduces all 51 reference meta files byte for byte).
  - `conformance/DEPARTURES.json`: `Array<{ case: string; files: Array<'html' | 'meta'>; category: 'PD2' | 'PD3' | 'PD4'; reason: string }>`, at most one entry per case; `[]` until Task 9.
  - The meta rules the references were generated with, which Tasks 4, 9 and 10 must reproduce:
    - `headings`: every `heading_open` in document order, `{ level, id, text }`, `text` = the `text` and `code_inline` children's content joined, then Python-stripped; `title` = the first level-1 heading's `text`, else `null`.
    - `figures` = the count of `<figure class="mermaid-figure"` in the html; `tables` = the count of `<div class="table-wrapper">`.
    - `mermaidKinds`, per fence whose `info.strip().split(' ')[0] === 'mermaid'`, in token order: take the content's lines (split on `\n`), each Python-stripped; skip lines that are empty or start with `%%`; if the next line is `---`, skip to the next `---` line and past it (none: no kind), then skip empty and `%%` lines again; the kind is the match of `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,39}` on the next line (none: no kind). Distinct, document order, at most 32.
    - `frontList` = the reference's `front_matter_list(text)` (a list, or `null`; an all-null or all-mapping YAML mapping gives `[]`), `front` = `null` when `frontList` is `null`, else `{ [key]: list ? vals : vals[0] }` in order.
  - The regeneration command (dev-only, from the repository root): `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 "$REFERENCE_PYTHON" -I scripts/golden/generate.py --renderer "$REFERENCE_RENDERER" --corpus conformance/corpus --out conformance/reference [--only <id> ...]`, then `UPDATE_EXPECTED=1 ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/expected.test.ts`. A commit that changes a file under `conformance/expected/` names those ids in a `Goldens-moved:` trailer (Task 11's ratchet).

**Decisions this task makes:**
1. **Section E's row 16 cannot be one file, so the front-matter probes move.** Front matter is recognised only at line 0, so one input can hold one block. `frontmatter` is one merged block covering the `frontmatter`, `yaml_anchor_list` and `fm_repr` probes (a flow list, a block list, a nested mapping, a YAML anchor and alias, a list with nested items, a duplicate key, an apostrophe, a heading straight after the closing `---`); `frontmatter_list` is row 18's `frontmatter-openers/list-root`. The `frontmatter` probe's `empty:` key (YAML null) is dropped there, so that case stays free of departures; `frontmatter-types` pins null under PD2.
2. **The ten probes section E did not place:** `fm_dashes4`, `fm_dots`, `fm_space_open`, `fm_unclosed`, `fm_not_first`, `fm_hr_eats` and `frontmatter_bad` go to row 18's ids (`dashes4`, `dots`, `space-open`, `unclosed`, `not-first`, `hr-eats`, `bad-yaml`); `hr_not_fm` and `hr_after_para_fm_like` join `frontmatter-openers/not-first`; `html_block_raw` joins `h-script-and-tags`. All 168 probes are now in exactly one entry, which `manifest.test.ts` enforces (stricter than section F's "union", so a probe cannot be counted twice).
3. **How probes are folded into one input.** In a multi-probe case each probe is preceded by a paragraph `Probe: <name>.` and a blank line, so a list, blockquote, table or footnote definition always closes before the next probe and the golden shows where each probe starts. Order is chosen so no probe changes another's behaviour: the unterminated comments (`comment_id`'s tail, `comment_block_unterminated_end`) come last in `comment-anchors`, because a block comment scans forward to the next `-->`; the unclosed `<details>` of the `details` probe comes last in `details/main`; `footnote_multi_ref`'s label is renamed `m` and placed first, so it is note 1 with `fnref1:1`. A separator that is a comment would have been swallowed by those unterminated comments. `nest_list` comes last in `lists-tasks` (ruling C14): markdown-it stops at its nesting limit inside that probe and renders nothing after it, so `ordered_start` and `tasklist_nested`, placed before it, render, and Task 8's task-list mutation goes red through `tasklist_nested`.
4. **Public-ready edits to probe text** (global constraint 1): the `byline` probe's tracker reference reads `Tracker: DOC-12`, and the `autolink` probe's address is `me@example.invalid`.
5. **Additions section E implies but no probe carried:** `line-endings/crlf` starts with a CRLF front-matter block (PD3 on its meta needs one); `mermaid-figures` ends with a fence whose kind (`stateDiagram-v2`) follows a `%%` line and a diagram front-matter block, so Task 10's M10.6 (no skip) has a red; `heading-unicode-case`, `spec-template`, `line-endings/bom` and the 14 hostile inputs are new text.
6. **The corpus bytes travel as a JSON line map.** Trailing spaces, tabs, CR, NUL, form feed, U+0085, U+2028, U+FEFF and combining marks do not survive a pasted Markdown fence; each static input is an array of lines (joined with `\n`), with every invisible or combining character written as a `\uXXXX` escape. Four inputs are computed by the writer (50 stray and 50 unclosed `<details>`, 25 nested alerts, the caps block with astral characters at both cuts, a 20005-character block). The sha256 list in Step 3 is the binding check.
7. **`PROVENANCE.json` is checked, not only written.** `manifest.test.ts` requires its `inputs` to name every golden and hostile input by its current sha256, so an edited input without regenerated references is red. Its other keys hold versions and hashes only; `date` is the UTC day of the run, so a regeneration on another day changes only that line.
8. **The generator's `--only`** regenerates the named ids and refuses (exit 2) when the Python, package or renderer hash recorded in `PROVENANCE.json` differs from the running toolchain; a full run also deletes reference files of ids no longer in the corpus.
9. **`DEPARTURES.json` starts empty** and its test checks both directions from now on: the shape (known case, files from `html`/`meta`, category from the closed list PD2-PD4 of ruling C1, a reason) and that a listed file differs from its derived reference. With the empty list every expected file is the derived reference.
