`test/normalise.test.ts`:

```ts
// normaliseForCompare (docserver L1, Task 2; architecture section D, departure PD1): highlighted code blocks
// compare by wrapper and text, everything else byte for byte. The two block shapes below are the reference
// renderer's (Pygments: no <code>, a leading empty span, &#39;) and this library's (highlight.js: a
// <code class="hljs language-…"> wrapper, &#x27;).
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { normaliseForCompare } from '../src/conformance/normalise.js';

const PYGMENTS =
  '<div class="codehilite" data-line="1-3"><pre><span></span><span class="nb">print</span>' +
  '<span class="p">(</span><span class="s1">&#39;a &lt; b &amp;&amp; &quot;c&quot;&#39;</span>' +
  '<span class="p">)</span>\n</pre></div>\n';
const HLJS =
  '<div class="codehilite" data-line="1-3"><pre><code class="hljs language-python">' +
  '<span class="hljs-built_in">print</span>(<span class="hljs-string">&#x27;a &lt; b &amp;&amp; &quot;c&quot;&#x27;</span>)' +
  '\n</code></pre></div>\n';
const CANONICAL = '<div class="codehilite" data-line="1-3"><pre>print(\'a &lt; b &amp;&amp; &quot;c&quot;\')\n</pre></div>\n';
const MERMAID =
  '<figure class="mermaid-figure" data-line="5-8"><pre class="mermaid">A --&gt; B &#x27;q&#x27; &amp;amp;\n' +
  '</pre><figcaption>Figure 1. <em>x</em></figcaption></figure>\n';
const INDENTED = '<pre data-line="10-11"><code>x &lt; y <span>\n</code></pre>\n';

describe('normaliseForCompare: highlighted blocks', () => {
  it('two codehilite blocks with different spans but equal text normalise equal', () => {
    expect(normaliseForCompare(PYGMENTS)).toBe(CANONICAL);
    expect(normaliseForCompare(HLJS)).toBe(CANONICAL);
  });

  it('different text normalises unequal', () => {
    const other = HLJS.replace('print', 'input');
    expect(normaliseForCompare(other)).not.toBe(normaliseForCompare(PYGMENTS));
    expect(normaliseForCompare(other)).toBe(CANONICAL.replace('print', 'input'));
  });

  it("the wrapper's data-line is preserved, and a wrapper without one is normalised too", () => {
    expect(normaliseForCompare(PYGMENTS.replace('1-3', '7-9'))).toBe(CANONICAL.replace('1-3', '7-9'));
    const bare = HLJS.replace(' data-line="1-3"', '');
    expect(normaliseForCompare(bare)).toBe(CANONICAL.replace(' data-line="1-3"', ''));
  });

  it('decodes entities in one pass, so an escaped entity stays text', () => {
    const block = '<div class="codehilite"><pre><span></span>&amp;lt;b&amp;gt; &amp;amp;\n</pre></div>\n';
    expect(normaliseForCompare(block)).toBe(block.replace('<span></span>', ''));
  });

  it('an empty fence keeps its single newline', () => {
    expect(normaliseForCompare('<div class="codehilite" data-line="1-2"><pre><span></span>\n</pre></div>\n')).toBe(
      '<div class="codehilite" data-line="1-2"><pre>\n</pre></div>\n',
    );
  });
});

describe('normaliseForCompare: everything else is untouched', () => {
  it('mermaid pre untouched', () => {
    expect(normaliseForCompare(MERMAID)).toBe(MERMAID);
    expect(normaliseForCompare(MERMAID + PYGMENTS)).toBe(MERMAID + CANONICAL);
  });

  it('indented pre code untouched', () => {
    expect(normaliseForCompare(INDENTED)).toBe(INDENTED);
    expect(normaliseForCompare(PYGMENTS + INDENTED)).toBe(CANONICAL + INDENTED);
  });

  it('HTML with no codehilite block is returned identical', () => {
    const html = '<h1 id="t" data-line="1-1">T &amp; &#39;q&#39;</h1>\n<p data-line="3-3"><code>&lt;b&gt;</code></p>\n';
    expect(normaliseForCompare(html)).toBe(html);
  });

  it('is idempotent', () => {
    const doc = `${MERMAID}${PYGMENTS}${INDENTED}${HLJS}`;
    const once = normaliseForCompare(doc);
    expect(normaliseForCompare(once)).toBe(once);
  });
});

describe('normaliseForCompare: on every reference', () => {
  const REFERENCE = fileURLToPath(new URL('../conformance/reference/', import.meta.url));
  const BLOCK = /<div class="codehilite"(?: data-line="[^"]*")?><pre>[\s\S]*?<\/pre><\/div>/g;
  const referenceFiles = (): string[] =>
    readdirSync(REFERENCE, { recursive: true, encoding: 'utf8' })
      .filter((f) => f.endsWith('.html'))
      .sort();

  it('finds the references', () => {
    expect(referenceFiles().length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  it('changes nothing outside highlighted blocks, leaves no tag inside one, and is idempotent', () => {
    const changed: string[] = [];
    for (const f of referenceFiles()) {
      const ref = readFileSync(path.join(REFERENCE, f), 'utf8');
      const out = normaliseForCompare(ref);
      if (ref.replace(BLOCK, '') !== out.replace(BLOCK, '')) changed.push(`${f}: outside a block`);
      for (const block of out.match(BLOCK) ?? []) {
        const inner = block.slice(block.indexOf('<pre>') + 5, -'</pre></div>'.length);
        if (inner.includes('<')) changed.push(`${f}: a tag left inside a block`);
      }
      if (normaliseForCompare(out) !== out) changed.push(`${f}: not idempotent`);
    }
    expect(changed).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```

`test/manifest.test.ts`:

```ts
// The corpus bookkeeping (docserver L1, Task 2; architecture sections D and E). manifest.json names every case
// once; a golden or hostile case has one input under corpus/, a reference under reference/ and an expected
// pair under expected/; a generated case (Task 11) has no input file. Every probe of the original scout run
// is folded into exactly one case (probes.txt is the committed list of their names). PROVENANCE.json ties
// each reference to the exact bytes of its input, so an edited input without regenerated references is red.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('../conformance/', import.meta.url));
const at = (rel: string): string => path.join(ROOT, rel);
const readText = (rel: string): string => readFileSync(at(rel), 'utf8');
const sha256 = (rel: string): string => createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(at(rel))).digest('hex');

/** Every file under a conformance/ subdirectory, as sorted paths relative to it ('/' separators). */
function filesUnder(dir: string): string[] {
  if (!existsSync(at(dir))) return [];
  return readdirSync(at(dir), { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true })
    .filter((e) => e.isFile())
    .map((e) => path.relative(at(dir), path.join(e.parentPath, e.name)).split(path.sep).join('/'))
    .sort();
}

type Kind = 'golden' | 'hostile' | 'generated';
interface Case {
  id: string;
  kind: Kind;
  pins: string;
  probes: string[];
  options?: Record<string, unknown>;
}

const manifest = JSON.parse(readText('manifest.json')) as Case[];
const withInput = manifest.filter((c) => c.kind !== 'generated');
const ID = /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*(?:\/[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*)?$/;
const PROBE = /^[a-z0-9]+(?:_[a-z0-9]+)*$/;
const KEYS = new Set(['id', 'kind', 'pins', 'probes', 'options']);
const KINDS = new Set<string>(['golden', 'hostile', 'generated']);

describe('manifest.json', () => {
  it('is an array of entries with known keys, a known kind and a probes array', () => {
    expect(Array.isArray(manifest)).toBe(true);
    const bad = manifest.filter(
      (c) =>
        Object.keys(c).some((k) => !KEYS.has(k)) ||
        !KINDS.has(c.kind) ||
        !Array.isArray(c.probes) ||
        (c.options !== undefined && (typeof c.options !== 'object' || c.options === null || Array.isArray(c.options))),
    );
    expect(bad.map((c) => c.id)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('ids are unique and well-formed', () => {
    const ids = manifest.map((c) => c.id);
    expect(ids.filter((id, i) => ids.indexOf(id) !== i)).toEqual([]);
    expect(ids.filter((id) => !ID.test(id))).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('pins is non-empty', () => {
    expect(manifest.filter((c) => typeof c.pins !== 'string' || c.pins.trim() === '').map((c) => c.id)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('every corpus file has an entry and every golden or hostile entry has a corpus file', () => {
    expect(filesUnder('corpus')).toEqual(withInput.map((c) => `${c.id}.md`).sort());
  });

  it('a generated case has no corpus file', () => {
    const generated = manifest.filter((c) => c.kind === 'generated');
    expect(generated.filter((c) => existsSync(at(`corpus/${c.id}.md`))).map((c) => c.id)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('probes', () => {
  const listed = readText('probes.txt').split('\n');

  it('probes.txt is sorted, unique, one name per line, newline-terminated', () => {
    expect(listed.at(-1)).toBe('');
    const names = listed.slice(0, -1);
    expect(names.filter((n) => !PROBE.test(n))).toEqual([]);
    expect(names).toEqual([...new Set(names)].sort());
  });

  it('probe union: every probe is folded into exactly one case', () => {
    const folded = manifest.flatMap((c) => c.probes);
    expect(folded.filter((p, i) => folded.indexOf(p) !== i)).toEqual([]);
    expect([...folded].sort()).toEqual(listed.slice(0, -1));
  });
});

describe('reference/ and expected/', () => {
  const pairs = (ids: string[]): string[] => ids.flatMap((id) => [`${id}.html`, `${id}.meta.json`]).sort();
  const ids = withInput.map((c) => c.id);

  it('every golden and hostile case has reference html and meta, and nothing else is there', () => {
    expect(filesUnder('reference')).toEqual([...pairs(ids), 'PROVENANCE.json'].sort());
  });

  it('every golden and hostile case has expected html and meta, and nothing else is there', () => {
    expect(filesUnder('expected')).toEqual(pairs(ids));
  });

  it('no reference renders the failure fallback', () => {
    expect(ids.filter((id) => readText(`reference/${id}.html`).includes('could not be rendered'))).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('reference/PROVENANCE.json', () => {
  interface Provenance {
    python: string;
    packages: Record<string, string>;
    renderer: string;
    inputs: Record<string, string>;
    date: string;
  }
  const prov = (): Provenance => JSON.parse(readText('reference/PROVENANCE.json')) as Provenance;
  const VERSION = /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/;
  const SHA = /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/;

  it('names every input by its current sha256', () => {
    const expected = Object.fromEntries(withInput.map((c) => [c.id, sha256(`corpus/${c.id}.md`)]));
    expect(prov().inputs).toEqual(expected);
  });

  it('records versions and hashes only', () => {
    const p = prov();
    expect(Object.keys(p)).toEqual(['python', 'packages', 'renderer', 'inputs', 'date']);
    expect(p.python).toMatch(VERSION);
    expect(Object.keys(p.packages)).toEqual(['markdown-it-py', 'mdit-py-plugins', 'Pygments', 'PyYAML']);
    expect(Object.values(p.packages).filter((v) => !VERSION.test(v))).toEqual([]);
    expect(p.renderer).toMatch(SHA);
    expect(Object.values(p.inputs).filter((v) => !SHA.test(v))).toEqual([]);
    expect(p.date).toMatch(/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/);
  });
});

`test/expected.test.ts`:

```ts
// The contract files (docserver L1, Task 2; architecture section D). For every golden and hostile case,
// expected/<id>.html is normaliseForCompare(reference/<id>.html) and expected/<id>.meta.json is
// reference/<id>.meta.json, byte for byte, unless DEPARTURES.json lists that file: a listed file must differ
// (no stale entry) and an unlisted one must not (no silent edit). Departures are PD2-PD4 only (ruling C1).
//
// Regenerate the unlisted files with `UPDATE_EXPECTED=1 ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/expected.test.ts`;
// listed files are edited by hand. CI never sets UPDATE_EXPECTED (test/ci-workflow.test.ts).
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { normaliseForCompare } from '../src/conformance/normalise.js';

const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('../conformance/', import.meta.url));
const at = (rel: string): string => path.join(ROOT, rel);
const readText = (rel: string): string => readFileSync(at(rel), 'utf8');

type File = 'html' | 'meta';
const FILES: readonly File[] = ['html', 'meta'];
const CATEGORIES = new Set(['PD2', 'PD3', 'PD4']);
interface Case {
  id: string;
  kind: 'golden' | 'hostile' | 'generated';
}
interface Departure {
  case: string;
  files: File[];
  category: string;
  reason: string;
}

const manifest = JSON.parse(readText('manifest.json')) as Case[];
const departures = JSON.parse(readText('DEPARTURES.json')) as Departure[];
const ids = manifest.filter((c) => c.kind !== 'generated').map((c) => c.id);
const listed = new Set(departures.flatMap((d) => d.files.map((f) => `${d.case} ${f}`)));
const name = (id: string, file: File): string => (file === 'html' ? `${id}.html` : `${id}.meta.json`);

/** What expected/ holds for a file no departure lists: derived from the reference. */
function derived(id: string, file: File): string {
  const ref = readText(`reference/${name(id, file)}`);
  return file === 'html' ? normaliseForCompare(ref) : ref;
}

if (process.env['UPDATE_EXPECTED'] === '1') {
  for (const id of ids) {
    for (const file of FILES) {
      if (listed.has(`${id} ${file}`)) continue;
      const target = at(`expected/${name(id, file)}`);
      mkdirSync(path.dirname(target), { recursive: true });
      writeFileSync(target, derived(id, file), 'utf8');
    }
  }
}

describe('DEPARTURES.json', () => {
  it('is a list of {case, files, category, reason}, one entry per known case', () => {
    expect(Array.isArray(departures)).toBe(true);
    const bad = departures.filter(
      (d) =>
        Object.keys(d).sort().join() !== 'case,category,files,reason' ||
        !ids.includes(d.case) ||
        !Array.isArray(d.files) ||
        d.files.length === 0 ||
        new Set(d.files).size !== d.files.length ||
        d.files.some((f) => !FILES.includes(f)) ||
        !CATEGORIES.has(d.category) ||
        typeof d.reason !== 'string' ||
        d.reason.trim() === '',
    );
    expect(bad).toEqual([]);
    const cases = departures.map((d) => d.case);
    expect(cases.filter((c, i) => cases.indexOf(c) !== i)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('expected/: unlisted equals reference', () => {
  for (const id of ids) {
    for (const file of FILES) {
      if (listed.has(`${id} ${file}`)) continue;
      it(`${id} ${file}`, () => {
        expect(readText(`expected/${name(id, file)}`)).toBe(derived(id, file));
      });
    }
  }
});

describe('expected/: listed differs', () => {
  it('every file DEPARTURES.json lists differs from its derived reference', () => {
    const stale = [...listed].filter((entry) => {
      const [id = '', file = 'html'] = entry.split(' ') as [string, File];
      return readText(`expected/${name(id, file)}`) === derived(id, file);
    });
    expect(stale).toEqual([]);
  });
});

- [ ] **Step 2: Implement the normaliser.** Create `src/conformance/normalise.ts` with exactly this content:

```ts
// Comparison normalisation for the conformance corpus (docserver L1; architecture section D, departure PD1).
// The reference renderer highlights fences with Pygments and this library with highlight.js; the two tokenise
// differently, so their span markup can never be byte-equal. What a reader sees, and what the reading layout
// reads (the text of `.codehilite > pre`), is the wrapper and the text, and those stay byte-exact: inside each
// highlighted block the markup is reduced to its text, escaped the way markdown-it escapes text. Nothing
// outside such a block is touched: not `pre.mermaid`, not indented `<pre><code>`, not any other element.

/** One highlighted fence as both renderers emit it: the wrapper (with or without data-line), then one <pre>.
 * Inside it every literal `<` is escaped, so the first `</pre></div>` is the block's own end. */
const CODE_BLOCK = /(<div class="codehilite"(?: data-line="[^"]*")?><pre>)([\s\S]*?)(<\/pre><\/div>)/g;

/** Any tag inside a block: Pygments' and highlight.js' spans, highlight.js' <code> wrapper. */
const TAG = /<[^>]*>/g;

/** The entities either highlighter writes, decoded in ONE pass so `&amp;lt;` stays the text `&lt;`. */
const ENTITY = /&(?:lt|gt|amp|quot|#39|#x27);/g;
const DECODED: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  '&lt;': '<',
  '&gt;': '>',
  '&amp;': '&',
  '&quot;': '"',
  '&#39;': "'",
  '&#x27;': "'",
};

/** markdown-it's escapeHtml: & < > " (an apostrophe stays as it is). */
const SPECIAL = /[&<>"]/g;
const ESCAPED: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = { '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;' };

/** The canonical text of one block's inner HTML: tags removed, entities decoded once, re-escaped. */
function canonicalText(inner: string): string {
  const text = inner.replace(TAG, '').replace(ENTITY, (e) => DECODED[e] ?? e);
  return text.replace(SPECIAL, (c) => ESCAPED[c] ?? c);
}

/**
 * Reduce every highlighted code block to `<div class="codehilite"{ data-line}><pre>{escaped text}</pre></div>`
 * and return everything else unchanged. Idempotent. The corpus compares `normaliseForCompare(actual.html)`
 * with `conformance/expected/<id>.html`, which is `normaliseForCompare(reference.html)` unless a departure
 * is listed.
 */
export function normaliseForCompare(html: string): string {
  return html.replace(CODE_BLOCK, (_block, open: string, inner: string, close: string) => open + canonicalText(inner) + close);
}
```

  "spec-template.md": [
    "---",
    "status: Draft",
    "owner: Docs team",
    "---",
    "",
    "# Shared renderer for team notes",
    "",
    "**Spec** · 2026-01-15 · Status: Draft",
    "",
    "## In short",
    "",
    "- **What:** one renderer for every notes page.",
    "- **Why:** two renderers drift apart.",
    "- **Cost:** a corpus of examples kept in step.",
    "",
    "## 1. Context",
    "",
    "Each page is written in Markdown. Two programs render it today, and their output differs in small ways.",
    "",
    "<!-- id:R1 -->",
    "`RULE-ONE` — **One renderer.** Every page renders through the same library.",
    "",
    "## 2. Design",
    "",
    "The flow below shows a page from source to screen.",
    "",
    "```mermaid",
    "flowchart LR",
    "  A[Source] --> B[Renderer]",
    "  B --> C[Page]",
    "```",
    "*Figure 1. A page from source to screen.*",
    "",
    "### 2.1 Options",
    "",
    "| Option | Choice | Status |",
    "|---|---|---|",
    "| One library | Shared package | Agreed |",
    "| Two renderers | Keep both | Rejected |",
    "",
    "> [!WARNING]",
    "> A change to the renderer moves the examples.",
    "",
    "```promise-delta",
    "+ D1: one renderer for every page",
    "```",
    "",
    "## 3. Where things stand",
    "",
    "<details>",
    "<summary>History</summary>",
    "",
    "Drafted, reviewed, revised.",
    "",
    "</details>",
    "",
    "- [x] **Agreed:** one renderer.",
    "- [ ] **Waiting on you:** the review.",
    "- [ ] **Later:** a second theme.",
    ""
  ],

`$WORK/write-corpus.mjs` (writes the 47 static inputs and computes the other four):

````js
// Writes conformance/corpus/** byte-exact: the static files from corpus.json, then the four computed ones.
// usage: node write-corpus.mjs <corpus.json> <repo-root>
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const [corpusJson, root] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!corpusJson || !root) throw new Error('usage: node write-corpus.mjs <corpus.json> <repo-root>');
const write = (rel, text) => {
  const p = path.join(root, 'conformance', 'corpus', rel);
  mkdirSync(path.dirname(p), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(p, text, 'utf8');
};
const files = JSON.parse(readFileSync(corpusJson, 'utf8'));
for (const [rel, lines] of Object.entries(files)) write(rel, lines.join('\n'));

const times = (n, f) => Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => f(i));
const pad = (n, w) => String(n).padStart(w, '0');

write(
  'h-details-hostile.md',
  [
    ...times(50, () => '</details>'),
    '',
    '<details open onclick=x>',
    '',
    '<details class="x">',
    '',
    '<details>',
    '<summary><img src=x onerror=1></summary>',
    '',
    'body',
    '',
    '</details>',
    '',
    '<details>',
    '<summary>line\u2028separator</summary>',
    '',
    '</details>',
    '',
    ...times(50, () => '<details>'),
    '',
  ].join('\n'),
);

write(
  'h-alert-caption-spoof.md',
  [
    '> [!NOTE"><script>alert(1)</script>]',
    '> spoofed marker',
    '',
    '> [!note]',
    '> lower case',
    '',
    ...times(25, (i) => `${'> '.repeat(i + 1)}[!NOTE] level ${i + 1}`),
    '',
    '```mermaid',
    'flowchart LR',
    '  A --> B',
    '```',
    '*Figure 1. <script>alert(1)</script>*',
    '',
    '```js',
    'let a = 1;',
    '```',
    '*Figure 2. after a code fence*',
    '',
  ].join('\n'),
);

// 501 code points whose 500th is astral; 301 code points whose 300th is astral.
const long = `${'a'.repeat(499)}\u{1F600}b`;
const item301 = `${'b'.repeat(299)}\u{1F600}c`;
write(
  'h-frontmatter-hostile/caps.md',
  [
    '---',
    `long: ${long}`,
    `list51: [${times(51, (i) => `v${pad(i + 1, 2)}`).join(', ')}]`,
    'list301:',
    `  - ${item301}`,
    ...times(300, (i) => `  - w${pad(i + 1, 3)}`),
    'nested: [x, [y], {z: 1}, w]',
    ...times(37, (i) => `k${pad(i + 5, 2)}: value ${i + 5}`),
    '---',
    '',
    'Body.',
    '',
  ].join('\n'),
);

write('h-frontmatter-hostile/oversize.md', ['---', `big: ${'x'.repeat(20000)}`, '---', '', 'Body.', ''].join('\n'));
````

- [ ] **Step 4: The generator and the references.** Create `scripts/golden/generate.py` with exactly this content:

```python
"""Write conformance/reference/ from a reference renderer (dev-only; never run by tests or CI).

Every path is an argument and none has a default, so no tracked file names a machine:

  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 "$REFERENCE_PYTHON" -I scripts/golden/generate.py \\
    --renderer "$REFERENCE_RENDERER" --corpus conformance/corpus --out conformance/reference [--only <id> ...]

REFERENCE_PYTHON is an interpreter with the reference renderer's packages; REFERENCE_RENDERER is the
renderer module (a file defining render_md, front_matter_list and _cm). The module is copied into a
temporary directory and imported from there, so nothing beside the original is read or written.

For each corpus/<id>.md (sorted) it writes reference/<id>.html (byte-exact) and reference/<id>.meta.json,
then reference/PROVENANCE.json: the Python and package versions, the renderer's sha256, every input's
sha256 and the UTC date. No path and no host name is recorded. Exit 0 on success, 1 when a reference
renders the failure fallback, 2 on a usage error or a renderer that lacks a required name.
"""

import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import importlib.util
import json
import platform
import re
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

PACKAGES = ("markdown-it-py", "mdit-py-plugins", "Pygments", "PyYAML")
REQUIRED = ("render_md", "front_matter_list", "_cm")
FAILED_MARK = "could not be rendered"
KIND = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,39}")
MAX_KINDS = 32


def die(code: int, message: str) -> None:
    print(f"generate.py: {message}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(code)


def sha256(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def load_renderer(path: Path, tmp: Path):
    copy = tmp / "reference_renderer.py"
    shutil.copyfile(path, copy)
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("reference_renderer", copy)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        die(2, "the renderer cannot be loaded as a module")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    missing = [name for name in REQUIRED if not hasattr(module, name)]
    if missing:
        die(2, "the renderer lacks " + ", ".join(missing))
    return module


def mermaid_kind(content: str):
    """The diagram keyword of one Mermaid source: skip blank and %% lines, then a --- ... --- block,
    then blank and %% lines again; the keyword is the leading [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,39} of the next line."""
    lines = [line.strip() for line in content.split("\n")]
    i = 0

    def skip(i: int) -> int:
        while i < len(lines) and (lines[i] == "" or lines[i].startswith("%%")):
            i += 1
        return i

    i = skip(i)
    if i < len(lines) and lines[i] == "---":
        i += 1
        while i < len(lines) and lines[i] != "---":
            i += 1
        if i >= len(lines):
            return None
        i = skip(i + 1)
    if i >= len(lines):
        return None
    m = KIND.match(lines[i])
    return m.group(0) if m else None


def build_meta(module, text: str, html: str) -> dict:
    tokens = module._cm.parse(text)
    headings, kinds = [], []
    for i, tok in enumerate(tokens):
        if tok.type == "heading_open":
            inline = tokens[i + 1]
            title = "".join(c.content for c in (inline.children or []) if c.type in ("text", "code_inline"))
            hid = tok.attrGet("id")
            if not isinstance(hid, str):
                die(1, "a heading has no id attribute")
            headings.append({"level": int(tok.tag[1]), "id": hid, "text": title.strip()})
        elif tok.type == "fence" and (tok.info or "").strip().split(" ")[0] == "mermaid":
            kind = mermaid_kind(tok.content)
            if kind is not None and kind not in kinds and len(kinds) < MAX_KINDS:
                kinds.append(kind)
    front_list = module.front_matter_list(text)
    front = None
    if front_list is not None:
        front = {}
        for entry in front_list:
            front[entry["key"]] = entry["vals"] if entry["list"] else entry["vals"][0]
    title = next((h["text"] for h in headings if h["level"] == 1), None)
    return {
        "front": front,
        "frontList": front_list,
        "title": title,
        "headings": headings,
        "figures": html.count('<figure class="mermaid-figure"'),
        "tables": html.count('<div class="table-wrapper">'),
        "mermaidKinds": kinds,
    }


def main() -> None:
    sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Write conformance/reference/ from a reference renderer.")
    ap.add_argument("--renderer", required=True, type=Path, help="the reference renderer module (.py)")
    ap.add_argument("--corpus", required=True, type=Path, help="the corpus directory (conformance/corpus)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path, help="the reference directory (conformance/reference)")
    ap.add_argument("--only", nargs="+", default=None, metavar="ID", help="regenerate only these case ids")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if not args.renderer.is_file():
        die(2, "--renderer is not a file")
    if not args.corpus.is_dir():
        die(2, "--corpus is not a directory")
    inputs = {p.relative_to(args.corpus).with_suffix("").as_posix(): p for p in args.corpus.rglob("*.md")}
    ids = sorted(inputs)
    if args.only is not None:
        unknown = sorted(set(args.only) - set(inputs))
        if unknown:
            die(2, "unknown case id: " + ", ".join(unknown))
        ids = sorted(set(args.only))

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        module = load_renderer(args.renderer, Path(tmp))
        rendered = {}
        for cid in ids:
            raw = inputs[cid].read_bytes()
            text = raw.decode("utf-8", "replace")
            html = module.render_md.__wrapped__(text)
            if FAILED_MARK in html:
                die(1, f"{cid}: the reference rendered its failure fallback")
            rendered[cid] = (html, build_meta(module, text, html))

    provenance = {
        "python": platform.python_version(),
        "packages": {name: importlib.metadata.version(name) for name in PACKAGES},
        "renderer": sha256(args.renderer.read_bytes()),
        "inputs": {},
        "date": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).date().isoformat(),
    }
    prov_path = args.out / "PROVENANCE.json"
    if args.only is not None:
        if not prov_path.is_file():
            die(2, "--only needs an existing PROVENANCE.json; run without --only first")
        old = json.loads(prov_path.read_text("utf-8"))
        for key in ("python", "packages", "renderer"):
            if old.get(key) != provenance[key]:
                die(2, f"the reference {key} changed since PROVENANCE.json; regenerate every case")
        provenance["inputs"] = {k: v for k, v in old.get("inputs", {}).items() if k in inputs}

    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for cid, (html, meta) in rendered.items():
        target = args.out / f"{cid}.html"
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        target.write_bytes(html.encode("utf-8"))
        (args.out / f"{cid}.meta.json").write_bytes(
            (json.dumps(meta, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))
        provenance["inputs"][cid] = sha256(inputs[cid].read_bytes())

    if args.only is None:
        keep = {f"{cid}.html" for cid in ids} | {f"{cid}.meta.json" for cid in ids} | {"PROVENANCE.json"}
        for p in sorted(args.out.rglob("*"), reverse=True):
            rel = p.relative_to(args.out).as_posix()
            if p.is_file() and rel not in keep:
                p.unlink()
            elif p.is_dir() and not any(p.iterdir()):
                p.rmdir()

    provenance["inputs"] = dict(sorted(provenance["inputs"].items()))
    prov_path.write_bytes((json.dumps(provenance, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))
    print(f"generate.py: wrote {len(rendered)} reference case(s)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

**Decisions this task makes:**
1. **Gate D1 fired: markdown-it is `14.3.2`, with `@types/markdown-it@14.2.0`.** Rendering all 51 corpus inputs with markdown-it 15.0.2 and with 14.3.2 under the same options differs on exactly one output line: the `img_alt` probe in `links-images`, `![a *b* `c`](x.png)`, where 15 writes `alt="a b c"` and 14 (and the reference, a port of 14) `alt="a b "`. 15's core chain also gains a `strip_references` rule. Both are 15-versus-14 behaviour, so ruling C6 picks 14.3.2 (the `v14-legacy` dist-tag, published 2026-09-12); 14 ships no types, so `@types/markdown-it@14.2.0` (2026-08-17) joins the dev dependencies. Both are older than Task 1's install cutoff, and the lock that cutoff produces is reproducible (two runs, same sha256). Step 4 shows the gate's red under 15, Step 5 the swap. Record this paragraph in the PR body.
2. **`line_attrs` moves from Task 4 into this task.** Every golden except the two empty documents carries `data-line`, so without the rule no corpus case can pass: section F's "core cases pass at the end of T3", and rows M3.1-M3.3 and M3.9, would be impossible. The rule is the reference's `_line_attrs`, exactly its token set, with the `lineAttrs: false` option through the env. Task 4 keeps heading ids, `meta.headings`/`title`, `slug.ts` and its `lineattrs.test.ts`; its rows M4.7 and M4.8 target `src/render/lineAttrs.ts` as it stands here.
3. **`pyLower` lowers the whole string; section C's "one code point at a time" is wrong.** Measured with CPython 3.12.3 (the reference's interpreter): `'ΟΔΟΣ'.lower()` is `'οδος'`, with the final sigma, and the `heading-unicode-case` golden's id is `οδος`; lowering per code point gives `'οδοσ'`. JS `toLowerCase()` applies the same context rule. Over every code point, Python's and Node's single-character mappings differ only on 55 characters assigned after Unicode 15.0 (architecture risk 2). Task 4's row M4.1 therefore reads the other way round: mutating `pyLower` to lower per code point reds `heading-unicode-case` (row L1-T3-M11 here already reds `pytext.test.ts`).
4. **The failure fallback escapes with `pyEscape`, not `escapeHtml`.** Section C wrote `escapeHtml(src)`, but the reference's `render_md` writes `html.escape(text)`, and global constraint 5 puts `pyEscape` wherever the reference called `html.escape`.
5. **`data:image/(gif|png|jpeg|webp);` is allowed on a link as well as on an image.** Section F's oracle allowed it on `img` only, but markdown-it's `validateLink` (unchanged by design) and the reference both render `[g](data:image/gif;base64,AA)` as a link, so the `links-images` golden failed the oracle (measured). The oracle's scheme rule is now exactly validateLink's policy; `oracle.test.ts` "accepts every expected file of the corpus" pins that the oracle and the contract agree (row L1-T3-M22).
6. **Oracle details beyond section F's list:** highlight.js writes a dotted scope as `class="hljs-title function_"` (measured with highlight.js 11.12.0), so a sub-scope token `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*_+$` is accepted only beside an `hljs-` token; `data-line` must be `\d+-\d+` and `ol start` digits; an attribute may appear once; only `open` on `details` may be bare; a closing tag carries nothing; only `br`, `hr`, `img` and `input` may self-close; references are decoded the way an HTML parser decodes an attribute (numeric with or without `;`, and `&colon;`, `&Tab;`, `&NewLine;` among the named ones), and every C0/C1 control, space and no-break space is removed before the scheme check. The class vocabulary already holds what Tasks 5-9 emit (`doc-anchor`, `gh-*`, `table-wrapper`, the task-list and footnote classes, `doc-meta`, `mermaid-figure`, `codehilite`), plus `page-subtitle` for the fallback.
7. **Byte gate and option checks.** An over-limit result's `bytes` is exactly `maxBytes + 1`, whichever character crossed the cap. A `maxBytes` that is not a non-negative safe integer throws `RangeError` before anything is read: `NaN` would otherwise disable the gate (`bytes > NaN` is false), and `Infinity` is spelled `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` by a host that wants no cap.
8. **`src/render/env.ts` is a file section B did not list.** `render.ts` and every rule import the env type from it, so no rule imports `render.ts` and there is no cycle.
9. **`runCorpus` details:** meta is compared as text, byte for byte, exactly as Task 2 derived the expected files; a render that throws or returns no html string is a failed case, not an exception; at most five oracle violations are listed per case, then a count; inputs are read with `Buffer#toString('utf8')`, which keeps a BOM and replaces invalid bytes as the reference's `decode('utf-8', 'replace')` does (`TextDecoder` would drop the BOM). Section F's `timing` and `timeScale` options have nothing to act on before Task 11's verdicts, so they arrive with them.
10. **`verdict.ts` declares the `Verdict` shape only** (section D's fields), so `./conformance`'s type surface exists from this task; Task 11 implements `evaluateVerdict` against it and may refine it.
11. **The pending labels are measured, not copied.** Nine cases pass now: section F's seven, plus `code-indented-breaks` (section F: T4) and `frontmatter-openers/unclosed` (section F: T9), which need nothing beyond `data-line`. Each of the other 42 is labelled with the task whose feature its expected file needs last, which differs from section F's lists for six cases: `headings` T5 (a `<br />` inside a heading), `heading-ids-edge` T8 (inline `sup` and a footnote reference), `comment-anchors` and `h-attr-smuggle` T8 (tables), `h-dom-clobber-names` T5 (comment anchors; section F did not place it), `frontmatter-openers/not-first` T4 (headings only).
12. **The html bound (ruling C20; one of departure PD8's bounds, ruling C19).** An input under `maxBytes` can still expand far past it: a reference definition with a 4000-character destination used 100000 times is 304 KB of input and 200 MB of html (measured). `render()` takes `maxHtmlBytes`, default 16 MiB (four times `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES`, a constant of `render.ts`, so the runtime exports do not change), and renders through `renderBounded`: markdown-it's `renderer.render` loop, rendering an inline token's children one at a time exactly as `renderer.renderInline` does, and counting each piece in UTF-8 bytes before appending it. The first piece that would pass the bound stops the render, so a paragraph of many long links is never built whole. The outcome is then `'output-over-limit'`, a word of its own (never folded into `'rendered'` or into the input's `'over-limit'`), with `EMPTY_META` and the failure block of decision 4. That block is cut to `maxHtmlBytes` too, in `failed` as well, by `fallbackHtml`: at a character, never inside a surrogate pair or an entity, and `''` when even the empty block (96 bytes) does not fit, so no outcome returns more html than the bound. The pieces are the ones `renderer.render` joins, so a finished html is unchanged and no golden moves: `render-shell.test.ts` renders every corpus input at exactly its html's size (unchanged) and one byte under (`'output-over-limit'`). A spy on the text rule shows that the render stops rather than being measured at its end (row M36). Task 11 adds the 304 KB document as the generated case `x-limits/html-expansion`.

// The markdown-it instance behind render() (docserver L1, Task 3; architecture section C, "Engine").
// The options, the nesting limit and the enabled rule chains are pinned as lists, so a rule added, dropped
// or moved is a deliberate edit here. Later tasks extend these lists as they add rules: front_matter and
// safe_block_html in the block chain, safe_inline_html and the footnote rules in the inline chain, and
// footnote_tail, task_lists, anchors, balance_details, alerts, figcaption and table_code in the core chain,
// each before line_attrs.
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { createEngine } from '../src/render/engine.js';
import { createEnv } from '../src/render/env.js';

interface RuleEntry {
  name: string;
  enabled: boolean;
  alt: string[];
}

/** markdown-it's internal rule list (Ruler.__rules__), which its published types do not declare. */
function rules(ruler: unknown): RuleEntry[] {
  return (ruler as { __rules__: RuleEntry[] }).__rules__;
}
const enabled = (ruler: unknown): string[] => rules(ruler).filter((r) => r.enabled).map((r) => r.name);

describe('createEngine: options', () => {
  const md = createEngine();

  it('is the CommonMark preset with raw HTML, linkify, typographer and breaks off, and XHTML output', () => {
    expect(md.options).toEqual({
      html: false,
      xhtmlOut: true,
      breaks: false,
      langPrefix: 'language-',
      linkify: false,
      typographer: false,
      quotes: '“”‘’',
      highlight: null,
      maxNesting: 20,
    });
  });

  it('maxNesting is the preset 20', () => {
    expect((md.options as { maxNesting?: unknown }).maxNesting).toBe(20);
  });

  it("validateLink and normalizeLink are markdown-it's own", () => {
    const stock = new MarkdownIt('commonmark');
    expect(md.validateLink).toBe(stock.validateLink);
    expect(md.normalizeLink).toBe(stock.normalizeLink);
    expect(md.normalizeLinkText).toBe(stock.normalizeLinkText);
  });

  it('each call returns a separate instance', () => {
    expect(createEngine()).not.toBe(md);
  });
});

describe('createEngine: rule chains', () => {
  const md = createEngine();

  it('core: the parse stages, then line_attrs last', () => {
    expect(enabled(md.core.ruler)).toEqual(['normalize', 'block', 'inline', 'text_join', 'line_attrs']);
  });

  it('block: the CommonMark rules plus table, in order', () => {
    expect(enabled(md.block.ruler)).toEqual([
      'table',
      'code',
      'fence',
      'blockquote',
      'hr',
      'list',
      'reference',
      'html_block',
      'heading',
      'lheading',
      'paragraph',
    ]);
  });

  it('inline: the CommonMark rules plus strikethrough, in order', () => {
    expect(enabled(md.inline.ruler)).toEqual([
      'text',
      'newline',
      'escape',
      'backticks',
      'strikethrough',
      'emphasis',
      'link',
      'image',
      'autolink',
      'html_inline',
      'entity',
    ]);
    expect(enabled(md.inline.ruler2)).toEqual(['balance_pairs', 'strikethrough', 'emphasis', 'fragments_join']);
  });
});

describe('createEngine: the raw-HTML wall and links', () => {
  const md = createEngine();

  it('escapes raw HTML in block and inline position', () => {
    const src = '<script>alert(1)</script>\n\nx <b onclick="y">b</b>\n';
    expect(md.render(src, createEnv({ lineAttrs: true }))).toBe(
      '<p data-line="1-1">&lt;script&gt;alert(1)&lt;/script&gt;</p>\n' +
        '<p data-line="3-3">x &lt;b onclick=&quot;y&quot;&gt;b&lt;/b&gt;</p>\n',
    );
  });

  it('leaves javascript:, vbscript:, file: and non-image data: links as text', () => {
    const src = '[a](javascript:x) [b](vbscript:x) [c](file:///x) [d](data:text/html,x) [e](data:image/png;base64,AA)\n';
    expect(md.render(src, createEnv({ lineAttrs: true }))).toBe(
      '<p data-line="1-1">[a](javascript:x) [b](vbscript:x) [c](file:///x) [d](data:text/html,x) ' +
        '<a href="data:image/png;base64,AA">e</a></p>\n',
    );
  });

  it("puts only text, not a code span's content, into an image's alt (markdown-it 14, as the reference)", () => {
    expect(md.render('![a *b* `c`](x.png)\n', createEnv({ lineAttrs: true }))).toBe(
      '<p data-line="1-1"><img src="x.png" alt="a b " /></p>\n',
    );
  });
});

describe('line_attrs', () => {
  const md = createEngine();
  const SRC = '# H\n\n3. a\n4. b\n\n- c\n\n> q\n\n***\n\n    code\n\n| x |\n|---|\n| y |\n\n```\nf\n```\n';

  /** `type data-line` for every token that carries one, in order. */
  const marked = (lineAttrs: boolean): string[] =>
    md
      .parse(SRC, createEnv({ lineAttrs }))
      .filter((t) => t.attrGet('data-line') !== null)
      .map((t) => `${t.type} ${t.attrGet('data-line') ?? ''}`);

  it("marks every block type of the reference's set, 1-based and inclusive, and nothing else", () => {
    expect(marked(true)).toEqual([
      'heading_open 1-1',
      'ordered_list_open 3-5',
      'list_item_open 3-3',
      'paragraph_open 3-3',
      'list_item_open 4-5',
      'paragraph_open 4-4',
      'bullet_list_open 6-7',
      'list_item_open 6-7',
      'paragraph_open 6-6',
      'blockquote_open 8-8',
      'paragraph_open 8-8',
      'hr 10-10',
      'code_block 12-12',
      'table_open 14-16',
      'tr_open 14-14',
      'tr_open 16-16',
    ]);
  });

  it('sets data-line after every other attribute of the token', () => {
    const tokens = md.parse(SRC, createEnv({ lineAttrs: true })).filter((t) => t.attrs !== null);
    expect(tokens.filter((t) => t.attrs?.at(-1)?.[0] !== 'data-line').map((t) => t.type)).toEqual([]);
    expect(md.render('3. a\n', createEnv({ lineAttrs: true }))).toBe(
      '<ol start="3" data-line="1-1">\n<li data-line="1-1">a</li>\n</ol>\n',
    );
  });

  it('marks nothing when the env says lineAttrs: false', () => {
    expect(marked(false)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

`test/render-shell.test.ts`:

```ts
// render() around the engine (docserver L1, Task 3; architecture section C, "Rules for render()"; rulings
// C2, C3 and C20): the byte gate, the html bound, the escaped fallback when the engine throws, the frozen
// empty meta of every result that is not 'rendered', the lineAttrs option, and determinism across calls.
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { createEngine } from '../src/render/engine.js';
import { DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES, render } from '../src/render/index.js';
import { EMPTY_META, FALLBACK_OPEN, fallbackHtml, renderWith } from '../src/render/render.js';

const EMPTY = {
  front: null,
  frontList: null,
  title: null,
  headings: [],
  figures: 0,
  tables: 0,
  mermaidKinds: [],
};

/** An engine whose core chain throws once it has parsed: the fault injection for the fallback. */
function faultyEngine(): ReturnType<typeof createEngine> {
  const md = createEngine();
  md.core.ruler.push('fault', () => {
    throw new Error('injected fault');
  });
  return md;
}

describe('render: the byte gate', () => {
  it('over-limit at maxBytes + 1, with a two-byte character at the boundary', () => {
    const text = 'é'.repeat(5); // 10 UTF-8 bytes
    expect(render(text, { maxBytes: 10 }).outcome).toBe('rendered');
    expect(render(text, { maxBytes: 9 })).toEqual({ html: '', outcome: 'over-limit', bytes: 10, meta: EMPTY });
  });

  it('a four-byte character that crosses the cap reports cap + 1, the point where counting stopped', () => {
    expect(render('a😀', { maxBytes: 5 }).outcome).toBe('rendered');
    expect(render('a😀', { maxBytes: 4 })).toMatchObject({ html: '', outcome: 'over-limit', bytes: 5 });
    expect(render('a😀😀😀', { maxBytes: 2 })).toMatchObject({ html: '', outcome: 'over-limit', bytes: 3 });
  });

  it('the meta of an over-limit result is the frozen EMPTY_META', () => {
    const r = render('xx', { maxBytes: 1 });
    expect(r.meta).toBe(EMPTY_META);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(r.meta)).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(r.meta.headings)).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.isFrozen(r.meta.mermaidKinds)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('a rendered result reports the exact UTF-8 length', () => {
    const text = 'a é € 😀\n';
    expect(render(text).bytes).toBe(new TextEncoder().encode(text).length);
  });

  it('the default cap is DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES', () => {
    // Field by field, outcome first: a whole-object diff of a 4 MiB html string would take minutes.
    const r = render('a'.repeat(DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES + 1));
    expect(r.outcome).toBe('over-limit');
    expect(r.bytes).toBe(DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES + 1);
    expect(r.html === '').toBe(true);
    expect(render('a'.repeat(DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES)).outcome).toBe('rendered');
  });

  it('maxBytes 0 admits only the empty document', () => {
    expect(render('', { maxBytes: 0 }).outcome).toBe('rendered');
    expect(render(' ', { maxBytes: 0 }).outcome).toBe('over-limit');
  });

  it('an invalid maxBytes is a RangeError, not a gate that lets everything through', () => {
    for (const maxBytes of [Number.NaN, -1, 1.5, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY]) {
      expect(() => render('x', { maxBytes })).toThrow(RangeError);
    }
  });
});

/** UTF-8 bytes of a string. */
const utf8 = (s: string): number => new TextEncoder().encode(s).length;

/** Every corpus input with a file of its own (generated cases have none), read the way loadCorpus reads it. */
function corpusInputs(): { id: string; input: string }[] {
  const dir = new URL('../conformance/', import.meta.url);
  const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL('manifest.json', dir), 'utf8')) as { id: string; kind: string }[];
  return manifest
    .filter((c) => c.kind !== 'generated')
    .map((c) => ({ id: c.id, input: readFileSync(new URL(`corpus/${c.id}.md`, dir)).toString('utf8') }));
}

describe('render: the html bound (ruling C20)', () => {
  it('html of exactly maxHtmlBytes renders; one byte less is output-over-limit, with the fallback', () => {
    const src = `[r]: /${'u'.repeat(50)}\n\n[r] [r] [r] [r] \u00e9\n`;
    const html = render(src).html;
    const bytes = utf8(src);
    expect(render(src, { maxHtmlBytes: utf8(html) })).toEqual({ html, outcome: 'rendered', bytes, meta: EMPTY });
    const r = render(src, { maxHtmlBytes: utf8(html) - 1 });
    expect(r).toEqual({ html: `${FALLBACK_OPEN}${src}</pre>`, outcome: 'output-over-limit', bytes, meta: EMPTY });
    expect(r.meta).toBe(EMPTY_META);
  });

  it('every piece counts, inline ones too: each corpus case renders at its html size and stops a byte under', () => {
    for (const c of corpusInputs()) {
      const { html } = render(c.input);
      expect(render(c.input, { maxHtmlBytes: utf8(html) }).html, c.id).toBe(html);
      const under = render(c.input, { maxHtmlBytes: Math.max(0, utf8(html) - 1) });
      expect(under.outcome, c.id).toBe(html === '' ? 'rendered' : 'output-over-limit');
    }
  });

  it('rendering stops at the bound: the rest of the document is never rendered', () => {
    const md = createEngine();
    const text = md.renderer.rules.text;
    if (text === undefined) throw new Error('markdown-it has no text rule');
    let calls = 0;
    md.renderer.rules.text = (tokens, idx, options, env, self) => {
      calls += 1;
      return text(tokens, idx, options, env, self);
    };
    expect(renderWith('word\n\n'.repeat(1000), { maxHtmlBytes: 100 }, md).outcome).toBe('output-over-limit');
    expect(calls).toBeLessThan(5);
  });

  it('the default is 16 MiB, four times DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES', () => {
    // A long destination defined once and used many times: about 50 KB of input, 16 MiB of html.
    const doc = (uses: number, fill: number): string =>
      `[r]: /${'u'.repeat(1000)}\n\n${'[r],'.repeat(uses)}${'a'.repeat(fill)}\n`;
    const one = utf8(render(doc(1, 0)).html);
    const fill = 16_777_216 - one - 15_999 * (utf8(render(doc(2, 0)).html) - one);
    expect(fill).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(render(doc(16_000, fill)).outcome).toBe('rendered');
    expect(render(doc(16_000, fill + 1)).outcome).toBe('output-over-limit');
    expect(4 * DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES).toBe(16_777_216);
  });

  it('an invalid maxHtmlBytes is a RangeError, not a bound that lets everything through', () => {
    for (const maxHtmlBytes of [Number.NaN, -1, 1.5, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY]) {
      expect(() => render('x', { maxHtmlBytes })).toThrow(RangeError);
    }
  });

  it('the fallback is cut to the bound at a character, never inside an escape; below its own size it is empty', () => {
    const shell = utf8(`${FALLBACK_OPEN}</pre>`);
    expect(shell).toBe(96);
    expect(fallbackHtml('a&b', shell + 5)).toBe(`${FALLBACK_OPEN}a</pre>`);
    expect(fallbackHtml('a&b', shell + 6)).toBe(`${FALLBACK_OPEN}a&amp;</pre>`);
    expect(fallbackHtml("it's", shell + 7)).toBe(`${FALLBACK_OPEN}it</pre>`);
    expect(fallbackHtml("it's", shell + 8)).toBe(`${FALLBACK_OPEN}it&#x27;</pre>`);
    expect(fallbackHtml('\u00e9\ud83d\ude00x', shell + 5)).toBe(`${FALLBACK_OPEN}\u00e9</pre>`);
    expect(fallbackHtml('\u00e9\ud83d\ude00x', shell + 6)).toBe(`${FALLBACK_OPEN}\u00e9\ud83d\ude00</pre>`);
    expect(fallbackHtml('x', shell)).toBe(`${FALLBACK_OPEN}</pre>`);
    expect(fallbackHtml('x', shell - 1)).toBe('');
    expect(fallbackHtml('a<b', 1000)).toBe(`${FALLBACK_OPEN}a&lt;b</pre>`);
  });

  it("a failed render's fallback is cut to maxHtmlBytes too", () => {
    const src = `<a href="x">'&'</a>\n`.repeat(20);
    const r = renderWith(src, { maxHtmlBytes: 200 }, faultyEngine());
    expect(r.outcome).toBe('failed');
    expect(r.html.startsWith(FALLBACK_OPEN) && r.html.endsWith('</pre>')).toBe(true);
    const body = r.html.slice(FALLBACK_OPEN.length, -'</pre>'.length);
    expect('&lt;a href=&quot;x&quot;&gt;&#x27;&amp;&#x27;&lt;/a&gt;\n'.repeat(20).startsWith(body)).toBe(true);
    // cut before the entity that would not fit, so at most five bytes short (the longest entity is six)
    expect(utf8(r.html)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(200);
    expect(utf8(r.html)).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(195);
  });
});

describe('render: the failure fallback', () => {
  it('fault-injected: a throwing engine gives outcome failed and the exact fallback HTML', () => {
    const r = renderWith('# T\n\nbody\n', undefined, faultyEngine());
    expect(r).toEqual({
      html: '<p class="page-subtitle">This document could not be rendered; its source follows.</p><pre># T\n\nbody\n</pre>',
      outcome: 'failed',
      bytes: 10,
      meta: EMPTY,
    });
    expect(r.meta).toBe(EMPTY_META);
    expect(FALLBACK_OPEN).toBe('<p class="page-subtitle">This document could not be rendered; its source follows.</p><pre>');
  });

  it('the fallback escapes <script> and every other special character as Python html.escape does', () => {
    const r = renderWith(`<script>alert('x' & "y")</script>`, undefined, faultyEngine());
    expect(r.html).toBe(
      `${FALLBACK_OPEN}&lt;script&gt;alert(&#x27;x&#x27; &amp; &quot;y&quot;)&lt;/script&gt;</pre>`,
    );
  });

  it('the byte gate comes before the engine', () => {
    expect(renderWith('xx', { maxBytes: 1 }, faultyEngine()).outcome).toBe('over-limit');
  });
});

describe('render: options and state', () => {
  it('a rendered result has outcome rendered and a fresh meta', () => {
    const r = render('a\n');
    expect(r).toEqual({ html: '<p data-line="1-1">a</p>\n', outcome: 'rendered', bytes: 2, meta: EMPTY });
    expect(r.meta).not.toBe(EMPTY_META);
  });

  it('lineAttrs: false leaves no data-line; the default is true', () => {
    const text = '> q\n\n- a\n\n---\n';
    expect(render(text, { lineAttrs: false }).html).not.toContain('data-line');
    expect(render(text).html).toBe(render(text, { lineAttrs: true }).html);
    expect(render(text).html).toContain('data-line="1-1"');
  });

  it('determinism: render(A), render(B), render(A) gives identical results', () => {
    const a = '# Same\n\n# Same\n\n> q\n\n| x |\n|---|\n| y |\n';
    const b = '# Same\n\n# Other\n\n[l](javascript:x)\n';
    const first = render(a);
    render(b);
    expect(render(a)).toEqual(first);
    expect(render(a, { lineAttrs: false })).toEqual(render(a, { lineAttrs: false }));
  });
});
```

`test/pytext.test.ts`:

```ts
// Python text semantics and the two escapers (docserver L1, Task 3; architecture section C, global
// constraints 5 and 6). Every expected value below is what CPython 3.12 (the reference renderer's
// interpreter) returns for the same call, measured while planning.
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { escapeHtml, pyEscape } from '../src/render/escape.js';
import { PY_WS, cpLength, cpSlice, isPyWs, pyLower, pyStrip, utf8Length } from '../src/render/pyText.js';

/** The code points for which CPython 3.12's str.isspace() is true (the whole range; all are in the BMP). */
const PYTHON_WHITESPACE = [
  0x9, 0xa, 0xb, 0xc, 0xd, 0x1c, 0x1d, 0x1e, 0x1f, 0x20, 0x85, 0xa0, 0x1680, 0x2000, 0x2001, 0x2002, 0x2003,
  0x2004, 0x2005, 0x2006, 0x2007, 0x2008, 0x2009, 0x200a, 0x2028, 0x2029, 0x202f, 0x205f, 0x3000,
];

describe('PY_WS and isPyWs', () => {
  it("are exactly Python's whitespace over the Basic Multilingual Plane", () => {
    const found: number[] = [];
    for (let c = 0; c <= 0xffff; c += 1) if (isPyWs(String.fromCharCode(c))) found.push(c);
    expect(found).toEqual(PYTHON_WHITESPACE);
  });

  it('PY_WS is a character-class body that builds the same set', () => {
    const re = new RegExp(`^[${PY_WS}]+$`);
    expect(re.test(String.fromCodePoint(...PYTHON_WHITESPACE))).toBe(true);
    expect(re.test('\ufeff')).toBe(false);
    expect(re.test('\u200b')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('a string of more than one character is not whitespace', () => {
    expect(isPyWs('  ')).toBe(false);
    expect(isPyWs('')).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('pyStrip', () => {
  it("strips \\x1c, \\x85 and \\u3000 as Python does, and keeps \\ufeff, which JS's trim() strips", () => {
    expect(pyStrip('\x1c\x85\u3000 x \t\x1f')).toBe('x');
    expect(pyStrip('\ufeffx\ufeff')).toBe('\ufeffx\ufeff');
    expect('\ufeffx\ufeff'.trim()).toBe('x');
    expect('\x1cx\x85'.trim()).toBe('\x1cx\x85');
  });

  it('keeps inner whitespace and returns an all-whitespace string as empty', () => {
    expect(pyStrip(' a \xa0 b ')).toBe('a \xa0 b');
    expect(pyStrip('\u2028\u2029 \n')).toBe('');
    expect(pyStrip('')).toBe('');
  });

  it('is linear: 200000 spaces around one letter', () => {
    const pad = ' '.repeat(200_000);
    expect(pyStrip(`${pad}x${pad}`)).toBe('x');
  });
});

describe('pyLower', () => {
  it('lowers the whole string, final sigma included, as Python does', () => {
    expect(pyLower('ΟΔΟΣ')).toBe('οδος');
    expect(pyLower('ΟΔΟΣ ΑΒ')).toBe('οδος αβ');
    expect(pyLower('AΣ.')).toBe('aς.');
    expect(pyLower('ΣΑ')).toBe('σα');
  });

  it('applies full case mappings', () => {
    expect(pyLower('İstanbul')).toBe('i\u0307stanbul');
    expect(pyLower('STRASSE ẞ')).toBe('strasse ß');
    expect(pyLower('𐐀𐐁')).toBe('𐐨𐐩');
  });
});

describe('cpLength and cpSlice', () => {
  it('count code points, a surrogate pair as one and a lone surrogate as one', () => {
    expect(cpLength('a😀b')).toBe(3);
    expect(cpLength('\ud800x\udc00')).toBe(3);
    expect(cpLength('')).toBe(0);
  });

  it('cpSlice never splits a surrogate pair', () => {
    expect(cpSlice('a😀b', 2)).toBe('a😀');
    expect(cpSlice('😀😀', 1)).toBe('😀');
    expect(cpSlice('😀😀', 0)).toBe('');
    expect(cpSlice('ab', 5)).toBe('ab');
  });

  it('cpSlice(s, n) has cpLength n when s is longer, at every n', () => {
    const s = 'a😀b𝐀c\u0301d';
    for (let n = 0; n <= cpLength(s); n += 1) {
      expect(cpLength(cpSlice(s, n))).toBe(n);
      expect(s.startsWith(cpSlice(s, n))).toBe(true);
    }
  });
});

describe('utf8Length', () => {
  const samples = ['', 'a', 'é', '€', '😀', 'aé€😀', '\ud800', 'x\udc00y', '\u0000\u007f\u0080\u07ff\u0800\uffff'];

  it("equals the UTF-8 encoder's byte count when under the cap", () => {
    for (const s of samples) expect(utf8Length(s, 1000)).toBe(new TextEncoder().encode(s).length);
  });

  it('returns exactly cap + 1 once the count passes the cap, whatever character crossed it', () => {
    expect(utf8Length('aaaa', 3)).toBe(4);
    expect(utf8Length('a😀', 4)).toBe(5);
    expect(utf8Length('a😀', 2)).toBe(3);
    expect(utf8Length('éé', 3)).toBe(4);
    expect(utf8Length('éé', 4)).toBe(4);
    expect(utf8Length('x', 0)).toBe(1);
  });
});

describe('escapeHtml and pyEscape', () => {
  const md = new MarkdownIt();
  const ascii = Array.from({ length: 128 }, (_, i) => String.fromCharCode(i)).join('');

  it("escapeHtml is markdown-it's escaper: & < > \" and never '", () => {
    expect(escapeHtml(ascii)).toBe(md.utils.escapeHtml(ascii));
    expect(escapeHtml(`<a href="x">'&amp;'</a>`)).toBe('&lt;a href=&quot;x&quot;&gt;\'&amp;amp;\'&lt;/a&gt;');
  });

  it("pyEscape is Python's html.escape(s, quote=True): also ' as &#x27;", () => {
    expect(pyEscape(`<a href="x">'&amp;'</a>`)).toBe(
      '&lt;a href=&quot;x&quot;&gt;&#x27;&amp;amp;&#x27;&lt;/a&gt;',
    );
    expect(pyEscape(ascii)).toBe(escapeHtml(ascii).replace("'", '&#x27;'));
  });
});

].join('\n');

describe('checkOutputSafety: a clean sample', () => {
  it('passes every shape the renderer emits', () => {
    expect(checkOutputSafety(CLEAN)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('passes text with no tags at all', () => {
    expect(checkOutputSafety('a &lt;script&gt; b &amp; c')).toEqual([]);
    expect(checkOutputSafety('')).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('checkOutputSafety: one violation per rule', () => {
  it('a raw < that begins no tag', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<p>a < b</p>')).toEqual(['unparsable']);
    expect(rulesOf('<P>x</P>')).toEqual(['unparsable', 'unparsable']);
    expect(rulesOf("<a href='x'>y</a>")).toEqual(['unparsable']);
    expect(rulesOf('<a href="x>y</a>')).toEqual(['unparsable']);
  });

  it('a comment', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<p>x</p><!-- id:a -->')).toEqual(['comment']);
  });

  it('a tag outside the list', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<script>alert(1)</script>')).toEqual(['tag', 'tag']);
    expect(rulesOf('<iframe src="x"></iframe><style></style><svg></svg><b>x</b>')).toEqual(
      Array.from({ length: 8 }, () => 'tag'),
    );
  });

  it('on* rejected, and any other attribute outside the per-tag lists', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<img src="x" onerror="alert(1)" />')).toEqual(['attribute']);
    expect(rulesOf('<sup onclick="x">1</sup>')).toEqual(['attribute']);
    expect(rulesOf('<details open ontoggle="x">')).toEqual(['attribute']);
    expect(rulesOf('<p style="color:red">x</p>')).toEqual(['attribute']);
    expect(rulesOf('<a href="x" target="_blank">x</a>')).toEqual(['attribute']);
    expect(rulesOf('<div href="x"></div>')).toEqual(['attribute']);
  });

  it('a duplicated attribute, and a bare attribute other than open on details', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<p class="footnotes" class="footnotes">a</p>')).toEqual(['attribute']);
    expect(rulesOf('<input class="task-list-item-checkbox" checked disabled="disabled" type="checkbox">')).toEqual([
      'attribute',
      'input',
    ]);
    expect(rulesOf('<a href>x</a>')).toEqual(['attribute']);
  });

  it('a class token outside the vocabulary', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<p class="evil">x</p>')).toEqual(['class']);
    expect(rulesOf('<code class="hljs language-&quot;&gt;">x</code>')).toEqual(['class']);
    expect(rulesOf('<code class="language-Python">x</code>')).toEqual(['class']);
    expect(rulesOf('<span class="function_">x</span>')).toEqual(['class']);
  });

  it('an id with a quote, space, angle bracket, ampersand or equals sign', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<span class="doc-anchor" id="a b"></span>')).toEqual(['id']);
    expect(rulesOf('<h1 id="a&amp;b">x</h1>')).toEqual(['id']);
    expect(rulesOf('<h1 id="a=b">x</h1>')).toEqual(['id']);
  });

  it('a data-line or start that is not digits', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<p data-line="1-x">a</p>')).toEqual(['attribute']);
    expect(rulesOf('<ol start="1 onclick">\n</ol>')).toEqual(['attribute']);
  });

  it('a style other than text-align', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<td style="text-align:left;position:fixed">x</td>')).toEqual(['style']);
    expect(rulesOf('<th style="background:url(x)">x</th>')).toEqual(['style']);
  });

  it('an input other than the disabled task-list checkbox', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<input type="text" disabled="disabled">')).toEqual(['input']);
    expect(rulesOf('<input type="checkbox">')).toEqual(['input']);
    expect(rulesOf('<input type="checkbox" disabled="disabled" checked="">')).toEqual(['input']);
  });

  it('a closing tag with attributes, and a self-closing non-void element', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<p>x</p class="y">')).toEqual(['closing']);
    expect(rulesOf('<p />')).toEqual(['closing']);
  });

  it('javascript:, vbscript: and file: in href or src, in any case', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<a href="javascript:alert(1)">x</a>')).toEqual(['scheme']);
    expect(rulesOf('<a href="JaVaScRiPt:x">x</a>')).toEqual(['scheme']);
    expect(rulesOf('<a href="vbscript:x">x</a>')).toEqual(['scheme']);
    expect(rulesOf('<img src="file:///etc/x" alt="" />')).toEqual(['scheme']);
  });

  it('&#106;avascript: (a character reference hides the scheme)', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<a href="&#106;avascript:x">x</a>')).toEqual(['scheme']);
    expect(rulesOf('<a href="&#x6A;avascript:x">x</a>')).toEqual(['scheme']);
    expect(rulesOf('<a href="&#106avascript:x">x</a>')).toEqual(['scheme']);
    expect(rulesOf('<a href="javascript&colon;x">x</a>')).toEqual(['scheme']);
  });

  it('a scheme split by controls or whitespace', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<a href="java\tscript:x">x</a>')).toEqual(['scheme']);
    expect(rulesOf('<a href="java&#9;script:x">x</a>')).toEqual(['scheme']);

  it('a data: URL other than a raster image', () => {
    expect(rulesOf('<a href="data:text/html,x">x</a>')).toEqual(['scheme']);
    expect(rulesOf('<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2Zz4=" alt="" />')).toEqual(['scheme']);
  });
});

describe('decodeCharRefs', () => {

    expect(decodeCharRefs('&#106;&#x61;&#118a&colon;&Tab;&amp;&unknown;')).toBe('java:\t&&unknown;');

      .filter((c) => c.kind !== 'generated')
      .flatMap((c) => checkOutputSafety(readFileSync(new URL(`expected/${c.id}.html`, ROOT), 'utf8')).map((v) => `${c.id}: ${v}`));
    expect(flagged).toEqual([]);
  });
});

```ts
// The conformance corpus against this library's render() (docserver L1, Task 3; architecture section F,
// "How tasks hand over"). test/corpus-pending.json names the cases a later task makes pass, each with that
// task (`"T<n>"`): a pending case must FAIL, so a case that starts passing is removed from the list in the
// same change, and every other case must pass. Each task removes its own cases; Task 12 asserts the list
// is empty. The first two blocks test runCorpus and loadCorpus themselves with stand-in render functions.
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { loadCorpus, runCorpus, type RenderFn } from '../src/conformance/index.js';
import { render } from '../src/render/index.js';
import type { RenderMeta } from '../src/render/types.js';

const pending = JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL('./corpus-pending.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8')) as Record<
  string,
  string
>;
const cases = loadCorpus();

/** A stand-in renderer that returns one case's expected output, plus `extra` appended to the HTML. */
function replay(id: string, extra = ''): RenderFn {
  const c = cases.find((x) => x.id === id);
  if (c === undefined) throw new Error(`no case ${id}`);
  return () => ({
    html: c.expected.html + extra,
    outcome: 'rendered',
    bytes: 0,
    meta: JSON.parse(c.expected.meta) as RenderMeta,
  });
}

describe('loadCorpus', () => {
  it('loads every case of the manifest, in order, with its input and expected files', () => {
    const manifest = JSON.parse(
      readFileSync(new URL('../conformance/manifest.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8'),
    ) as { id: string }[];
    expect(cases.map((c) => c.id)).toEqual(manifest.map((m) => m.id));
    expect(cases.filter((c) => c.kind === 'golden')).toHaveLength(37);
    expect(cases.filter((c) => c.kind === 'hostile')).toHaveLength(14);
    expect(cases.filter((c) => !c.expected.meta.endsWith('}\n')).map((c) => c.id)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('keeps a BOM and CRLF in the input, as the reference read it', () => {
    expect(cases.find((c) => c.id === 'line-endings/bom')?.input.startsWith('\ufeff')).toBe(true);
    expect(cases.find((c) => c.id === 'line-endings/crlf')?.input.includes('\r\n')).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe('runCorpus', () => {
  it('passes a case whose output is its expected files', () => {
    const run = runCorpus(replay('text-edges'), { only: ['text-edges'] });
    expect(run).toMatchObject({ ok: true, total: 1, passed: 1 });
    expect(run.results[0]?.failures).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('fails a case on its html, and on the oracle, with one line per check', () => {
    const run = runCorpus(replay('text-edges', '<script>x</script>'), { only: ['text-edges'] });
    expect(run.ok).toBe(false);
    expect(run.results[0]?.failures.map((f) => f.split(' ')[0])).toEqual(['html', 'oracle:', 'oracle:']);
  });

  it('fails a case on its meta and on its outcome', () => {
    const good = replay('text-edges')('');
    const run = runCorpus(() => ({ ...good, outcome: 'failed', meta: { ...good.meta, title: 'x' } }), {
      only: ['text-edges'],
    });
    expect(run.results[0]?.failures.map((f) => f.split(' ')[0])).toEqual(['outcome:', 'meta']);
  });

  it('records a render that throws as a failure, not an exception', () => {
    const run = runCorpus(
      () => {
        throw new Error('boom');
      },
      { only: ['empty-docs/empty'] },
    );
    expect(run.results[0]).toMatchObject({ id: 'empty-docs/empty', ok: false, failures: ['render threw: Error: boom'] });
  });

  it('records a result with no html string as a failure', () => {
    const run = runCorpus(() => ({}) as ReturnType<RenderFn>, { only: ['empty-docs/empty'] });
    expect(run.results[0]?.failures).toEqual(['render returned no html string']);
  });

  it('refuses an unknown id, and an empty run is not ok', () => {
    expect(() => runCorpus(render, { only: ['no-such-case'] })).toThrow(/unknown case id\(s\): no-such-case/);
    expect(runCorpus(render, { only: [] })).toEqual({ ok: false, total: 0, passed: 0, results: [] });
  });
});

describe('the corpus against render()', () => {
  const run = runCorpus(render);
  const ids = new Set(cases.map((c) => c.id));

  it('pending names only known cases, each with the later task that makes it pass', () => {
    expect(Object.keys(pending).filter((id) => !ids.has(id))).toEqual([]);
    const bad = Object.entries(pending).filter(([, task]) => !/^T(?:[4-9]|1[0-2])$/.test(task));
    expect(bad).toEqual([]);
  });

  for (const r of run.results) {
    const task = pending[r.id];
    if (task !== undefined) {
      it(`${r.id}: pending must fail (until ${task})`, () => {
        expect(r.ok, `${r.id} passes now: remove it from pending`).toBe(false);
      });
    } else {
      it(`${r.id}: passes`, () => {
        expect(r.failures).toEqual([]);
      });
    }
  }
});

`src/render/pyText.ts`:

```ts
// Python text semantics for the rules ported from the reference renderer (docserver L1; architecture
// section C, global constraint 6). Wherever the reference used Python's `\s`, `str.strip()`, `str.lower()`,
// `len()` or `[:n]`, the port calls these and never JS's `\s`, `trim()`, `.length` or `.slice()`:
// - Python's whitespace is not JS's: Python counts \x1c-\x1f and \x85 and not U+FEFF; JS the reverse.
// - Python's len() and slices count code points; JS's count UTF-16 code units and can split a surrogate pair.
// Every function here is linear in its input: no regular expression that can backtrack over a long run.

/**
 * The characters Python 3.12's `str.isspace()` accepts (its `\s` and `strip()` set), as the body of a
 * regular-expression character class, for rules that build their own patterns (`new RegExp(`[${PY_WS}]`)`).
 * All are in the Basic Multilingual Plane, so each is one UTF-16 code unit.
 */
export const PY_WS = '\\t\\n\\v\\f\\r \\x1c-\\x1f\\x85\\xa0\\u1680\\u2000-\\u200a\\u2028\\u2029\\u202f\\u205f\\u3000';

const PY_WS_CHAR = new RegExp(`^[${PY_WS}]$`);

/** True when the one-code-unit string `ch` is Python whitespace. */
export function isPyWs(ch: string): boolean {
  return PY_WS_CHAR.test(ch);
}

/** Python's `str.strip()` with no argument: removes leading and trailing Python whitespace. */
export function pyStrip(s: string): string {
  let start = 0;
  let end = s.length;
  while (start < end && isPyWs(s.charAt(start))) start += 1;
  while (end > start && isPyWs(s.charAt(end - 1))) end -= 1;
  return start === 0 && end === s.length ? s : s.substring(start, end);
}

/**
 * Python's `str.lower()`. Both Python and JS apply Unicode's full lower-case mapping to the whole string,
 * including the context-sensitive final sigma ('ΟΔΟΣ' gives 'οδος' in both), so this is `toLowerCase()`
 * on the whole string. Lowering one code point at a time would give 'οδοσ', which Python never does.
 * Python 3.12 uses Unicode 15.0 and Node's ICU a later version; characters assigned since 15.0 may differ.
 */
export function pyLower(s: string): string {
  return s.toLowerCase();
}

/** Python's `len()`: the number of code points; a lone surrogate counts as one. */
export function cpLength(s: string): number {
  let n = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i += 1) {
    const c = s.charCodeAt(i);
    if (c >= 0xd800 && c <= 0xdbff && i + 1 < s.length) {
      const d = s.charCodeAt(i + 1);
      if (d >= 0xdc00 && d <= 0xdfff) i += 1;
    }
    n += 1;
  }
  return n;
}

/** Python's `s[:n]` for n >= 0: the first `n` code points. Never splits a surrogate pair. */
export function cpSlice(s: string, n: number): string {
  let i = 0;
  let taken = 0;
  while (i < s.length && taken < n) {
    const c = s.charCodeAt(i);
    if (c >= 0xd800 && c <= 0xdbff && i + 1 < s.length) {
      const d = s.charCodeAt(i + 1);
      if (d >= 0xdc00 && d <= 0xdfff) i += 1;
    }
    i += 1;
    taken += 1;
  }
  return i === s.length ? s : s.substring(0, i);
}

/**
 * The UTF-8 length of `s` (a lone surrogate counts 3 bytes, as an encoder writes U+FFFD for it), counting
 * no further than `cap`: once the count passes `cap` it returns `cap + 1`, so a caller gating on
 * `utf8Length(s, cap) > cap` never walks the rest of an oversized input.
 */
export function utf8Length(s: string, cap: number): number {
  let bytes = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i += 1) {
    const c = s.charCodeAt(i);
    if (c < 0x80) bytes += 1;
    else if (c < 0x800) bytes += 2;
    else if (c >= 0xd800 && c <= 0xdbff && i + 1 < s.length) {
      const d = s.charCodeAt(i + 1);
      if (d >= 0xdc00 && d <= 0xdfff) {
        bytes += 4;
        i += 1;
      } else bytes += 3;
    } else bytes += 3;
    if (bytes > cap) return cap + 1;
  }
  return bytes;
}
```

`src/render/escape.ts`:

```ts
// The two escapers of the port (docserver L1; architecture section C, global constraint 5). Each is used
// exactly where the reference renderer used its counterpart, because the two differ on the apostrophe:
// - escapeHtml is markdown-it's text escaper (& < > "), for everything markdown-it itself would escape;
// - pyEscape is Python's html.escape(s, quote=True) (& < > " and ' as &#x27;), for the places the reference
//   called html.escape: the failure fallback, summary text, Mermaid source, front-matter dt and dd.

const MD_SPECIAL = /[&<>"]/g;
const MD_ESCAPED: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = { '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;' };

const PY_SPECIAL = /[&<>"']/g;
const PY_ESCAPED: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = { ...MD_ESCAPED, "'": '&#x27;' };

/** markdown-it's escapeHtml: & < > " become entities; an apostrophe stays as it is. */
export function escapeHtml(s: string): string {
  return s.replace(MD_SPECIAL, (c) => MD_ESCAPED[c] ?? c);
}

/** Python's html.escape(s, quote=True): & < > " become entities, and ' becomes &#x27;. */
export function pyEscape(s: string): string {
  return s.replace(PY_SPECIAL, (c) => PY_ESCAPED[c] ?? c);
}
```

// The per-render state (docserver L1; architecture section C, rule 3 of render(), global constraint 2).
// One RenderEnv is created for each render() call and handed to markdown-it as its `env`; every rule that
// needs state for the length of one document keeps it here, never at module scope, so two renders cannot
// see each other. Later tasks add their fields (the heading slug set, the figure and table counters, the
// front-matter result) to this interface and to createEnv together.

export interface RenderEnv {
  /** Emit data-line="a-b" on block elements (RenderOptions.lineAttrs, default true). */
  readonly lineAttrs: boolean;
}

/** A fresh env for one render. */
export function createEnv(o: { lineAttrs: boolean }): RenderEnv {
  return { lineAttrs: o.lineAttrs };
}

// The line_attrs core rule (docserver L1; architecture section C, the `data-line` row; contract section
// 2.4). Each block token of the types below that has a source map gets data-line="{first}-{last}", 1-based
// and inclusive, set with attrSet so it comes after any attribute an earlier rule set (a heading's id, a
// list's start, a task item's class). It runs last in the core chain; a rule that must come before it is
// inserted with `md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', …)`. Fences, Mermaid figures and front matter carry
// data-line through their own render rules, not through this one.
import type { StateCore } from 'markdown-it';
import type { RenderEnv } from './env.js';

/** The token types the reference renderer marks, exactly (its _LINE_TOKENS). */
export const LINE_TOKENS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  'paragraph_open',
  'heading_open',
  'list_item_open',
  'tr_open',
  'blockquote_open',
  'table_open',
  'hr',
  'code_block',
  'bullet_list_open',
  'ordered_list_open',
]);

export function lineAttrs(state: StateCore): void {
  const env = state.env as RenderEnv;
  if (!env.lineAttrs) return;
  for (const t of state.tokens) {
    if (t.map && LINE_TOKENS.has(t.type)) t.attrSet('data-line', `${t.map[0] + 1}-${t.map[1]}`);
  }
}
```

`src/render/engine.ts`:

```ts
// The markdown-it instance behind render() (docserver L1; architecture section C, "Engine"; contract
// section 1). The CommonMark preset with raw HTML off, plus tables and strikethrough, configured once.
// The instance carries no per-document state: everything one render needs lives in its RenderEnv (env.ts).
//
// Pinned on purpose:
// - `html: false` is the raw-HTML wall: markdown-it escapes every tag, and only this library's own rules
//   (Task 5's allowlist) ever emit markup.
// - `maxNesting` stays the preset's 20, as in the reference: deeper blockquotes and lists stop nesting.
// - `validateLink` and `normalizeLink` are markdown-it's own: javascript:, vbscript:, file: and non-image
//   data: links stay text, and destinations are percent-encoded. Never override them.
//
// markdown-it is 14.3.2, not 15: 15 puts a code span's text into an image's alt (`![a `c`](x)` gives
// alt="a c"), where markdown-it-py, a port of 14, gives alt="a " (decision gate D1, measured on the corpus).
//
// The core chain ends with line_attrs; later rules go `before('line_attrs', …)` so data-line stays last.
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it';
import { lineAttrs } from './lineAttrs.js';

export function createEngine(): MarkdownIt {
  const md = new MarkdownIt('commonmark', {
    html: false,
    xhtmlOut: true,
    breaks: false,
    linkify: false,
    typographer: false,
  });
  md.enable(['table', 'strikethrough']);
  md.core.ruler.push('line_attrs', lineAttrs);
  return md;
}
```
