describe('nesting is capped at 64 levels per tag kind (this library, deliberately unlike the reference)', () => {
  // Departure PD8 (ruling C21). The reference nests without end: 10000 unclosed <details> lines became 10000
  // nested <details open>, deep enough to overflow a consumer's recursive walk. Here an opener past 64 open
  // levels of its kind is escaped text, and so is the closer that pairs with it, so the html stays balanced.
  // No ordinary document comes near it, and no golden moves.
  it('10000 unclosed details: 64 forced open and closed at the end, the rest escaped text', () => {
    const reference = '<details open>\n'.repeat(10000) + '</details>\n'.repeat(10000);
    const html = render('<details>\n'.repeat(10000)).html;
    expect(MAX_TAG_DEPTH).toBe(64);
    expect(html).toBe('<details open>\n'.repeat(64) + '&lt;details&gt;\n'.repeat(9936) + '</details>\n'.repeat(64));
    expect(html).not.toBe(reference);
  });

  it('65 nested details: the 65th and the closer that pairs with it are text, the rest pair as written', () => {
    const reference = '<details>\n'.repeat(65) + '</details>\n'.repeat(65);
    const html = render('<details>\n'.repeat(65) + '</details>\n'.repeat(65)).html;
    expect(html).toBe(
      '<details>\n'.repeat(64) + '&lt;details&gt;\n&lt;/details&gt;\n' + '</details>\n'.repeat(64),
    );
    expect(html).not.toBe(reference);
  });

  it('65 nested sup: the 65th and the closer that pairs with it are text', () => {
    const reference = `<p data-line="1-1">${'<sup>'.repeat(65)}x${'</sup>'.repeat(65)}</p>\n`;
    const html = render(`${'<sup>'.repeat(65)}x${'</sup>'.repeat(65)}\n`).html;
    expect(html).toBe(`<p data-line="1-1">${'<sup>'.repeat(64)}&lt;sup&gt;x&lt;/sup&gt;${'</sup>'.repeat(64)}</p>\n`);
    expect(html).not.toBe(reference);
  });

  it('each kind has its own 64 levels', () => {
    const html = render(`${'<sup>'.repeat(65)}${'<sub>'.repeat(65)}${'<kbd>'.repeat(65)}x\n`).html;
    expect(html).toBe(
      `<p data-line="1-1">${'<sup>'.repeat(64)}&lt;sup&gt;${'<sub>'.repeat(64)}&lt;sub&gt;` +
        `${'<kbd>'.repeat(64)}&lt;kbd&gt;x</p>\n`,
    );
  });

  it('the count spans the document: the 65th unclosed sup is text in its own paragraph too', () => {
    const html = render('<sup>a\n\n'.repeat(65)).html;
    const para = (k: number, body: string): string => `<p data-line="${2 * k + 1}-${2 * k + 1}">${body}a</p>\n`;
    expect(html).toBe(Array.from({ length: 64 }, (_, k) => para(k, '<sup>')).join('') + para(64, '&lt;sup&gt;'));
  });

  it("an image's alt text renders no tag, so its sup does not count", () => {
    const image = '<img src="x" alt="&lt;sup&gt;" />';
    const html = render(`${'![<sup>](x) '.repeat(100)}${'<sup>'.repeat(64)}y\n`).html;
    expect(html).toBe(`<p data-line="1-1">${`${image} `.repeat(100)}${'<sup>'.repeat(64)}y</p>\n`);
  });
});

describe('ASCII-only tag names (this library, deliberately unlike the reference)', () => {
  // The reference's Python re.I lets U+0130 and U+0131 match i, U+212A k and U+017F s: it emits the author's
  // raw <U+017Fup> tag and reads <U+017Fummary>x</U+017Fummary> as a <details> line. Here only ASCII letters
  // fold, so these stay text; no corpus case holds them.
  cases([
    [
      'inline: look-alike letters are text',
      '<\u017fup>x</\u017fup> <\u212abd>y</\u212abd> <sub>z</sub>\n',
      '<p data-line="1-1">&lt;\u017fup&gt;x&lt;/\u017fup&gt; &lt;\u212abd&gt;y&lt;/\u212abd&gt; <sub>z</sub></p>\n',
    ],
    [
      'block: look-alike letters are text',
      '<deta\u0130ls>\n\n<\u017fummary>s</\u017fummary>\n\n</deta\u0131ls>\n',
      '<p data-line="1-1">&lt;deta\u0130ls&gt;</p>\n<p data-line="3-3">&lt;\u017fummary&gt;s&lt;/\u017fummary&gt;</p>\n' +
        '<p data-line="5-5">&lt;/deta\u0131ls&gt;</p>\n',
    ],
  ]);
});

describe('comment search is linear (the reference rescans to the end from every <!--)', () => {
  // The output follows from 'lines of unterminated comments are one paragraph' and 'a run of unterminated
  // comments is text' above. The bound is a backstop: measured while planning, these take under 0.6 s here
  // and over 20 s each when the search restarts at every <!--, as the reference's does.
  it('20000 lines of unterminated <!-- render in under 5 s', () => {
    const n = 20_000;
    const started = performance.now();
    const html = render('<!--\n'.repeat(n)).html;
    expect(performance.now() - started).toBeLessThan(5000);
    expect(html).toBe(`<p data-line="1-${n}">${'&lt;!--\n'.repeat(n - 1)}&lt;!--</p>\n`);
  });

  it('40000 unterminated <!-- in one paragraph render in under 5 s', () => {
    const n = 40_000;
    const started = performance.now();
    const html = render('<!-- '.repeat(n)).html;
    expect(performance.now() - started).toBeLessThan(5000);
    expect(html).toBe(`<p data-line="1-1">${'&lt;!-- '.repeat(n - 1)}&lt;!--</p>\n`);
  });

  it('40000 images whose alt text opens a comment, each followed by an unterminated <!--, render in under 5 s', () => {
    // An image's alt text is parsed in an inline state of its own; its search must not evict the paragraph's.
    const n = 40_000;
    const started = performance.now();
    const html = render('![<!--](b) <!-- '.repeat(n)).html;
    expect(performance.now() - started).toBeLessThan(5000);
    const image = '<img src="b" alt="&lt;!--" /> &lt;!--';
    expect(html).toBe(`<p data-line="1-1">${`${image} `.repeat(n - 1)}${image}</p>\n`);
  });

  it('4000 <!-- lines that all reach one long closing line render in under 5 s', () => {
    // Every <!-- line's silent probe reaches the same closing line; its `-->` and the text after it are read once.
    const n = 4000;
    const m = 40_000;
    const started = performance.now();
    const html = render(`${'<!--\n'.repeat(n)}${'x'.repeat(m)}-->${' '.repeat(m)}y\n`).html;
    expect(performance.now() - started).toBeLessThan(5000);
    expect(html).toBe(`<p data-line="1-${n + 1}">${' '.repeat(m)}y</p>\n`);
  });
});
```

```ts
// The raw-HTML allowlist (docserver L1; architecture section C, "The raw-HTML allowlist and its rules";
// contract sections 2.1 and 2.2). Raw HTML stays off (`html: false`); these two rules recognise the few
// pieces of HTML a document may use and emit their own fixed markup, never the author's text:
//   <br>, <br/>, <br />            a hard break (inline)
//   <sup> <sub> <kbd> and closers  without attributes, unbalanced allowed, lower-cased (inline)
//   <!-- ... -->                   dropped; alone on its line, `<!-- id:X -->` becomes an anchor span
//   <details>, <details open>, </details>, <summary>text</summary>, each alone on its line (block)
// Everything else stays text, which markdown-it escapes.
//
// Ported from the reference renderer with two deliberate differences, neither visible in its corpus:
// - Tag names match ASCII letters case-insensitively and nothing else (the `i` flag without `u`). The
//   reference's Python `re.I` also lets U+0130 and U+0131 stand for `i`, U+212A for `k` and U+017F for
//   `s`, so it writes the author's `<U+017Fup>` as a raw tag and reads `<U+017Fummary>x</U+017Fummary>`
//   as a `<details>` line. Here those stay escaped text.
// - Finding a comment's `-->` is linear in the document. The reference rescans from each `<!--` to the
//   end of the text, so a document of unterminated `<!--` lines takes quadratic time. The answers are
//   the same; CommentScan (below) remembers where each search ended, per inline text and per line.
import type { StateBlock, StateInline } from 'markdown-it';
import type { RenderEnv } from './env.js';
import { pyEscape } from './escape.js';
import { PY_WS, pyLower, pyStrip } from './pyText.js';

/** What the two rules accept. The rules build their patterns from these values, never from copies. */
export const ALLOWLIST: Readonly<{
  inlineTags: readonly ['br', 'sup', 'sub', 'kbd'];
  blockLines: readonly ['<details>', '<details open>', '</details>', '<summary>…</summary>'];
  anchorId: '[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}';
}> = Object.freeze({
  inlineTags: Object.freeze(['br', 'sup', 'sub', 'kbd'] as const),
  blockLines: Object.freeze(['<details>', '<details open>', '</details>', '<summary>…</summary>'] as const),
  anchorId: '[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}' as const,
});

const [BR, ...PAIRED] = ALLOWLIST.inlineTags;

/**
 * An inline tag at the current position: `<br>` with Python whitespace and an optional `/` before the
 * `>`, or a bare `<sup>`, `<sub>`, `<kbd>` or its closer. Sticky: it matches only where lastIndex points,
 * and the rule sets lastIndex before every use. Case-insensitive for ASCII letters only (no `u` flag).
 * Group 1 is the closer's slash ('' or '/'), group 2 the tag name; both are undefined for `<br>`.
 */
export const INLINE_TAG = new RegExp(`<(?:${BR}[${PY_WS}]*\\/?|(\\/?)(${PAIRED.join('|')}))>`, 'iy');

/** A whole stripped comment that names an anchor: `<!--`, Python whitespace, `id:X`, whitespace, `-->`. */
export const COMMENT_ID = new RegExp(`^<!--[${PY_WS}]*id:(${ALLOWLIST.anchorId})[${PY_WS}]*-->$`);

/**
 * A whole stripped details line. Group 1 is the whitespace and `open` of an opener; group 2 the summary
 * text, which may hold any character but a line feed (`[^\n]`, as Python's `.`; JS's `.` would also
 * stop at U+2028 and U+2029). Case-insensitive for ASCII letters only.
 */
export const DETAILS_LINE = new RegExp(
  `^(?:<details([${PY_WS}]+open)?>|<\\/details>|<summary>([^\\n]*)<\\/summary>)$`,
  'i',
);

const LT = 0x3c;
const COMMENT_OPEN = '<!--';
const COMMENT_CLOSE = '-->';

/** One inline text's last search: `at` is the first `-->` at or after `from` in that text (-1: none). */
interface InlineSearch {
  from: number;
  at: number;
}

/**
 * Per-render memory of the comment searches, kept in the RenderEnv (never at module scope):
 * - `block`/`next`: for the document's block state, next[k] is the first line at or after k whose
 *   physical source line holds `-->` (the document's line count when none), built once per document over
 *   ALL its lines, whatever nested rule first asks;
 * - `from`/`close`/`tail`, for that block state and per line k: the source offset the line's text was last
 *   read from (-1: never), the offset of the first `-->` in that text (-1: none), and whether anything but
 *   Python whitespace follows it (1) or not (0). A closing line that many `<!--` lines reach is read once,
 *   not once per `<!--`;
 * - `inline`: the last search of each inline text, which answers every later search in that text from a
 *   position between `from` and `at`. A text nested in another (an image's alt text, a footnote's inline
 *   text) is parsed in a state of its own, so each keeps its own entry and neither evicts the other's.
 */
export interface CommentScan {
  block: StateBlock | null;
  next: Int32Array | null;
  from: Int32Array | null;
  close: Int32Array | null;
  tail: Uint8Array | null;
  readonly inline: WeakMap<StateInline, InlineSearch>;
}

export function createCommentScan(): CommentScan {
  return { block: null, next: null, from: null, close: null, tail: null, inline: new WeakMap() };
}

/** The index of the first `-->` at or after `from` in this inline text, or -1. */
function inlineClose(state: StateInline, from: number): number {
  const memo = (state.env as RenderEnv).comments.inline;
  const last = memo.get(state);
  if (last !== undefined && from >= last.from && (last.at === -1 || from <= last.at)) return last.at;
  const at = state.src.indexOf(COMMENT_CLOSE, from);
  memo.set(state, { from, at });
  return at;
}

/**
 * The safe_inline_html rule, before markdown-it's html_inline. A comment is consumed with no token, in
 * silent mode too (so a comment can hide a `]` from a link label, as in the reference); `<br>` pushes a
 * hardbreak; `<sup>`, `<sub>`, `<kbd>` and their closers push an html_inline token holding the bare,
 * lower-cased tag. Anything else returns false, and markdown-it escapes it as text.
 */
export function safeInlineHtml(state: StateInline, silent: boolean): boolean {
  const pos = state.pos;
  if (state.src.charCodeAt(pos) !== LT) return false;
  if (state.src.startsWith(COMMENT_OPEN, pos)) {
    const at = inlineClose(state, pos + COMMENT_OPEN.length);
    if (at === -1) return false;
    state.pos = at + COMMENT_CLOSE.length;
    return true;
  }
  INLINE_TAG.lastIndex = pos;
  const m = INLINE_TAG.exec(state.src);
  if (m === null) return false;
  if (!silent) {
    const name = m[2];
    if (name === undefined) state.push('hardbreak', 'br', 0);
    else state.push('html_inline', '', 0).content = `<${m[1] ?? ''}${pyLower(name)}>`;
  }
  state.pos = pos + m[0].length;
  return true;
}

/** Line k of the block state as the reference reads it: from after its indent to its end. */
function srcLine(state: StateBlock, k: number): string {
  return state.src.slice((state.bMarks[k] ?? 0) + (state.tShift[k] ?? 0), state.eMarks[k] ?? 0);
}

/**
 * For each line k, the first line at or after k whose physical source line holds `-->` (else the line
 * count). The count is the document's (bMarks holds one entry per line plus a final one), never
 * state.lineMax: a blockquote narrows lineMax to its own end while its content is parsed, and the index
 * is built on the first ask, which may come from inside one; built from that, it would end at the quote
 * and every later line would read as having no `-->` (ruling C13). The per-line memory of closeAt is
 * created with it.
 */
function closeIndex(state: StateBlock): Int32Array {
  const scan = (state.env as RenderEnv).comments;
  if (scan.block === state && scan.next !== null) return scan.next;
  const lines = state.bMarks.length - 1;
  const next = new Int32Array(lines + 1).fill(lines);
  let line = 0;
  for (let i = state.src.indexOf(COMMENT_CLOSE); i !== -1; i = state.src.indexOf(COMMENT_CLOSE, i + 1)) {
    while (line < lines && (state.eMarks[line] ?? 0) < i) line += 1;
    if (line < lines) next[line] = line;
  }
  for (let k = lines - 1; k >= 0; k -= 1) if (next[k] !== k) next[k] = next[k + 1] ?? lines;
  scan.block = state;
  scan.next = next;
  scan.from = new Int32Array(lines).fill(-1);
  scan.close = new Int32Array(lines);
  scan.tail = new Uint8Array(lines);
  return next;
}

/**
 * The offset of the first `-->` in line k's text as srcLine reads it (from after its indent to its end),
 * or -1, and with it whether text follows that `-->`; remembered per line and read start (closeIndex has
 * run for this state, and k is below the document's line count).
 */
function closeAt(state: StateBlock, k: number): number {
  const scan = (state.env as RenderEnv).comments;
  const from = scan.from as Int32Array;
  const close = scan.close as Int32Array;
  const start = (state.bMarks[k] ?? 0) + (state.tShift[k] ?? 0);
  if (from[k] === start) return close[k] ?? -1;
  const end = state.eMarks[k] ?? 0;
  const found = state.src.slice(start, end).indexOf(COMMENT_CLOSE);
  const at = found === -1 ? -1 : start + found;
  from[k] = start;
  close[k] = at;
  (scan.tail as Uint8Array)[k] = at !== -1 && pyStrip(state.src.slice(at + COMMENT_CLOSE.length, end)) !== '' ? 1 : 0;
  return at;
}

/**
 * The first line in [from, endLine) whose text (as srcLine reads it) holds `-->`, or -1: where the
 * reference's `while "-->" not in text` loop stops. A line's text is part of its physical line, so lines
 * whose physical line has no `-->` are skipped without being read.
 */
function closeLine(state: StateBlock, from: number, endLine: number): number {
  const next = closeIndex(state);
  for (let k = next[from] ?? endLine; k < endLine; k = next[k + 1] ?? endLine) {
    if (closeAt(state, k) !== -1) return k;
  }
  return -1;
}

/** A block comment starting at startLine: an anchor, a silently dropped comment, or not a block (false). */
function blockComment(state: StateBlock, startLine: number, endLine: number, silent: boolean): boolean {
  const last = closeLine(state, startLine, endLine);
  if (last === -1) return false; // unterminated: it stays paragraph text
  // text after the comment: the inline rule drops the comment (closeAt read it once for this line)
  if ((state.env as RenderEnv).comments.tail?.[last] === 1) return false;
  if (silent) return true;
  const lines: string[] = [];
  for (let k = startLine; k <= last; k += 1) lines.push(srcLine(state, k));
  const m = COMMENT_ID.exec(pyStrip(lines.join('\n')));
  if (m !== null) {
    const tok = state.push('html_block', '', 0);
    tok.content = `<span class="doc-anchor" id="${m[1] ?? ''}"></span>\n`;
    tok.map = [startLine, last + 1];
  }
  state.line = last + 1;
  return true;
}

/**
 * The safe_block_html rule, before markdown-it's html_block, with alt paragraph, reference and
 * blockquote (so these lines interrupt a paragraph; they do not end a list item). Not at an indent of
 * four or more (that is indented code).
 */
export function safeBlockHtml(state: StateBlock, startLine: number, endLine: number, silent: boolean): boolean {
  if ((state.sCount[startLine] ?? 0) - state.blkIndent >= 4) return false;
  const first = srcLine(state, startLine);
  if (first.startsWith(COMMENT_OPEN)) return blockComment(state, startLine, endLine, silent);
  const m = DETAILS_LINE.exec(pyStrip(first));
  if (m === null) return false;
  if (silent) return true;
  const tok = state.push('html_block', '', 0);
  if (m[2] !== undefined) tok.content = `<summary>${pyEscape(m[2])}</summary>\n`;
  else if (m[0].charAt(1) === '/') tok.content = '</details>\n';
  else tok.content = m[1] === undefined ? '<details>\n' : '<details open>\n';
  tok.map = [startLine, startLine + 1];
  state.line = startLine + 1;
  return true;
}
```

`src/render/details.ts`:

```ts
// The balance_details core rule (docserver L1; architecture section C, the `balance_details` row; contract
// section 2.3; ruling C21). The allowlist's rules emit details lines and inline sup, sub and kbd tags one by
// one, so a document can close one it never opened, leave one open, or nest them without end. This rule walks
// the whole token stream (every nesting level; markdown-it's block tokens are one flat list, and each inline
// token holds its own tags) and, as the reference does:
// - empties a `</details>` with no open `<details>` before it, so it renders nothing;
// - rewrites every `<details>` still open at the end to `<details open>`, so an unclosed one can never fold
//   the rest of the document out of sight, and appends one `</details>` for each at the very end of the
//   token list (after the footnotes, once Task 8 adds them).
// Unlike the reference (departure PD8, ruling C21), it also caps the nesting of each of the four tag kinds at
// MAX_TAG_DEPTH open levels in the whole document: an opener past the cap renders as escaped text, and so
// does the closer that pairs with it, so the html stays balanced and a consumer's recursive walk never meets
// more than 64 levels of one kind. An inline closer with nothing open stays a tag, as before. The tags of an
// image's alt text render as attribute text, never as tags, so they are not counted.
// It runs after the anchors rule and before line_attrs; html_block tokens carry no data-line.
import type { StateCore, Token } from 'markdown-it';
import { pyEscape } from './escape.js';

/** Most open levels of each allowlisted tag kind (details, sup, sub, kbd) in one document (ruling C21). */
export const MAX_TAG_DEPTH = 64;

const OPEN = '<details';
const CLOSE = '</details';

/** One inline tag kind's open levels, and the openers past the cap whose closers have not come yet. */
interface Depth {
  open: number;
  over: number;
}

/** Caps one inline token's sup, sub and kbd tags (the allowlist's only html_inline tokens) against `depths`. */
function capInline(children: readonly Token[], depths: Map<string, Depth>): void {
  for (const t of children) {
    if (t.type !== 'html_inline') continue;
    const closer = t.content.charAt(1) === '/';
    const name = t.content.slice(closer ? 2 : 1, -1);
    let d = depths.get(name);
    if (d === undefined) {
      d = { open: 0, over: 0 };
      depths.set(name, d);
    }
    if (!closer) {
      if (d.open < MAX_TAG_DEPTH) d.open += 1;
      else {
        d.over += 1;
        t.type = 'text';
      }
    } else if (d.over > 0) {
      d.over -= 1;
      t.type = 'text';
    } else if (d.open > 0) d.open -= 1;
  }
}

export function balanceDetails(state: StateCore): void {
  const tokens = state.tokens;
  const open: Token[] = [];
  let over = 0;
  const depths = new Map<string, Depth>();
  for (const t of tokens) {
    if (t.type === 'inline') capInline(t.children ?? [], depths);
    if (t.type !== 'html_block') continue;
    if (t.content.startsWith(OPEN)) {
      if (open.length < MAX_TAG_DEPTH) open.push(t);
      else {
        over += 1;
        t.content = pyEscape(t.content);
      }
    } else if (t.content.startsWith(CLOSE)) {
      if (over > 0) {
        over -= 1;
        t.content = pyEscape(t.content);
      } else if (open.length === 0) t.content = '';
      else open.pop();
    }
  }
  for (const t of open) {
    t.content = '<details open>\n';
    const close = new state.Token('html_block', '', 0);
    close.content = '</details>\n';
    tokens.push(close);
  }
}

```ts
// The per-render state (docserver L1; architecture section C, rule 3 of render(), global constraint 2).
// One RenderEnv is created for each render() call and handed to markdown-it as its `env`; every rule that
// needs state for the length of one document keeps it here, never at module scope, so two renders cannot
// see each other. Later tasks add their fields (the figure and table counters, the front-matter result) to
// this interface and to createEnv together.
import { createCommentScan, type CommentScan } from './allowlist.js';
import { createSlugState, type SlugState } from './slug.js';
import type { Heading } from './types.js';

export interface RenderEnv {
  /** Emit data-line="a-b" on block elements (RenderOptions.lineAttrs, default true). */
  readonly lineAttrs: boolean;
  /** The heading ids this document has handed out (the anchors rule). */
  readonly slugs: SlugState;
  /** Every heading in document order, as the anchors rule set its id (meta.headings). */
  readonly headings: Heading[];
  /** Where the allowlist's comment rules last searched for `-->` (allowlist.ts). */
  readonly comments: CommentScan;
}

/** A fresh env for one render. */
export function createEnv(o: { lineAttrs: boolean }): RenderEnv {
  return { lineAttrs: o.lineAttrs, slugs: createSlugState(), headings: [], comments: createCommentScan() };
}

`src/render/engine.ts`:

```ts
// The markdown-it instance behind render() (docserver L1; architecture section C, "Engine"; contract
// section 1). The CommonMark preset with raw HTML off, plus tables and strikethrough, configured once.
// The instance carries no per-document state: everything one render needs lives in its RenderEnv (env.ts).
//
// Pinned on purpose:
// - `html: false` is the raw-HTML wall: markdown-it escapes every tag, and only this library's own rules
//   (the allowlist, allowlist.ts) ever emit markup.
// - `maxNesting` stays the preset's 20, as in the reference: deeper blockquotes and lists stop nesting.
// - `validateLink` and `normalizeLink` are markdown-it's own: javascript:, vbscript:, file: and non-image
//   data: links stay text, and destinations are percent-encoded. Never override them.
//
// markdown-it is 14.3.2, not 15: 15 puts a code span's text into an image's alt (`![a `c`](x)` gives
// alt="a c"), where markdown-it-py, a port of 14, gives alt="a " (decision gate D1, measured on the corpus).
//
// The core chain ends with line_attrs; later rules go `before('line_attrs', …)` so data-line stays last.
// block_strip goes right after block, before inline parsing reads the text it strips (blockStrip.ts).
// The allowlist's rules go right before markdown-it's own raw-HTML rules, which html: false disables:
// safe_block_html with alt paragraph, reference and blockquote (it interrupts those, as in the reference,
// and is not a list terminator), safe_inline_html in the inline chain. balance_details runs after anchors.
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it';
import { safeBlockHtml, safeInlineHtml } from './allowlist.js';
import { blockStrip } from './blockStrip.js';
import { balanceDetails } from './details.js';
import { lineAttrs } from './lineAttrs.js';
import { anchors } from './slug.js';

export function createEngine(): MarkdownIt {
  const md = new MarkdownIt('commonmark', {
    html: false,
    xhtmlOut: true,
    breaks: false,
    linkify: false,
    typographer: false,
  });
  md.enable(['table', 'strikethrough']);
  md.core.ruler.push('line_attrs', lineAttrs);
  md.core.ruler.after('block', 'block_strip', blockStrip);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'anchors', anchors);
  md.block.ruler.before('html_block', 'safe_block_html', safeBlockHtml, {
    alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote'],
  });
  md.inline.ruler.before('html_inline', 'safe_inline_html', safeInlineHtml);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'balance_details', balanceDetails);
  return md;
}

**Decisions this task makes:**
1. **The counters and the whole keyword rule land here, not in Task 10.** Section F gives Task 6 "counters for `meta.figures` and `mermaidKinds`" and Task 10 "the `mermaidKinds` bound, `figures`". `h-fence-injection`'s expected meta is `figures: 1, mermaidKinds: ["flowchart"]` behind a `%%{init: …}%%` first line, so it can only leave the pending list with the `%%` skip in place; the `---` skip, the 40-character keyword and the 32-kind cap are the same function and are pinned here against the reference generator's own rule (`fence.test.ts`). Rows M13, M14 and M15 are section F's M10.6 and M10.7, measured now; Task 10 adds `scanRefs` and its invariants and need not move these rows.
2. **The code text is Pygments', which also drops one leading U+FEFF.** Section C says `stripnl(content) + '\n'`. Pygments' lexer preprocessing, which the reference runs on every fence it does not make a figure, first removes one leading U+FEFF, then strips leading and trailing line feeds, then adds one; measured on the reference: content U+FEFF, `x=1` renders `x=1`, content U+FEFF U+FEFF `y` renders U+FEFF `y`, and a U+FEFF after the first character stays. `codeText` does exactly this (row M9). The Mermaid source is never stripped and keeps a BOM, as in the reference.
3. **The highlighter is a private highlight.js instance.** `highlight.js/lib/core`'s default export is a mutable singleton that any other code in a page may `configure` or extend; `hljsCore.newInstance()` gives this library its own, created and filled once at load and never changed afterwards (global constraint 2: no per-render state at module scope; the instance, like the markdown-it engine, is configuration). `highlight.test.ts` changes the shared instance's class prefix and checks the output does not move (row M10).
4. **The registry is this library's, not highlight.js's.** A name resolves through a `Map` of the canonical names and aliases above only, lowered with `pyLower` (the reference's Pygments lookup lowers with Python's `str.lower()`), so highlight.js's own other names (`gyp`, `patch`, `docker`, `golang`, `rs`, `mjs`, `jsonc`) and object keys (`constructor`, `__proto__`) resolve to nothing, and the class a page carries is always a canonical name. `highlightCode` refuses any other name with a `RangeError` before highlight.js sees it (row M21): highlight.js would answer an unknown name by calling `console.error` and throwing, and `console` is not a JavaScript intrinsic (Task 12 runs the bundle in an empty VM context). No auto-detection anywhere in `src/render` (`highlight.test.ts` greps for `highlightAuto`).
5. **Unregistered names are escaped with `escapeHtml`, registered ones by highlight.js.** The reference shows both through Pygments; under normaliseForCompare (PD1) the two compare equal to it, because the normaliser decodes `&#x27;` and re-escapes with markdown-it's escaper. `fence.test.ts` pins the exact markup of both, since no reference has it.
6. **Section F's M6.8 cannot red as written.** With `ignoreIllegals: false`, highlight.js does not throw on an illegal lexeme: in its default safe mode it returns the whole block as escaped plain text. So `x-limits/code-pathological` (a generated case of Task 11 in any event) would not render `failed`, and the text compares equal under normaliseForCompare. `highlight.test.ts` pins `x = 1 ?` in Python, which highlights its number only when illegal lexemes are ignored (row M8).
7. **Normalisation hides the class, so section F's M6.1 and M6.3 red elsewhere.** normaliseForCompare reduces a code block to its text, so a wrong language class is invisible to every golden. Row M1 still reds three corpus cases through the oracle (an input-made class is not a class token, and `h-fence-injection`'s info opens a `<script>`); row M3 (`fence_info_firstword_tab`) reds only through `fence.test.ts`, which reads the classes and checks that `mermaid<TAB>x` stays code.
8. **`mermaid-figures` stays pending until Task 7.** Its html differs from the golden only by its captions (measured: the first difference is the first `<figcaption>`); its meta is already exact, and `fence.test.ts` checks it against the case's expected meta, so rows M2, M5, M12, M13, M14 and M16 red there instead of in section F's golden.
9. **The pending hand-over, measured.** The four cases Task 3 labelled `T6` pass after this task and leave the list: `fences/main`, `fences/empty`, `fences/unclosed` and `h-fence-injection`. No other case starts passing (the remaining failures are captions, alerts, tables, task lists, footnotes and front matter). 23 of the 51 cases now pass, 28 are pending.
10. **Two test files.** `highlight.test.ts` holds what section F lists for it (the registry, an unknown name, escaping, no `highlightAuto`); `fence.test.ts` holds the render-level cases, each expected string produced by the reference from the same input.
11. **`lineAttr` is shared.** The data-line value has one definition in `lineAttrs.ts`, used by the core rule and by render rules that write their own markup (fences and figures here; front matter in Task 9).
12. **Highlighting is bounded, not only the input.** Several registered grammars take time quadratic in the length of one line: a run of `_`, `1e` or `0x` makes their number and identifier modes rescan, so a single 30000-character line took 5-10 s in `ini`, `java`, `typescript` and `javascript`, and a 1 MB `ini` fence of 500-character lines about 10 s (measured on Task 12's tree; 4 MiB on one line would take hours). The input cap does not bound that. `renderFence` highlights a fence only when none of its lines is longer than `MAX_HIGHLIGHT_LINE` (256 code units) and the document's highlighted code units stay within `MAX_HIGHLIGHT_CHARS` (262144, counted in `env.highlighted`); any other fence keeps its `hljs language-NAME` class and gets `escapeHtml`'s text, exactly as an unregistered name does. Measured: 1024 lines of 255 `_` (the whole budget) take 0.25-1.7 s in the four slow grammars and under 0.25 s in the rest, a 30000-character line 1 ms, and a 3.8 MB document of such fences 0.5 s. The reference highlights everything, but PD1 compares only the text inside the wrapper, so no golden depends on it. `fence.test.ts` pins both bounds and that the fallback escapes (rows M25 and M26, and M7 through the long-line case); Task 11 adds generated cases with `maxMs` for the long lines.

```ts
// The code highlighter (docserver L1, Task 6; architecture section C, the "Fence info" row and section F's
// T6 entry). A fixed registry of languages, resolved without case and never from the input's own spelling,
// highlighted by highlight.js on a private instance with illegal lexemes ignored and no auto-detection. The
// reference highlights with Pygments, so nothing here is compared with it (departure PD1); fence.test.ts
// compares the text inside the wrapper.
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import core from 'highlight.js/lib/core';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { checkOutputSafety } from '../src/conformance/oracle.js';
import { highlightCode, LANGUAGES, resolveLanguage } from '../src/render/highlight.js';

const REGISTRY = {
  bash: ['sh', 'zsh'],
  shell: ['console'],
  css: [],
  diff: [],
  dockerfile: [],
  go: [],
  ini: ['toml'],
  java: [],
  javascript: ['js', 'jsx'],
  json: [],
  markdown: ['md'],
  python: ['py'],
  rust: [],
  sql: [],
  typescript: ['ts', 'tsx'],
  xml: ['html', 'svg'],
  yaml: ['yml'],
  plaintext: ['text'],
};

/** highlight.js's own escaping of text: & < > " and ' (as &#x27;). */
function hljsEscape(s: string): string {
  const map: Record<string, string> = { '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;', "'": '&#x27;' };
  return s.replace(/[&<>"']/g, (c) => map[c] ?? c);
}

describe('the language registry', () => {
  it('is exactly these languages and their other names, frozen', () => {
    expect(LANGUAGES).toEqual(REGISTRY);
    expect(Object.keys(LANGUAGES)).toEqual(Object.keys(REGISTRY));
    expect(Object.isFrozen(LANGUAGES)).toBe(true);
    expect(Object.values(LANGUAGES).every((names) => Object.isFrozen(names))).toBe(true);
  });

  it('resolves every name and other name to its canonical name, in any case', () => {
    for (const [name, aliases] of Object.entries(REGISTRY)) {
      for (const n of [name, ...aliases]) {
        expect(resolveLanguage(n)).toBe(name);
        expect(resolveLanguage(n.toUpperCase())).toBe(name);
      }
    }
    expect(resolveLanguage('PyThOn')).toBe('python');
  });

  it("resolves nothing else: not highlight.js's own other names, not object keys, not padded names", () => {
    const others = ['', 'nonsense', 'mermaid', 'gyp', 'ipython', 'patch', 'docker', 'golang', 'rs', 'mjs', 'jsonc'];
    const keys = ['constructor', '__proto__', 'toString', 'hasOwnProperty', 'valueOf'];
    const padded = [' python', 'python ', 'python\t', 'py py', 'language-python'];
    expect([...others, ...keys, ...padded].map((n) => resolveLanguage(n)).filter((r) => r !== null)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('highlightCode', () => {
  const SAMPLE =
    '<&>"\' </code></pre></div><script>alert(1)</script> <!-- c --> ${a} `b` # c // d /* e */ -- f\n' +
    'class A(B):\n  def f(self): return "x" if a <= 1 else \'y\'\n<div onclick="x"><style>a{}</style></div>\n';

  for (const name of Object.keys(REGISTRY)) {
    it(`${name}: the text escaped, and nothing added but highlight.js spans`, () => {
      const html = highlightCode(SAMPLE, name);
      const tags = html.match(/<[^>]*>/g) ?? [];
      expect(tags.filter((t) => !/^<span class="[^"<>&]*">$|^<\/span>$/.test(t))).toEqual([]);
      expect(html.replace(/<[^>]*>/g, '')).toBe(hljsEscape(SAMPLE));
      expect(checkOutputSafety(`<pre><code class="hljs language-${name}">${html}</code></pre>`)).toEqual([]);
    });
  }

  it('ignores an illegal lexeme instead of giving up on the block', () => {
    expect(highlightCode('x = 1 ?\n', 'python')).toBe('x = <span class="hljs-number">1</span> ?\n');
  });

  it('refuses a name the registry does not hold', () => {
    expect(() => highlightCode('x', 'gyp')).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => highlightCode('x', 'Python')).toThrow(RangeError);
  });

  it("uses its own highlight.js instance: changing the package's shared instance does not move it", () => {
    const before = highlightCode("print('hi')\n", 'python');
    core.configure({ classPrefix: 'changed-' });
    try {
      expect(highlightCode("print('hi')\n", 'python')).toBe(before);
    } finally {
      core.configure({ classPrefix: 'hljs-' });
    }
  });
});

describe('the highlighter in src/render', () => {
  const dir = new URL('../src/render/', import.meta.url);
  const sources = readdirSync(dir)
    .filter((f) => f.endsWith('.ts'))
    .map((f) => ({ file: f, text: readFileSync(new URL(f, dir), 'utf8') }));

  it('never auto-detects a language', () => {
    expect(sources.filter((s) => s.text.includes('highlightAuto')).map((s) => s.file)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("imports highlight.js's core and the registered languages only, all in highlight.ts", () => {
    const imports = sources.flatMap((s) =>
      [...s.text.matchAll(/from '(highlight\.js[^']*)'/g)].map((m) => `${s.file} ${m[1] ?? ''}`),
    );
    expect(imports.sort()).toEqual(
      [
        'highlight.ts highlight.js/lib/core',
        ...Object.keys(REGISTRY).map((n) => `highlight.ts highlight.js/lib/languages/${n}`),
      ].sort(),
    );
  });
});

// Fences and Mermaid figures (docserver L1, Task 6; architecture section C, the "Fence info" and "Meta" rows;
// contract sections 2.5 and 2.6). Every expected html string and every expected figure count and kind list
// in the first four blocks was produced by the reference renderer and the golden generator's mermaid-kind
// rule from the same input. Code blocks are compared after normaliseForCompare (departure PD1: the
// reference highlights with Pygments and this library with highlight.js, so only the wrapper and the text
// can be equal); figures are left alone by it, so they are compared exactly. The later blocks pin this
// library's own markup inside the wrapper, which no reference has. Captions are Task 7's: no case here puts
// a `*Figure N. …*` paragraph after a figure.
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { loadCorpus } from '../src/conformance/index.js';
import { normaliseForCompare } from '../src/conformance/normalise.js';
import { checkOutputSafety } from '../src/conformance/oracle.js';
import { createEngine } from '../src/render/engine.js';
import { renderFence } from '../src/render/fence.js';
import { render } from '../src/render/index.js';

type Case = readonly [name: string, src: string, html: string];
type MetaCase = readonly [name: string, src: string, figures: number, kinds: readonly string[]];

function cases(list: readonly Case[]): void {
  for (const [name, src, html] of list) {
    it(name, () => {
      expect(normaliseForCompare(render(src).html)).toBe(html);
    });
  }
}

/** The class attribute of the <code> in every codehilite wrapper, in document order. */
function codeClasses(html: string): string[] {
  return [...html.matchAll(/<div class="codehilite"[^>]*><pre><code class="([^"]*)">/g)].map((m) => m[1] ?? '');
}

/** One fence per info string, each holding the line `x`. */
function fences(infos: readonly string[]): string {
  return infos.map((info) => `\`\`\`${info}\nx\n\`\`\`\n`).join('\n');
}

`src/render/highlight.ts`:

```ts
// The code highlighter (docserver L1; architecture section C, the "Fence info" row; ruling C1's PD1).
// highlight.js's core with a fixed set of languages. A fence's name resolves through LANGUAGES only, without
// case (the reference's Pygments lookup lowers the name too), so the language class a page carries is always
// one of these canonical names and never the author's spelling. Highlighting ignores illegal lexemes (a
// block is highlighted as far as it can be rather than dropped to plain text) and never guesses a language.
//
// The languages are registered on a private highlight.js instance (newInstance), created once at load and
// never changed afterwards: the package's shared instance is a mutable singleton that any other code in the
// page may configure or extend, and that must not move this library's output. highlight.js escapes the text
// itself (& < > " and ' as &#x27;) and adds only <span class="..."> markup; the reference's Pygments markup
// differs, so the corpus compares the text inside the wrapper (normaliseForCompare).
import hljsCore from 'highlight.js/lib/core';
import bash from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/bash';
import css from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/css';
import diff from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/diff';
import dockerfile from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/dockerfile';
import go from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/go';
import ini from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/ini';
import java from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/java';
import javascript from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/javascript';
import json from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/json';
import markdown from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/markdown';
import plaintext from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/plaintext';
import python from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/python';
import rust from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/rust';
import shell from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/shell';
import sql from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/sql';
import typescript from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/typescript';
import xml from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/xml';
import yaml from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/yaml';
import { pyLower } from './pyText.js';

type LanguageDefinition = Parameters<typeof hljsCore.registerLanguage>[1];

/** Each registered language: its canonical name, its highlight.js definition, its other names. */
const DEFINITIONS: readonly (readonly [name: string, definition: LanguageDefinition, aliases: readonly string[]])[] = [
  ['bash', bash, ['sh', 'zsh']],
  ['shell', shell, ['console']],
  ['css', css, []],
  ['diff', diff, []],
  ['dockerfile', dockerfile, []],
  ['go', go, []],
  ['ini', ini, ['toml']],
  ['java', java, []],
  ['javascript', javascript, ['js', 'jsx']],
  ['json', json, []],
  ['markdown', markdown, ['md']],
  ['python', python, ['py']],
  ['rust', rust, []],
  ['sql', sql, []],
  ['typescript', typescript, ['ts', 'tsx']],
  ['xml', xml, ['html', 'svg']],
  ['yaml', yaml, ['yml']],
  ['plaintext', plaintext, ['text']],
];

/** The registry: each canonical language name and the other names that resolve to it. Frozen. */
export const LANGUAGES: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>> = Object.freeze(
  Object.fromEntries(DEFINITIONS.map(([name, , aliases]) => [name, Object.freeze([...aliases])])),
);

/** Every name and other name, lower-case, to its canonical name. A Map, so no object key ever resolves. */
const BY_NAME: ReadonlyMap<string, string> = new Map(
  DEFINITIONS.flatMap(([name, , aliases]) => [name, ...aliases].map((n) => [n, name] as const)),
);

const hljs = hljsCore.newInstance();
for (const [name, definition] of DEFINITIONS) hljs.registerLanguage(name, definition);

/**
 * The canonical name of a registered language, or null. `info` is the first word of a fence's info string
 * (fence.ts); it is lowered the Python way and must otherwise match a name exactly: no trimming here.
 */
export function resolveLanguage(info: string): string | null {
  return BY_NAME.get(pyLower(info)) ?? null;
}

/**
 * `text` highlighted as `language`, a canonical name resolveLanguage returned: escaped text and
 * highlight.js spans. Throws RangeError for any other name.
 */
export function highlightCode(text: string, language: string): string {
  if (!Object.hasOwn(LANGUAGES, language)) throw new RangeError(`highlightCode: unregistered language ${language}`);
  return hljs.highlight(text, { language, ignoreIllegals: true }).value;
}

`src/render/fence.ts`:

```ts
// The fence render rule (docserver L1; architecture section C, the "Fence info" and "Meta" rows; contract
// sections 2.5 and 2.6). A fence's name is the first word of its info string as the reference reads it:
// stripped the Python way, then split on a space only (a tab does not separate), never entity-decoded.
// - Exactly `mermaid` (case-sensitive) makes a figure. Its source is the raw fence content, escaped with
//   Python's html.escape (pyEscape: `'` becomes &#x27;), not stripped:
//     <figure class="mermaid-figure"{ data-line}><pre class="mermaid">{source}</pre></figure>\n
//   The figure is counted for meta.figures and its diagram keyword recorded for meta.mermaidKinds.
// - Anything else is code:
//     <div class="codehilite"{ data-line}><pre><code class="hljs{ language-NAME}">{code}</code></pre></div>\n
//   NAME is a canonical name from the registry (highlight.ts), never the author's text. The code is the
//   text the reference's highlighter (Pygments) shows: one leading U+FEFF removed, leading and trailing
//   line feeds removed, one line feed added. A registered language is highlighted by highlight.js; any
//   other name gets the text escaped as markdown-it escapes text.
// - Highlighting is bounded, not only the input: several registered grammars (ini, java, javascript and
//   typescript among them) take time quadratic in a line's length, so a 30000-character line took 5-10 s.
//   A fence with a line longer than MAX_HIGHLIGHT_LINE code units, or one that would take the document past
//   MAX_HIGHLIGHT_CHARS highlighted code units, keeps its language class and gets the escaped text, as an
//   unregistered name does. The corpus compares the text inside the wrapper (PD1), so no golden depends
//   on which fences were highlighted.
// Task 7's figcaption rule adds the caption; scanRefs (Task 10) reads fenceName, MERMAID and mermaidKind.
import type { Token } from 'markdown-it';
import type { RenderEnv } from './env.js';
import { escapeHtml, pyEscape } from './escape.js';
import { highlightCode, resolveLanguage } from './highlight.js';
import { lineAttr } from './lineAttrs.js';
import { pyStrip } from './pyText.js';

/** The fence name that makes a Mermaid figure. */
export const MERMAID = 'mermaid';

/** At most this many distinct diagram keywords in meta.mermaidKinds. */
export const MAX_MERMAID_KINDS = 32;

/** A fence is highlighted only when none of its lines is longer than this, in code units. */
export const MAX_HIGHLIGHT_LINE = 256;

/** At most this many code units of one document are highlighted; a fence that would pass it is escaped text. */
export const MAX_HIGHLIGHT_CHARS = 262_144;

/** A diagram keyword: an ASCII letter, then up to 39 ASCII letters, digits, `_` or `-`, at a line's start. */
const KIND = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,39}/;

const BOM = 0xfeff;
const LF = 0x0a;

/** The first word of a fence's info string: Python's `info.strip().split(" ")[0]`. */
export function fenceName(info: string): string {
  return pyStrip(info).split(' ')[0] ?? '';
}

/**
 * The code text of a fence, as the reference's highlighter reads it (Pygments' lexer preprocessing): one
 * leading U+FEFF removed, then every leading and trailing line feed, then one line feed added.
 */
export function codeText(content: string): string {
  let start = content.charCodeAt(0) === BOM ? 1 : 0;
  let end = content.length;
  while (start < end && content.charCodeAt(start) === LF) start += 1;
  while (end > start && content.charCodeAt(end - 1) === LF) end -= 1;
  return `${content.substring(start, end)}\n`;
}

/**
 * The diagram keyword of a Mermaid source, or null. Lines are read stripped the Python way: blank lines and
 * `%%` lines are skipped; then a `---` line opens a block skipped through the next `---` (no closing line:
 * null); then blank and `%%` lines again; the keyword is the KIND at the start of the next line.
 */
export function mermaidKind(source: string): string | null {
  const lines = source.split('\n').map(pyStrip);
  const skip = (from: number): number => {
    let i = from;
    while (i < lines.length && (lines[i] === '' || (lines[i] ?? '').startsWith('%%'))) i += 1;
    return i;
  };
  let i = skip(0);
  if (lines[i] === '---') {
    i += 1;
    while (i < lines.length && lines[i] !== '---') i += 1;
    if (i >= lines.length) return null;
    i = skip(i + 1);
  }
  const line = lines[i];
  return line === undefined ? null : (KIND.exec(line)?.[0] ?? null);
}

/** Whether no line of `text` is longer than MAX_HIGHLIGHT_LINE code units. */
function shortLines(text: string): boolean {
  for (let from = 0; from < text.length; ) {
    const end = text.indexOf('\n', from);
    const stop = end === -1 ? text.length : end;
    if (stop - from > MAX_HIGHLIGHT_LINE) return false;
    from = stop + 1;
  }
  return true;
}

/** Count one rendered figure and record its keyword: distinct, in document order, at most MAX_MERMAID_KINDS. */
function recordFigure(env: RenderEnv, source: string): void {
  env.figures += 1;
  const kind = mermaidKind(source);
  if (kind !== null && !env.mermaidKinds.includes(kind) && env.mermaidKinds.length < MAX_MERMAID_KINDS) {
    env.mermaidKinds.push(kind);
  }
}

/** The fence render rule (markdown-it's `renderer.rules.fence`). */
export function renderFence(tokens: Token[], idx: number, _options: unknown, env: RenderEnv): string {
  const token = tokens[idx];
  if (token === undefined) return '';
  const name = fenceName(token.info);
  const dl = lineAttr(token, env);
  if (name === MERMAID) {
    recordFigure(env, token.content);
    return `<figure class="mermaid-figure"${dl}><pre class="mermaid">${pyEscape(token.content)}</pre></figure>\n`;
  }
  const text = codeText(token.content);
  const language = resolveLanguage(name);
  const highlight = language !== null && env.highlighted + text.length <= MAX_HIGHLIGHT_CHARS && shortLines(text);
  if (highlight) env.highlighted += text.length;
  const code = highlight ? highlightCode(text, language) : escapeHtml(text);
  const cls = language === null ? 'hljs' : `hljs language-${language}`;
  return `<div class="codehilite"${dl}><pre><code class="${cls}">${code}</code></pre></div>\n`;
}
```

```ts
// The line_attrs core rule (docserver L1; architecture section C, the `data-line` row; contract section
// 2.4). Each block token of the types below that has a source map gets data-line="{first}-{last}", 1-based
// and inclusive, set with attrSet so it comes after any attribute an earlier rule set (a heading's id, a
// list's start, a task item's class). It runs last in the core chain; a rule that must come before it is
// inserted with `md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', …)`. Fences, Mermaid figures and front matter carry
// data-line through their own render rules, not through this one: those rules write lineAttr(token, env).
import type { StateCore, Token } from 'markdown-it';
import type { RenderEnv } from './env.js';

/** The token types the reference renderer marks, exactly (its _LINE_TOKENS). */
export const LINE_TOKENS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  'paragraph_open',
  'heading_open',
  'list_item_open',
  'tr_open',
  'blockquote_open',
  'table_open',
  'hr',
  'code_block',
  'bullet_list_open',
  'ordered_list_open',
]);

/** The data-line value of a source map: its first and last line, 1-based and inclusive. */
function lineValue(map: [number, number]): string {
  return `${map[0] + 1}-${map[1]}`;
}

export function lineAttrs(state: StateCore): void {
  const env = state.env as RenderEnv;
  if (!env.lineAttrs) return;
  for (const t of state.tokens) {
    if (t.map && LINE_TOKENS.has(t.type)) t.attrSet('data-line', lineValue(t.map));
  }
}

/**
 * The data-line attribute a render rule writes into its own markup (fence.ts; front matter in Task 9):
 * ` data-line="{first}-{last}"`, or '' when the env has lineAttrs off or the token has no source map.
 */
export function lineAttr(token: Token, env: RenderEnv): string {
  return env.lineAttrs && token.map ? ` data-line="${lineValue(token.map)}"` : '';
}

// The per-render state (docserver L1; architecture section C, rule 3 of render(), global constraint 2).
// One RenderEnv is created for each render() call and handed to markdown-it as its `env`; every rule that
// needs state for the length of one document keeps it here, never at module scope, so two renders cannot
// see each other. Later tasks add their fields (the figure and table counters, the front-matter result) to
// this interface and to createEnv together.
import { createCommentScan, type CommentScan } from './allowlist.js';
import { createSlugState, type SlugState } from './slug.js';
import type { Heading } from './types.js';

export interface RenderEnv {
  /** Emit data-line="a-b" on block elements (RenderOptions.lineAttrs, default true). */
  readonly lineAttrs: boolean;
  /** The heading ids this document has handed out (the anchors rule). */
  readonly slugs: SlugState;
  /** Every heading in document order, as the anchors rule set its id (meta.headings). */
  readonly headings: Heading[];
  /** Where the allowlist's comment rules last searched for `-->` (allowlist.ts). */
  readonly comments: CommentScan;
  /** Mermaid figures the fence rule has emitted so far (meta.figures; fence.ts). */
  figures: number;
  /** Their distinct diagram keywords, in document order, at most 32 (meta.mermaidKinds; fence.ts). */
  readonly mermaidKinds: string[];
  /** Code units the fence rule has highlighted so far, at most MAX_HIGHLIGHT_CHARS (fence.ts). */
  highlighted: number;
}

/** A fresh env for one render. */
export function createEnv(o: { lineAttrs: boolean }): RenderEnv {
  return {
    lineAttrs: o.lineAttrs,
    slugs: createSlugState(),
    headings: [],
    comments: createCommentScan(),
    figures: 0,
    mermaidKinds: [],
    highlighted: 0,
  };
}
```

// The meta of a rendered document (docserver L1; architecture section C, the "Meta" row; ruling C2).
// Every field is read from what the rules recorded in the document's RenderEnv while it was parsed and
// rendered, so meta and html come from one pass and cannot disagree. Task 4 filled `headings` and `title`,
// Task 6 `figures` and `mermaidKinds` (the fence rule, fence.ts); Task 9 fills `front` and `frontList`,
// Task 8 `tables`.
import type { RenderEnv } from './env.js';
import type { RenderMeta } from './types.js';

/** The meta of one rendered document. Call it after the env's render has finished. */
export function collectMeta(env: RenderEnv): RenderMeta {
  const headings = env.headings;
  return {
    front: null,
    frontList: null,
    title: headings.find((h) => h.level === 1)?.text ?? null,
    headings,
    figures: env.figures,
    tables: 0,
    mermaidKinds: env.mermaidKinds,
  };
}
```

```ts
// The markdown-it instance behind render() (docserver L1; architecture section C, "Engine"; contract
// section 1). The CommonMark preset with raw HTML off, plus tables and strikethrough, configured once.
// The instance carries no per-document state: everything one render needs lives in its RenderEnv (env.ts).
//
// Pinned on purpose:
// - `html: false` is the raw-HTML wall: markdown-it escapes every tag, and only this library's own rules
//   (the allowlist, allowlist.ts) ever emit markup.
// - `maxNesting` stays the preset's 20, as in the reference: deeper blockquotes and lists stop nesting.
// - `validateLink` and `normalizeLink` are markdown-it's own: javascript:, vbscript:, file: and non-image
//   data: links stay text, and destinations are percent-encoded. Never override them.
//
// markdown-it is 14.3.2, not 15: 15 puts a code span's text into an image's alt (`![a `c`](x)` gives
// alt="a c"), where markdown-it-py, a port of 14, gives alt="a " (decision gate D1, measured on the corpus).
//
// The core chain ends with line_attrs; later rules go `before('line_attrs', …)` so data-line stays last.
// block_strip goes right after block, before inline parsing reads the text it strips (blockStrip.ts).
// The allowlist's rules go right before markdown-it's own raw-HTML rules, which html: false disables:
// safe_block_html with alt paragraph, reference and blockquote (it interrupts those, as in the reference,
// and is not a list terminator), safe_inline_html in the inline chain. balance_details runs after anchors.
// Fences render through this library's own rule (fence.ts), not markdown-it's: a Mermaid figure or a
// highlighted code block, with options.highlight left unset.
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it';
import { safeBlockHtml, safeInlineHtml } from './allowlist.js';
import { blockStrip } from './blockStrip.js';
import { balanceDetails } from './details.js';
import { renderFence } from './fence.js';
import { lineAttrs } from './lineAttrs.js';
import { anchors } from './slug.js';

export function createEngine(): MarkdownIt {
  const md = new MarkdownIt('commonmark', {
    html: false,
    xhtmlOut: true,
    breaks: false,
    linkify: false,
    typographer: false,
  });
  md.enable(['table', 'strikethrough']);
  md.core.ruler.push('line_attrs', lineAttrs);
  md.core.ruler.after('block', 'block_strip', blockStrip);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'anchors', anchors);
  md.block.ruler.before('html_block', 'safe_block_html', safeBlockHtml, {
    alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote'],
  });
  md.inline.ruler.before('html_inline', 'safe_inline_html', safeInlineHtml);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'balance_details', balanceDetails);
  md.renderer.rules.fence = renderFence;
  return md;
}
```

### Task 7: Figure captions and alerts

**Model routing:** `sonnet`, effort `high` — two core rules that stand in for the reference's two HTML post-passes (a caption regex and an alert regex over finished HTML) and must agree with them on the token stream, quirks included, plus the `noLine` hook in `line_attrs`. Every expected string in the two new test files was produced by the reference renderer from the same input. Every number below was measured on the shared scratch tree at Task 6's commit; the mutations were measured each in its own throwaway copy.

**Architecture rows:** section F, T7 (files, the `figcaption` and `alerts` core rules, the `alert_open`/`alert_close` render rules, `meta.noLine` honoured by `line_attrs`, M7.1-M7.9); section C (the "Caption" and "Alerts" rows of "The raw-HTML allowlist and its rules", the final core order `…, anchors, balance_details, alerts, figcaption, table_code, line_attrs`); contract sections 2.4, 2.7 and 2.8, and section 6 items 10 and 11; ruling C8 (the core chain). Task 4's, Task 5's and Task 6's hand-over conventions (per-render state in `RenderEnv`, data-line written last and through `lineAttr(token, env)` by render rules, a caption recorded on the fence token for `renderFence`, the pending list). Global constraints 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 12.

**Interfaces:**

- Produces, in `src/render/figcaption.ts` (imports `markdown-it` types, `fence.ts`, `pyText.ts`, `tokens.ts`):
  - `export const CAPTION: RegExp` — `^<em>(Figure[PY_WS]+\p{Nd}+\.[\s\S]*?)</em>$` with the `u` flag, matched against a paragraph's rendered inline HTML; group 1 is the caption.
  - `export function figcaption(state: StateCore): void` — the core rule.
- Produces, in `src/render/alerts.ts` (imports `markdown-it` types, `env.ts` types, `lineAttrs.ts`, `pyText.ts`, `tokens.ts`):
  - `export const ALERT_TITLES: Readonly<Record<string, string>>` — `NOTE: 'Note'`, `TIP: 'Tip'`, `IMPORTANT: 'Important'`, `WARNING: 'Warning'`, `CAUTION: 'Caution'`, in this order, frozen.
  - `export const MARKER: RegExp` — `^\[!(NOTE|TIP|IMPORTANT|WARNING|CAUTION)\][ \t]*`, built from `ALERT_TITLES`, no flags.
  - `export interface AlertMeta { readonly kind: string; readonly title: string; readonly bare: boolean }` — what an `alert_open` token's `meta` holds.
  - `export function alerts(state: StateCore): void` — the core rule.

- Produces, in `src/render/tokens.ts` (imports `markdown-it` types and `pyText.ts`): `export function skipBlank(tokens: readonly Token[], from: number): number` and `export function removeTokens(tokens: Token[], drop: ReadonlySet<number>): void`.
- Produces, in `src/render/fence.ts`: `export interface FenceMeta { readonly caption: string }` — what the figcaption rule records on a Mermaid fence token's `meta`.
- Produces, in `src/render/lineAttrs.ts`: `export interface LineMeta { readonly noLine?: boolean }`; `lineAttr(token, env)` keeps its signature and now also returns `''` for a token marked `noLine`.
- Produces, for every later task:
  - **The core chain is `normalize, block, block_strip, inline, text_join, anchors, balance_details, alerts, figcaption, line_attrs`.** Task 8's `table_code` goes `before('line_attrs')`, so after `figcaption`, as section C orders it; its `footnote_tail` (inserted after `inline` by the plugin) and `task_lists` (before `text_join`) run before both rules, so an alert or a caption inside a footnote is made like any other.
  - **A rule that rebuilds a block without its data-line** sets `token.meta = { noLine: true } satisfies LineMeta`.
  - **A rule that needs "the next block, as the reference's HTML patterns saw it"** uses `skipBlank`; a rule that drops tokens collects their indexes and calls `removeTokens` once.
  - **Pending labels are `T8`-`T12` only** (`corpus.test.ts`).

**Decisions this task makes:**
1. **Token rules, with parity measured.** Section C specifies both as token rules; the reference implements both as regular expressions over finished HTML (contract 2.7 and 2.8). Each rule reproduces what the reference's pattern can see on markdown-it's output: the caption pattern needs `</figure>`, whitespace, then `<p…><em>Figure …</em></p>`; the alert pattern needs `<blockquote…>`, whitespace, `<p…>[!KIND]`. The 19 cases of the first block of each test file are the reference's own output for the same input (decision 10), and a seeded run of 4000 random documents built from fences, captions, markers, lists, blockquotes and details lines matched the reference on every one after normaliseForCompare (measured while planning, item 4).
2. **The caption pattern is the reference's, read on the rendered inline.** Python's `\s` is `PY_WS` (it includes U+001F, which JavaScript's lacks) and Python's `\d` is any Unicode decimal digit, so `\p{Nd}` with the `u` flag (`Figure ١.` and fullwidth digits are captions in the reference). Section C's `(?:(?!</p>)[\s\S])*?` becomes `[\s\S]*?` with a `$` anchor: rendered inline content never holds `</p>` (markdown-it escapes `<` in text; the allowlist emits only `br`, `sup`, `sub` and `kbd`), so the paragraph's own `</p>` is the only one the reference could meet, and a guard that cannot fire would have no red. The caption is group 1 of the rendered HTML, so it is escaped as the paragraph's text was, and `*Figure 1. a* *b*` keeps the reference's unbalanced `Figure 1. a</em> <em>b` (risk 6 of section H).
3. **"The next block" steps over blocks that render nothing.** Section C says the next sibling; the reference's `\s*` also steps over a stray `</details>` (an html_block Task 5 empties) and over a dropped comment (which leaves no token), measured: `` ```mermaid `` A `` ``` ``, `</details>`, `*Figure 2. b*` is captioned, and `> </details>` before `> [!TIP]` still makes an alert. An anchor, a details line, a heading or another figure in between stops both rules. `skipBlank` holds the one definition.
4. **One place the port does not follow the reference: a caption never reaches past the block after its figure.** In a tight list the paragraph after a figure renders no `<p>`, so the reference's pattern keeps looking, past `</li>` and `</ul>`, for the first `</em></p>`; when a later paragraph ends in emphasis it moves everything in between into the figcaption and leaves the figure, the list and that paragraph unbalanced (measured: `- ` + Mermaid fence + `  *Figure 1. x*`, a blank line, `*y*`). This library treats a hidden paragraph as no caption, as section C says, and the HTML stays balanced. No corpus case has this shape and no golden moves; `figcaption.test.ts`'s last block pins both outputs. This is departure PD7 (ruling C12): parity would have meant emitting unbalanced HTML.
5. **Where section C's conditions are implied or unreachable.** The caption's "same level" is implied (a paragraph_open directly after a fence, past blank blocks, is its sibling), so it is not checked. A blockquote's paragraph is never hidden (markdown-it hides only a tight list item's own paragraphs), so the alert rule does not check `hidden`; the caption rule does, and row M3 reds it through a tight list. mermaid-figures' `mermaid_in_list` is a loose list, so section F's M7.3 cannot red there.
6. **The marker is read from the first paragraph's first text token, after `text_join`.** The reference matches HTML, so whatever renders `[!NOTE]` counts: `\[!NOTE]`, `&#91;!TIP&#93;` and `[!NO<!-- c -->TE]` make alerts, a link `[!NOTE](u)` or a reference `[!TIP]` does not, and `text_join` is what makes each of those one text token. After the marker, spaces and tabs go (Python whitespace such as U+3000 stays), then one line break: a line feed inside the text itself (`&#10;`), or else a softbreak or hardbreak token right after a text the marker emptied (`<br>`, two trailing spaces, a backslash); a second break stays.
7. **The rebuilt paragraph.** The reference drops the first `<p data-line>` and writes a bare `<p>`; here the paragraph_open is marked `noLine`, which `line_attrs` and `lineAttr` honour (one predicate, `lined`). When nothing is left after the marker, the reference strips the `</p>` and keeps its line feed; here the paragraph's three tokens are dropped and `renderAlertOpen` writes that line feed after the title (`AlertMeta.bare`).
8. **"No alert inside an alert" resumes after the alert's close.** The reference skips a match that starts inside an earlier replacement; the rule converts a blockquote and continues from its matching `blockquote_close` (the next one at the same level), which is section C's depth counter. Alerts inside a plain blockquote and alerts side by side are still made. `alert_open`/`alert_close` keep the blockquote's map and level; `LINE_TOKENS` is unchanged, and the render rule writes the div's data-line through `lineAttr`, as fences do.
9. **`tokens.ts` is a file section B does not list.** Both rules need the same "next block" and the same one-pass removal (an index set, compacted once, so a document with many captions or bare alerts stays linear).

// Figure captions (docserver L1, Task 7; architecture section C, the "Caption" row; contract section 2.7).
// Every expected html string in the first block was produced by the reference renderer from the same input
// and is compared after normaliseForCompare (it only touches code blocks; figures and captions are compared
// exactly). The reference finds a caption with a regular expression over its finished HTML; this library
// decides on the token stream (figcaption.ts), and these cases pin that the two agree, quirks included.
// The later blocks pin this library's own behaviour where the reference has nothing to say, and the one
// place where it differs from the reference on purpose.
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { normaliseForCompare } from '../src/conformance/normalise.js';
import { checkOutputSafety } from '../src/conformance/oracle.js';
import { createEngine } from '../src/render/engine.js';
import { CAPTION, figcaption } from '../src/render/figcaption.js';
import { render } from '../src/render/index.js';

type Case = readonly [name: string, src: string, html: string];

function cases(list: readonly Case[]): void {
  for (const [name, src, html] of list) {
    it(name, () => {
      expect(normaliseForCompare(render(src).html)).toBe(html);
    });
  }
}

describe("figcaption: this library's own cases", () => {
  it('lineAttrs: false leaves the figure and its caption without data-line', () => {
    expect(render('```mermaid\nA\n```\n*Figure 1. a*\n', { lineAttrs: false }).html).toBe(
      '<figure class="mermaid-figure"><pre class="mermaid">A\n</pre><figcaption>Figure 1. a</figcaption></figure>\n',
    );
  });

  it('a caption changes neither meta.figures nor meta.mermaidKinds', () => {
    const { meta } = render('```mermaid\nflowchart\n```\n*Figure 1. a*\n\n```mermaid\npie\n```\n');
    expect({ figures: meta.figures, mermaidKinds: meta.mermaidKinds }).toEqual({
      figures: 2,
      mermaidKinds: ['flowchart', 'pie'],
    });
  });

  it('a caption is checked against the inline HTML as rendered, and is safe output', () => {
    expect(CAPTION.exec('<em>Figure 1. a</em> <em>b</em>')?.[1]).toBe('Figure 1. a</em> <em>b');
    expect(CAPTION.exec('<em>Figure 1. a</em> b')).toBeNull();
    const html = render('```mermaid\nA\n```\n*Figure 1. <img src=x onerror=y> [a](javascript:b)*\n').html;
    expect(html).toContain('<figcaption>Figure 1. &lt;img src=x onerror=y&gt; [a](javascript:b)</figcaption>');
    expect(checkOutputSafety(html)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('is a core rule of the engine', () => {
    const core = createEngine().core.ruler as unknown as { __rules__: { name: string; fn: unknown }[] };
    expect(core.__rules__.find((r) => r.name === 'figcaption')?.fn).toBe(figcaption);
  });
});

describe('figcaption: where this library differs from the reference', () => {
  // A tight list item's paragraph renders no <p>, so the reference's pattern, which ends at `</em></p>`,
  // looks further: past the end of the list item and the list, to the first paragraph that ends in an
  // emphasis. It then moves all of that into the figure's caption, which leaves the figure, the list and
  // that paragraph unbalanced. This library never looks past the block after the figure: the hidden
  // paragraph is not a caption, and the HTML stays balanced. No corpus case has this shape.
  const SRC = '- ```mermaid\n  A\n  ```\n  *Figure 1. x*\n\n*y*\n';
  const REFERENCE =
    '<ul data-line="1-5">\n<li data-line="1-5">\n' +
    '<figure class="mermaid-figure" data-line="1-3"><pre class="mermaid">A\n</pre><figcaption>Figure 1. x</em></li>\n' +
    '</ul>\n<p data-line="6-6"><em>y</figcaption></figure>\n';
  const THIS =
    '<ul data-line="1-5">\n<li data-line="1-5">\n' +
    '<figure class="mermaid-figure" data-line="1-3"><pre class="mermaid">A\n</pre></figure>\n' +
    '<em>Figure 1. x</em></li>\n</ul>\n<p data-line="6-6"><em>y</em></p>\n';

  it('a caption never reaches past the block after its figure', () => {
    const html = render(SRC).html;
    expect(html).toBe(THIS);
    expect(html).not.toBe(REFERENCE);
  });
});
```

// Two token-stream helpers for the core rules that stand in for the reference's HTML post-passes
// (docserver L1; architecture section C, the "Caption" and "Alerts" rows). The reference rewrote the
// rendered HTML with regular expressions; this library rewrites the token stream before it is rendered,
// so these helpers say what the reference's patterns saw between two blocks and how a rule drops tokens.
import type { Token } from 'markdown-it';
import { pyStrip } from './pyText.js';

/**
 * The index of the first token at or after `from` that renders more than whitespace. The reference's
 * patterns step over whitespace (Python's `\s*`) between one block's HTML and the next; the only block
 * token here that renders as whitespace alone is an html_block emptied by balance_details (a stray
 * `</details>`). A comment the allowlist drops leaves no token at all.
 */
export function skipBlank(tokens: readonly Token[], from: number): number {
  let k = from;
  while (isBlank(tokens[k])) k += 1;
  return k;
}

function isBlank(t: Token | undefined): boolean {
  return t !== undefined && t.type === 'html_block' && pyStrip(t.content) === '';
}

/** Removes the tokens at the given indexes in one pass, keeping the array and the order of the rest. */
export function removeTokens(tokens: Token[], drop: ReadonlySet<number>): void {
  if (drop.size === 0) return;
  let w = 0;
  for (const [r, t] of tokens.entries()) {
    if (drop.has(r)) continue;
    tokens[w] = t;
    w += 1;
  }
  tokens.length = w;
}
```

`src/render/figcaption.ts`:

```ts
// The figcaption core rule (docserver L1; architecture section C, the "Caption" row; contract section 2.7).
// The reference renderer finds a caption with a regular expression over its finished HTML: a Mermaid
// figure, whitespace, then a paragraph that is exactly `<em>Figure N. …</em>`. This rule makes the same
// decision on the token stream, before anything is rendered:
// - a fence that renders a Mermaid figure (fence.ts's own test: fenceName(info) === MERMAID);
// - its next block, stepping over blocks that render as whitespace (skipBlank), is a paragraph that is
//   not hidden: a tight list's paragraph renders no <p>, and the reference's pattern needs one;
// - the paragraph's inline content, rendered by this engine, is `<em>`, `Figure`, Python whitespace, a
//   decimal digit run (Python's \d: any Unicode decimal digit), `.`, anything, then `</em>` at its end.
// The caption is the rendered HTML between that first `<em>` and that last `</em>`, so its text is escaped
// exactly as the paragraph's would have been, and `*Figure 1. a* *b*` keeps the reference's unbalanced
// `Figure 1. a</em> <em>b`. The paragraph's three tokens are dropped (with its data-line), and renderFence
// writes `<figcaption>{caption}</figcaption>` before `</figure>`.
//
// The reference's pattern also forbids `</p>` inside the caption; rendered inline content never holds one
// (markdown-it escapes `<` in text, and the allowlist emits only br, sup, sub and kbd), so the paragraph's
// own close is the only `</p>` it could meet, and the `$` anchor below stands for it.
import type { StateCore } from 'markdown-it';
import { fenceName, MERMAID, type FenceMeta } from './fence.js';
import { PY_WS } from './pyText.js';
import { removeTokens, skipBlank } from './tokens.js';

/** A caption paragraph's rendered inline content; group 1 is the caption. */
export const CAPTION = new RegExp(`^<em>(Figure[${PY_WS}]+\\p{Nd}+\\.[\\s\\S]*?)</em>$`, 'u');

export function figcaption(state: StateCore): void {
  const tokens = state.tokens;
  const drop = new Set<number>();
  for (let i = 0; i < tokens.length; i += 1) {
    const fence = tokens[i];
    if (fence?.type !== 'fence' || fenceName(fence.info) !== MERMAID) continue;
    const k = skipBlank(tokens, i + 1);
    const open = tokens[k];
    const inline = tokens[k + 1];
    if (open?.type !== 'paragraph_open' || open.hidden || inline?.type !== 'inline') continue;
    const m = CAPTION.exec(state.md.renderer.renderInline(inline.children ?? [], state.md.options, state.env));
    if (m === null) continue;
    fence.meta = { caption: m[1] ?? '' } satisfies FenceMeta;
    drop.add(k).add(k + 1).add(k + 2);
    i = k + 2;
  }
  removeTokens(tokens, drop);
}
```

`src/render/alerts.ts`:

```ts
// The alerts core rule and its two render rules (docserver L1; architecture section C, the "Alerts" row;
// contract section 2.8). The reference renderer turns a blockquote into a GitHub alert with a regular
// expression over its finished HTML; this rule makes the same decision on the token stream:
// - a blockquote whose first block (stepping over blocks that render as whitespace, skipBlank) is a
//   paragraph whose inline content starts with the text `[!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]`
//   or `[!CAUTION]`, upper case only. (A blockquote's paragraph is never hidden: markdown-it hides only a
//   tight list item's own paragraphs.) The text is read after text_join, so `\[!NOTE]` and `&#91;!NOTE]`
//   count, as they render the same characters; a link `[!NOTE](x)` does not, as it renders `<a`.
// - The marker is removed, then spaces and tabs, then one line break: a `\n` in the text itself, or else
//   a softbreak or hardbreak token right after the text (the reference's `(?:\n|<br\s*/?>\n?)?`).
// - The blockquote becomes alert_open/alert_close, rendered
//     <div class="gh-alert gh-{kind}"{ data-line}><p class="gh-alert-title">{Kind}</p>…</div>\n
//   with the blockquote's data-line on the div. The first paragraph loses its data-line (the reference
//   rebuilt it as a bare <p>); a paragraph left empty is dropped, and the line feed its `</p>\n` left in
//   the reference's output is written after the title instead.
// - No alert is made inside an alert: the reference skips a match that starts inside a replacement, so
//   the rule resumes after the alert's closing token. An alert inside a plain blockquote is still made.
import type { StateCore, Token } from 'markdown-it';
import type { RenderEnv } from './env.js';
import { lineAttr, type LineMeta } from './lineAttrs.js';
import { pyLower } from './pyText.js';
import { removeTokens, skipBlank } from './tokens.js';

/** The five alert kinds, upper case as they are written, each with its title (Python's `kind.capitalize()`). */
export const ALERT_TITLES: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = Object.freeze({
  NOTE: 'Note',
  TIP: 'Tip',
  IMPORTANT: 'Important',
  WARNING: 'Warning',
  CAUTION: 'Caution',
});

/** The marker at the start of the first paragraph's text, and the spaces and tabs after it. */
export const MARKER = new RegExp(`^\\[!(${Object.keys(ALERT_TITLES).join('|')})\\][ \\t]*`);

/** What the alerts rule records on an alert_open token. */
export interface AlertMeta {
  /** The kind, lower case (the class gh-{kind}). */
  readonly kind: string;
  /** The title shown in the alert. */
  readonly title: string;
  /** True when the first paragraph held only the marker and was dropped. */
  readonly bare: boolean;
}

const BREAKS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['softbreak', 'hardbreak']);

/**
 * The index of the blockquote_close that closes the blockquote_open at `open` (the first one after it at
 * the same nesting level), or -1. markdown-it always closes what it opens, so -1 never comes back from a
 * parsed stream; the rule treats it as "no alert" all the same.
 */
function closeOf(tokens: readonly Token[], open: number): number {
  const level = tokens[open]?.level;
  for (let j = open + 1; j < tokens.length; j += 1) {
    const t = tokens[j];
    if (t?.type === 'blockquote_close' && t.level === level) return j;
  }
  return -1;
}

export function alerts(state: StateCore): void {
  const tokens = state.tokens;
  const drop = new Set<number>();
  for (let i = 0; i < tokens.length; i += 1) {
    const open = tokens[i];
    if (open?.type !== 'blockquote_open') continue;
    const k = skipBlank(tokens, i + 1);
    const para = tokens[k];
    const inline = tokens[k + 1];
    if (para?.type !== 'paragraph_open' || inline?.type !== 'inline') continue;
    const children = inline.children ?? [];
    const text = children[0];
    if (text?.type !== 'text') continue;
    const m = MARKER.exec(text.content);
    if (m === null) continue;
    const close = closeOf(tokens, i);
    const end = tokens[close];
    if (end === undefined) continue;
    let rest = text.content.slice(m[0].length);
    if (rest.startsWith('\n')) rest = rest.slice(1);
    else if (rest === '' && BREAKS.has(children[1]?.type ?? '')) children.splice(1, 1);
    text.content = rest;
    if (rest === '') children.splice(0, 1);
    const bare = children.length === 0;
    if (bare) drop.add(k).add(k + 1).add(k + 2);
    else para.meta = { noLine: true } satisfies LineMeta;
    const kind = m[1] ?? '';
    open.type = 'alert_open';
    open.tag = 'div';
    open.meta = { kind: pyLower(kind), title: ALERT_TITLES[kind] ?? '', bare } satisfies AlertMeta;
    end.type = 'alert_close';
    end.tag = 'div';
    i = close;
  }
  removeTokens(tokens, drop);
}

/** The alert_open render rule. */
export function renderAlertOpen(tokens: Token[], idx: number, _options: unknown, env: RenderEnv): string {
  const token = tokens[idx];
  if (token === undefined) return '';
  const meta = token.meta as AlertMeta;
  const title = `<p class="gh-alert-title">${meta.title}</p>`;
  return `<div class="gh-alert gh-${meta.kind}"${lineAttr(token, env)}>${title}${meta.bare ? '\n' : ''}`;
}

/** The alert_close render rule. */
export function renderAlertClose(): string {
  return '</div>\n';
}
