```ts
// The fence render rule (docserver L1; architecture section C, the "Fence info" and "Meta" rows; contract
// sections 2.5 and 2.6). A fence's name is the first word of its info string as the reference reads it:
// stripped the Python way, then split on a space only (a tab does not separate), never entity-decoded.
// - Exactly `mermaid` (case-sensitive) makes a figure. Its source is the raw fence content, escaped with
//   Python's html.escape (pyEscape: `'` becomes &#x27;), not stripped:
//     <figure class="mermaid-figure"{ data-line}><pre class="mermaid">{source}</pre></figure>\n
//   The figure is counted for meta.figures and its diagram keyword recorded for meta.mermaidKinds.
// - Anything else is code:
//     <div class="codehilite"{ data-line}><pre><code class="hljs{ language-NAME}">{code}</code></pre></div>\n
//   NAME is a canonical name from the registry (highlight.ts), never the author's text. The code is the
//   text the reference's highlighter (Pygments) shows: one leading U+FEFF removed, leading and trailing
//   line feeds removed, one line feed added. A registered language is highlighted by highlight.js; any
//   other name gets the text escaped as markdown-it escapes text.
// - Highlighting is bounded, not only the input: several registered grammars (ini, java, javascript and
//   typescript among them) take time quadratic in a line's length, so a 30000-character line took 5-10 s.
//   A fence with a line longer than MAX_HIGHLIGHT_LINE code units, or one that would take the document past
//   MAX_HIGHLIGHT_CHARS highlighted code units, keeps its language class and gets the escaped text, as an
//   unregistered name does. The corpus compares the text inside the wrapper (PD1), so no golden depends
//   on which fences were highlighted.
// A figure's caption is found by the figcaption core rule (figcaption.ts), which records it on the fence
// token's meta (FenceMeta); this rule writes it as <figcaption>…</figcaption> right before </figure>.
// scanRefs (Task 10) reads fenceName, MERMAID and mermaidKind.
import type { Token } from 'markdown-it';
import type { RenderEnv } from './env.js';
import { escapeHtml, pyEscape } from './escape.js';
import { highlightCode, resolveLanguage } from './highlight.js';
import { lineAttr } from './lineAttrs.js';
import { pyStrip } from './pyText.js';

/** The fence name that makes a Mermaid figure. */
export const MERMAID = 'mermaid';

/** What the figcaption rule records on a Mermaid fence token: its caption, as rendered HTML. */
export interface FenceMeta {
  readonly caption: string;
}

/** At most this many distinct diagram keywords in meta.mermaidKinds. */
export const MAX_MERMAID_KINDS = 32;

/** A fence is highlighted only when none of its lines is longer than this, in code units. */
export const MAX_HIGHLIGHT_LINE = 256;

/** At most this many code units of one document are highlighted; a fence that would pass it is escaped text. */
export const MAX_HIGHLIGHT_CHARS = 262_144;

/** A diagram keyword: an ASCII letter, then up to 39 ASCII letters, digits, `_` or `-`, at a line's start. */
const KIND = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,39}/;

const BOM = 0xfeff;
const LF = 0x0a;

/** The first word of a fence's info string: Python's `info.strip().split(" ")[0]`. */
export function fenceName(info: string): string {
  return pyStrip(info).split(' ')[0] ?? '';
}

/**
 * The code text of a fence, as the reference's highlighter reads it (Pygments' lexer preprocessing): one
 * leading U+FEFF removed, then every leading and trailing line feed, then one line feed added.
 */
export function codeText(content: string): string {
  let start = content.charCodeAt(0) === BOM ? 1 : 0;
  let end = content.length;
  while (start < end && content.charCodeAt(start) === LF) start += 1;
  while (end > start && content.charCodeAt(end - 1) === LF) end -= 1;
  return `${content.substring(start, end)}\n`;
}

/**
 * The diagram keyword of a Mermaid source, or null. Lines are read stripped the Python way: blank lines and
 * `%%` lines are skipped; then a `---` line opens a block skipped through the next `---` (no closing line:
 * null); then blank and `%%` lines again; the keyword is the KIND at the start of the next line.
 */
export function mermaidKind(source: string): string | null {
  const lines = source.split('\n').map(pyStrip);
  const skip = (from: number): number => {
    let i = from;
    while (i < lines.length && (lines[i] === '' || (lines[i] ?? '').startsWith('%%'))) i += 1;
    return i;
  };
  let i = skip(0);
  if (lines[i] === '---') {
    i += 1;
    while (i < lines.length && lines[i] !== '---') i += 1;
    if (i >= lines.length) return null;
    i = skip(i + 1);
  }
  const line = lines[i];
  return line === undefined ? null : (KIND.exec(line)?.[0] ?? null);
}

/** Whether no line of `text` is longer than MAX_HIGHLIGHT_LINE code units. */
function shortLines(text: string): boolean {
  for (let from = 0; from < text.length; ) {
    const end = text.indexOf('\n', from);
    const stop = end === -1 ? text.length : end;
    if (stop - from > MAX_HIGHLIGHT_LINE) return false;
    from = stop + 1;
  }
  return true;
}

/** Count one rendered figure and record its keyword: distinct, in document order, at most MAX_MERMAID_KINDS. */
function recordFigure(env: RenderEnv, source: string): void {
  env.figures += 1;
  const kind = mermaidKind(source);
  if (kind !== null && !env.mermaidKinds.includes(kind) && env.mermaidKinds.length < MAX_MERMAID_KINDS) {
    env.mermaidKinds.push(kind);
  }
}

/** The fence render rule (markdown-it's `renderer.rules.fence`). */
export function renderFence(tokens: Token[], idx: number, _options: unknown, env: RenderEnv): string {
  const token = tokens[idx];
  if (token === undefined) return '';
  const name = fenceName(token.info);
  const dl = lineAttr(token, env);
  if (name === MERMAID) {
    recordFigure(env, token.content);
    const caption = (token.meta as FenceMeta | null)?.caption;
    const cap = caption === undefined ? '' : `<figcaption>${caption}</figcaption>`;
    return `<figure class="mermaid-figure"${dl}><pre class="mermaid">${pyEscape(token.content)}</pre>${cap}</figure>\n`;
  }
  const text = codeText(token.content);
  const language = resolveLanguage(name);
  const highlight = language !== null && env.highlighted + text.length <= MAX_HIGHLIGHT_CHARS && shortLines(text);
  if (highlight) env.highlighted += text.length;
  const code = highlight ? highlightCode(text, language) : escapeHtml(text);
  const cls = language === null ? 'hljs' : `hljs language-${language}`;
  return `<div class="codehilite"${dl}><pre><code class="${cls}">${code}</code></pre></div>\n`;
}
```

`src/render/lineAttrs.ts`:

```ts
// The line_attrs core rule (docserver L1; architecture section C, the `data-line` row; contract section
// 2.4). Each block token of the types below that has a source map gets data-line="{first}-{last}", 1-based
// and inclusive, set with attrSet so it comes after any attribute an earlier rule set (a heading's id, a
// list's start, a task item's class). It runs last in the core chain; a rule that must come before it is
// inserted with `md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', …)`. Fences, Mermaid figures, alerts and front matter
// carry data-line through their own render rules, not through this one: those rules write lineAttr(token,
// env). A token whose meta says `noLine` gets none either way: the alerts rule marks the paragraph it
// rebuilds, which the reference rendered as a bare <p>.
import type { StateCore, Token } from 'markdown-it';
import type { RenderEnv } from './env.js';

/** The token types the reference renderer marks, exactly (its _LINE_TOKENS). */
export const LINE_TOKENS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  'paragraph_open',
  'heading_open',
  'list_item_open',
  'tr_open',
  'blockquote_open',
  'table_open',
  'hr',
  'code_block',
  'bullet_list_open',
  'ordered_list_open',
]);

/** What a rule records on a token's meta to keep data-line off it (alerts.ts). */
export interface LineMeta {
  readonly noLine?: boolean;
}

/** True when the token has a source map and no rule has marked it `noLine`. */
function lined(t: Token): t is Token & { map: [number, number] } {
  return t.map !== null && (t.meta as LineMeta | null)?.noLine !== true;
}

/** The data-line value of a source map: its first and last line, 1-based and inclusive. */
function lineValue(map: [number, number]): string {
  return `${map[0] + 1}-${map[1]}`;
}

export function lineAttrs(state: StateCore): void {
  const env = state.env as RenderEnv;
  if (!env.lineAttrs) return;
  for (const t of state.tokens) {
    if (LINE_TOKENS.has(t.type) && lined(t)) t.attrSet('data-line', lineValue(t.map));
  }
}

/**
 * The data-line attribute a render rule writes into its own markup (fence.ts; front matter in Task 9):
 * ` data-line="{first}-{last}"`, or '' when the env has lineAttrs off, the token has no source map or its
 * meta says `noLine`.
 */
export function lineAttr(token: Token, env: RenderEnv): string {
  return env.lineAttrs && lined(token) ? ` data-line="${lineValue(token.map)}"` : '';
}
```

`src/render/engine.ts`:

```ts
// The markdown-it instance behind render() (docserver L1; architecture section C, "Engine"; contract
// section 1). The CommonMark preset with raw HTML off, plus tables and strikethrough, configured once.
// The instance carries no per-document state: everything one render needs lives in its RenderEnv (env.ts).
//
// Pinned on purpose:
// - `html: false` is the raw-HTML wall: markdown-it escapes every tag, and only this library's own rules
//   (the allowlist, allowlist.ts) ever emit markup.
// - `maxNesting` stays the preset's 20, as in the reference: deeper blockquotes and lists stop nesting.
// - `validateLink` and `normalizeLink` are markdown-it's own: javascript:, vbscript:, file: and non-image
//   data: links stay text, and destinations are percent-encoded. Never override them.
//
// markdown-it is 14.3.2, not 15: 15 puts a code span's text into an image's alt (`![a `c`](x)` gives
// alt="a c"), where markdown-it-py, a port of 14, gives alt="a " (decision gate D1, measured on the corpus).
//
// The core chain ends with line_attrs; later rules go `before('line_attrs', …)` so data-line stays last.
// block_strip goes right after block, before inline parsing reads the text it strips (blockStrip.ts).
// The allowlist's rules go right before markdown-it's own raw-HTML rules, which html: false disables:
// safe_block_html with alt paragraph, reference and blockquote (it interrupts those, as in the reference,
// and is not a list terminator), safe_inline_html in the inline chain. balance_details runs after anchors.
// Fences render through this library's own rule (fence.ts), not markdown-it's: a Mermaid figure or a
// highlighted code block, with options.highlight left unset.
// alerts and figcaption follow balance_details. They stand in for the reference's HTML post-passes (its
// caption pass ran first, then its alert pass; the two never touch the same tokens, so their order here
// changes nothing). alerts turns blockquotes into alert_open/alert_close, which render through this
// library's own two rules; figcaption records a caption on its fence token, which renderFence writes.
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it';
import { alerts, renderAlertClose, renderAlertOpen } from './alerts.js';
import { safeBlockHtml, safeInlineHtml } from './allowlist.js';
import { blockStrip } from './blockStrip.js';
import { balanceDetails } from './details.js';
import { renderFence } from './fence.js';
import { figcaption } from './figcaption.js';
import { lineAttrs } from './lineAttrs.js';
import { anchors } from './slug.js';

export function createEngine(): MarkdownIt {
  const md = new MarkdownIt('commonmark', {
    html: false,
    xhtmlOut: true,
    breaks: false,
    linkify: false,
    typographer: false,
  });
  md.enable(['table', 'strikethrough']);
  md.core.ruler.push('line_attrs', lineAttrs);
  md.core.ruler.after('block', 'block_strip', blockStrip);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'anchors', anchors);
  md.block.ruler.before('html_block', 'safe_block_html', safeBlockHtml, {
    alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote'],
  });
  md.inline.ruler.before('html_inline', 'safe_inline_html', safeInlineHtml);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'balance_details', balanceDetails);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'alerts', alerts);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'figcaption', figcaption);
  md.renderer.rules.fence = renderFence;
  md.renderer.rules.alert_open = renderAlertOpen;
  md.renderer.rules.alert_close = renderAlertClose;
  return md;
}
```

**Decisions this task makes:**
1. **The table rule is ported with Python's strip, not hooked; no PD6 is needed (ruling C10).** A strip hook on cell text, run after markdown-it's table rule, cannot recover the reference's output, because markdown-it trims whole lines with JavaScript's `trim()` before it decides anything. Measured on the reference: a U+0085 before a header line's first pipe still makes a table there and makes a paragraph in markdown-it (the trimmed line keeps U+0085 as an extra first column); a U+FEFF there makes a paragraph in the reference and a table in markdown-it; a line holding only U+0085 ends the reference's table and adds an empty row in markdown-it; a cell-edge U+FEFF is kept by the reference and gone before any later rule sees it here. `pyTable` is markdown-it 14.3.2's own rule, step for step, with each of its five `trim()` calls (header line, body lines, header cells, body cells, delimiter columns) made `pyStrip`. It is set with `md.block.ruler.at('table', pyTable, { alt: ['paragraph', 'reference'] })`, so its name, place and alternatives are markdown-it's. `tables.ts` therefore holds a block rule that section B does not list for it.
2. **`table_code` and the wrapper are token rules equal to the reference's two HTML passes.** The reference replaces `\|` in every `<code>…</code>` between `<table…>` and `</table>`; inside a table only a cell's code span can render `<code>` (a note's content renders after the table, never inside it), so the rule rewrites the `code_inline` children of the `inline` tokens between `table_open` and `table_close`. The wrapper rules wrap markdown-it's own `renderToken` output, so the line feed markdown-it writes before a block that follows a hidden token (a tight list item's paragraph) stays before the `<div>`, where the reference's `<table` substitution left it.
3. **`meta.tables` is counted by the `table_open` render rule** into `RenderEnv.tables`, as `renderFence` counts figures. It equals the reference's count of `<div class="table-wrapper">`.
4. **Task lists: the reference's plugin, ported with its quirks; one change in cost only.** The marker is followed by GFM whitespace (the plugin's own class: space, tab, `\n`, `\v`, `\f`, `\r`), not by Python whitespace as section C's row says: `[ ]` then U+00A0 or U+3000 is no task in the reference. The checkbox is chosen by `[ ] `, `[x] ` or `[X] ` with a space; with any other whitespace after the marker the reference writes an empty string, and the item is still a task item with no checkbox. The list that gets `contains-task-list` is the nearest token one level above the item; the reference searched backwards from each item, which made 20000 items take 19.3 s here, so the rule keeps the last index seen at each level in one pass (the same token, 0.5 s). The marker is dropped with `cpSlice` (Python's `[3:]`, global constraint 6); its first three characters are always ASCII, so no mutation of that slice can be observed, and it has no row.
5. **Where `task_lists` runs.** Before `text_join` and after `footnote_tail`, as the reference's does, so a task item inside a note is made like any other. Moving it after `text_join` changes no output: the marker is literal text at the start of the item's first inline token, and `text_join` only merges escape and entity tokens into their neighbours, none of which can stand in a matching marker. So section F's M8.6 reds only through the engine's order pin (row M6); it is reported there, not dropped.
6. **Footnotes: markdown-it-footnote 4.0.0 as it ships** (section H risk 8, measured): it declares no peer dependency and no types, so it runs with markdown-it 14.3.2 and is typed by the local declaration; its `xhtmlOut` branch gives `<hr class="footnotes-sep" />` and its anchor names have no prefix (this library never sets `env.docId`). Its output equals the reference plugin's on every case below and in the differential run (item 4 of the measurements).
7. **A fix in Task 7's `figcaption` that footnotes make necessary.** `footnote_tail` puts a note's back-references between its last paragraph's inline token and its `paragraph_close`. The caption rule dropped the three tokens after a Mermaid fence's paragraph_open and left that `</p>` behind, unbalanced, where the reference makes no caption (its pattern needs `</em></p>`). The rule now also requires `paragraph_close` right after the inline token. This is the "footnote input that waits for Task 8" of Task 7's measurements.
8. **Three test files.** Each holds a block of cases whose expected HTML is the reference's own output for the same input (pasted, compared after normaliseForCompare, which touches code blocks only), then this library's own parts (`lineAttrs: false`, registrations, the fixed strings, the 65536-cell limit, linear cost, output safety).
9. **`lists-tasks` renders `ordered_start` and `tasklist_nested` (ruling C14).** Its `nest_list` probe nests 24 lists, and markdown-it's nesting limit (20) stops it and, in markdown-it and in the reference's port alike, ends the whole document. Task 2 therefore puts `nest_list` last in that input, so `ordered_start` (`<ol start="7">`) and `tasklist_nested` (two `contains-task-list` lists and an ordered task list) are in the reference and in the expected file, and section F's M8.5 reds through `lists-tasks` as section F says (row M5). `tasklists.test.ts` covers both shapes against the reference as well.
10. **The pending hand-over, measured.** The eight cases earlier tasks labelled `T8` pass after this task and leave the list: `heading-ids-edge` (its footnote heading), `comment-anchors`, `h-attr-smuggle` and `doc-shapes/byline-status` (each holds a table), `tables`, `lists-tasks`, `doc-shapes/plan` and `footnotes`. No other case starts passing. 35 of the 51 cases now pass; 16 are pending (15 for Task 9, `spec-template` for Task 10). Section F's generated cases for this task (`x-tables/*`, `x-collisions/footnote-refs-10000`) do not exist before Task 11; their shapes were measured (item 5 below), and the 65536-cell limit and 10000 references to one note are pinned as unit cases.
11. **Where section F's named reds cannot happen.** M8.2 names `code-indented-breaks` (`code_inline_pipe`), but that probe is `` `a < b & c` `` and holds no pipe; row M2 reds through `tables` (its `` `not in table a\|b` `` paragraph) and two table cases. M8.6 is decision 5.
12. **One limit markdown-it keeps per table holds for the whole document too.** markdown-it ends a table once short rows have added 65536 empty cells to it (`MAX_AUTOCOMPLETED_CELLS`; the reference's port has the same limit), but the count starts again in each table. A 1807-byte table of 128 columns and 517 one-cell rows adds 65536 cells, about 2.4 MB of html (1300 times its input), so 16 such tables (29 KB) rendered 38 MB in 4.7 s with 1.08 GB of heap, and 64 of them (115 KB, far under the 4 MiB input cap) ended in a fatal out-of-memory error: a crash `render()` cannot catch, so it never reached its fallback. `pyTable` also counts the empty cells it adds in `env.emptyCells` and ends a table, exactly as at its own limit, once the document's count would pass 65536. One table alone behaves as before unless its long rows had cancelled short ones out (markdown-it's per-table count goes down on a long row; the document's does not), so no corpus case and no golden moves. Measured: those 64 tables now render 2.8 MB in 0.5 s, and 256 of them 3.9 MB in 0.6 s. `tables.test.ts` pins it with two 2000-column tables (row M28), and Task 11 adds the generated case `x-tables/many-ragged`. This differs from the reference only for a document whose tables add more than 65536 empty cells in all: it is **departure PD8** (ruling C19, bounds that only hostile documents reach, with Task 3's html bound and Task 5's nesting cap).

**Measured while planning** (Node v24.14.1, npm 11.11.0; the reference renderer run as `"$REFERENCE_PYTHON"` on `"$REFERENCE_RENDERER"` for every expected string the three test files hold):

```ts
// Tables (docserver L1, Task 8; architecture section C, the "Tables" row; contract section 2.9).
// Every expected html string in the first block was produced by the reference renderer from the same input
// and is compared after normaliseForCompare (it only touches code blocks). The reference parses tables with
// a Python port of markdown-it's table rule, which strips the Python way, then rewrites its finished HTML
// twice: `\|` in a table's code spans, and the wrapper around every table. This library ports the rule
// with Python's strip and makes both rewrites on the token stream (tables.ts); these cases pin that the
// two agree. The later block pins this library's own parts.
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { normaliseForCompare } from '../src/conformance/normalise.js';
import { checkOutputSafety } from '../src/conformance/oracle.js';
import { createEngine } from '../src/render/engine.js';
import { render } from '../src/render/index.js';
import { pyTable, renderTableClose, renderTableOpen, tableCode } from '../src/render/tables.js';

type Case = readonly [name: string, src: string, html: string];

function cases(list: readonly Case[]): void {
  for (const [name, src, html] of list) {
    it(name, () => {
      expect(normaliseForCompare(render(src).html)).toBe(html);
    });
  }
}

interface RuleEntry {
  name: string;
  fn: unknown;
  alt: string[];
}

/** markdown-it's internal rule list (Ruler.__rules__), which its published types do not declare. */
function rules(ruler: unknown): RuleEntry[] {
  return (ruler as { __rules__: RuleEntry[] }).__rules__;
}

describe("tables: this library's own parts", () => {
  it('meta.tables counts every table; lineAttrs: false leaves the wrapper and drops every data-line', () => {
    const src = '| a |\n|---|\n| b |\n\n> | c |\n> |---|\n\n- | d |\n  |---|\n';
    expect(render(src).meta.tables).toBe(3);
    expect(render('| a |\n|---|\n| b |\n', { lineAttrs: false }).html).toBe(
      '<div class="table-wrapper"><table>\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>a</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n' +
        '<td>b</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table></div>\n',
    );
    expect(render('no table | here\n').meta.tables).toBe(0);
  });

  it('short rows add at most 65536 empty cells to one table; the rows after that are a paragraph', () => {
    const src = `|${' h |'.repeat(2000)}\n|${'-|'.repeat(2000)}\n${'| b |\n'.repeat(40)}`;
    const html = render(src).html;
    expect(html.match(/<tr /g)).toHaveLength(33);
    expect(html.match(/<td>/g)).toHaveLength(64000);
    expect(html.endsWith(`</table></div>\n<p data-line="35-42">${'| b |\n'.repeat(7)}| b |</p>\n`)).toBe(true);
    expect(checkOutputSafety(html)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('the 65536-cell limit holds for the whole document too: a later table adds no empty cell past it', () => {
    // markdown-it counts per table only, so many small tables could each add 65536 empty cells.
    const table = `|${' h |'.repeat(2000)}\n|${'-|'.repeat(2000)}\n${'| b |\n'.repeat(32)}`;
    const html = render(`${table}\n${table}`).html;
    expect(html.match(/<table[ >]/g)).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(html.match(/<td>/g)).toHaveLength(64000);
    expect(html.endsWith(`</table></div>\n<p data-line="38-69">${'| b |\n'.repeat(31)}| b |</p>\n`)).toBe(true);
    expect(checkOutputSafety(html)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("the table rule is this library's port, in markdown-it's place and with its alternatives", () => {
    const md = createEngine();
    const table = rules(md.block.ruler).find((r) => r.name === 'table');
    expect(table?.fn).toBe(pyTable);
    expect(table?.alt).toEqual(['paragraph', 'reference']);
  });

  it("table_code and the two wrapper rules are the engine's", () => {
    const md = createEngine();
    expect(rules(md.core.ruler).find((r) => r.name === 'table_code')?.fn).toBe(tableCode);
    expect(md.renderer.rules.table_open).toBe(renderTableOpen);
    expect(md.renderer.rules.table_close).toBe(renderTableClose);
  });
});
```

```ts
// markdown-it-footnote 4.0.0 ships no type declarations. This is the one shape this library uses: the
// default export is a markdown-it plugin taking no options. A local declaration, not @types/markdown-it-
// footnote, so the footnote plugin's types never pull in a second copy of markdown-it's.
declare module 'markdown-it-footnote' {
  import type { PluginSimple } from 'markdown-it';

  const footnote: PluginSimple;
  export default footnote;
}
```

`src/render/tables.ts`:

```ts
// Tables (docserver L1; architecture section C, the "Tables" row; contract section 2.9). Three parts:
// - pyTable, the GFM table block rule. It is markdown-it 14.3.2's own rule with each of its five `trim()`
//   calls made Python's `str.strip()` (pyStrip), because the reference's parser, a Python port of the same
//   rule, strips there: the header line and each body line, every cell's text, and the delimiter row's
//   columns (which can only hold `|`, `-`, `:`, spaces and tabs, so there the two agree). JavaScript's
//   trim() and Python's strip() differ on U+FEFF (JS strips it, Python keeps it) and on \x1c-\x1f and \x85
//   (the reverse). A stripped line edge decides whether an outer pipe makes an empty first or last column,
//   so whether the header matches the delimiter row and the table exists at all, and whether a line of such
//   whitespace ends the table; a stripped cell edge is the cell's text. Everything else is the rule as
//   markdown-it ships it, so it keeps the name `table` and its place in the block chain, with one addition:
//   the limit on the empty cells added to short rows holds for the whole document as well as for each
//   table. markdown-it counts them per table only, so many small tables could each add 65536 cells, about
//   1300 bytes of html per byte of input, and exhaust the heap (an out-of-memory error is fatal, so render()
//   could not even fall back). The document's count is env.emptyCells; past the limit a table ends exactly
//   as it ends at its own limit.
// - tableCode, a core rule: inside a table, a code span's `\|` becomes `|`. The reference does this on
//   its finished HTML, for every <code>…</code> between <table…> and </table>; the only <code> a table can
//   hold is a code span in a cell, so this rule changes those code spans and nothing else. The table rule
//   already turns `\|` into `|` when it splits a row, so this only shows on `\\|` (`a\\|b` renders a|b).
// - renderTableOpen and renderTableClose: every table is wrapped in <div class="table-wrapper">…</div>,
//   as the reference wraps every <table…> and </table> of its HTML, and counted for meta.tables.
import type { Options, Renderer, StateBlock, StateCore, Token } from 'markdown-it';
import type { RenderEnv } from './env.js';
import { pyStrip } from './pyText.js';

/**
 * Empty cells one table may add to short rows before it ends (markdown-it's MAX_AUTOCOMPLETED_CELLS), and
 * the empty cells all the tables of one document may add.
 */
const MAX_AUTOCOMPLETED_CELLS = 0x10000;

const PIPE = 0x7c;
const DASH = 0x2d;
const COLON = 0x3a;
const BACKSLASH = 0x5c;
const ALIGN = /^:?-+:?$/;

/** markdown-it's isSpace: a space or a tab, nothing else. */
function isSpace(code: number): boolean {
  return code === 0x09 || code === 0x20;
}

function getLine(state: StateBlock, line: number): string {
  const pos = (state.bMarks[line] ?? 0) + (state.tShift[line] ?? 0);
  return state.src.slice(pos, state.eMarks[line]);
}

/** A row split on unescaped pipes; an escaped pipe `\|` becomes `|` in its cell (markdown-it's escapedSplit). */
function escapedSplit(str: string): string[] {
  const result: string[] = [];
  const max = str.length;
  let pos = 0;
  let ch = str.charCodeAt(pos);
  let isEscaped = false;
  let lastPos = 0;
  let current = '';
  while (pos < max) {
    if (ch === PIPE) {
      if (!isEscaped) {
        result.push(current + str.substring(lastPos, pos));
        current = '';
        lastPos = pos + 1;
      } else {
        current += str.substring(lastPos, pos - 1);
        lastPos = pos;
      }
    }
    isEscaped = ch === BACKSLASH;
    pos += 1;
    ch = str.charCodeAt(pos);
  }
  result.push(current + str.substring(lastPos));
  return result;
}

/** A row's cells: the line split, then one empty cell dropped from each end (the outer pipes). */
function rowCells(line: string): string[] {
  const columns = escapedSplit(line);
  if (columns.length > 0 && columns[0] === '') columns.shift();
  if (columns.length > 0 && columns[columns.length - 1] === '') columns.pop();
  return columns;
}

/** The delimiter row's alignments, or null when the line is not a delimiter row. */
function alignments(state: StateBlock, line: number): string[] | null {
  let pos = (state.bMarks[line] ?? 0) + (state.tShift[line] ?? 0);
  const max = state.eMarks[line] ?? 0;
  if (pos >= max) return null;
  const firstCh = state.src.charCodeAt(pos);
  pos += 1;
  if (firstCh !== PIPE && firstCh !== DASH && firstCh !== COLON) return null;
  if (pos >= max) return null;
  const secondCh = state.src.charCodeAt(pos);
  pos += 1;
  if (secondCh !== PIPE && secondCh !== DASH && secondCh !== COLON && !isSpace(secondCh)) return null;
  // A first `-` followed by a space would be a list item.
  if (firstCh === DASH && isSpace(secondCh)) return null;
  while (pos < max) {
    const ch = state.src.charCodeAt(pos);
    if (ch !== PIPE && ch !== DASH && ch !== COLON && !isSpace(ch)) return null;
    pos += 1;
  }
  const columns = getLine(state, line).split('|');
  const aligns: string[] = [];
  for (const [i, column] of columns.entries()) {
    const t = pyStrip(column);
    if (t === '') {
      // An empty column is allowed before and after the table, never between two columns.
      if (i === 0 || i === columns.length - 1) continue;
      return null;
    }
    if (!ALIGN.test(t)) return null;
    if (t.charCodeAt(t.length - 1) === COLON) aligns.push(t.charCodeAt(0) === COLON ? 'center' : 'right');
    else if (t.charCodeAt(0) === COLON) aligns.push('left');
    else aligns.push('');
  }
  return aligns;
}

function pushCell(state: StateBlock, tag: 'th' | 'td', align: string | undefined, content: string): void {
  const open = state.push(`${tag}_open`, tag, 1);
  if (align !== undefined && align !== '') open.attrs = [['style', `text-align:${align}`]];
  const inline = state.push('inline', '', 0);
  inline.content = content;
  inline.children = [];
  state.push(`${tag}_close`, tag, -1);
}

/** The table block rule: markdown-it's, with Python's strip wherever markdown-it trims. */
export function pyTable(state: StateBlock, startLine: number, endLine: number, silent: boolean): boolean {
  if (startLine + 2 > endLine) return false;
  let nextLine = startLine + 1;
  if ((state.sCount[nextLine] ?? 0) < state.blkIndent) return false;
  // Indented four or more: a code block.
  if ((state.sCount[nextLine] ?? 0) - state.blkIndent >= 4) return false;
  const aligns = alignments(state, nextLine);
  if (aligns === null) return false;

  const headerLine = pyStrip(getLine(state, startLine));
  if (!headerLine.includes('|')) return false;
  if ((state.sCount[startLine] ?? 0) - state.blkIndent >= 4) return false;
  const header = rowCells(headerLine);
  const columnCount = header.length;
  if (columnCount === 0 || columnCount !== aligns.length) return false;
  if (silent) return true;

  const oldParentType = state.parentType;
  state.parentType = 'table' as StateBlock['parentType'];
  // A table ends where a blockquote would be ended.
  const terminatorRules = state.md.block.ruler.getRules('blockquote');

  const tableOpen = state.push('table_open', 'table', 1);
  const tableLines: [number, number] = [startLine, 0];
  tableOpen.map = tableLines;
  state.push('thead_open', 'thead', 1).map = [startLine, startLine + 1];
  state.push('tr_open', 'tr', 1).map = [startLine, startLine + 1];
  for (const [i, cell] of header.entries()) pushCell(state, 'th', aligns[i], pyStrip(cell));
  state.push('tr_close', 'tr', -1);
  state.push('thead_close', 'thead', -1);

  let tbodyLines: [number, number] | undefined;
  let autocompletedCells = 0;
  const env = state.env as RenderEnv;
  for (nextLine = startLine + 2; nextLine < endLine; nextLine += 1) {
    if ((state.sCount[nextLine] ?? 0) < state.blkIndent) break;
    if (terminatorRules.some((rule) => rule(state, nextLine, endLine, true))) break;
    const lineText = pyStrip(getLine(state, nextLine));
    if (lineText === '') break;
    if ((state.sCount[nextLine] ?? 0) - state.blkIndent >= 4) break;
    const columns = rowCells(lineText);
    // Can go negative when a row is longer than the header; that does not matter for the limit.
    autocompletedCells += columnCount - columns.length;
    if (autocompletedCells > MAX_AUTOCOMPLETED_CELLS) break;
    // The document's empty cells, counted only where a row is short.
    const added = Math.max(0, columnCount - columns.length);
    if (env.emptyCells + added > MAX_AUTOCOMPLETED_CELLS) break;
    env.emptyCells += added;
    if (nextLine === startLine + 2) {
      tbodyLines = [startLine + 2, 0];
      state.push('tbody_open', 'tbody', 1).map = tbodyLines;
    }
    state.push('tr_open', 'tr', 1).map = [nextLine, nextLine + 1];
    for (let i = 0; i < columnCount; i += 1) {
      const cell = columns[i];
      pushCell(state, 'td', aligns[i], cell === undefined || cell === '' ? '' : pyStrip(cell));
    }
    state.push('tr_close', 'tr', -1);
  }
  if (tbodyLines !== undefined) {
    state.push('tbody_close', 'tbody', -1);
    tbodyLines[1] = nextLine;
  }
  state.push('table_close', 'table', -1);
  tableLines[1] = nextLine;
  state.parentType = oldParentType;
  state.line = nextLine;
  return true;
}

/** The table_code core rule: inside a table, `\|` in a code span's text becomes `|`. */
export function tableCode(state: StateCore): void {
  let depth = 0;
  for (const t of state.tokens) {
    if (t.type === 'table_open') depth += 1;
    else if (t.type === 'table_close') depth -= 1;
    else if (depth > 0 && t.type === 'inline') {
      for (const c of t.children ?? []) {
        if (c.type === 'code_inline') c.content = c.content.replaceAll('\\|', '|');
      }
    }
  }
}

const WRAPPER_OPEN = '<div class="table-wrapper">';

/** The table_open render rule: markdown-it's own <table…> with the wrapper's <div> right before it. */
export function renderTableOpen(
  tokens: Token[],
  idx: number,
  options: Options,
  env: RenderEnv,
  self: Renderer,
): string {
  env.tables += 1;
  return self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options).replace('<table', `${WRAPPER_OPEN}<table`);
}

/** The table_close render rule: markdown-it's own </table> and the wrapper's </div>. */
export function renderTableClose(
  tokens: Token[],
  idx: number,
  options: Options,
  _env: RenderEnv,
  self: Renderer,
): string {
  return self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options).replace('</table>', '</table></div>');
}
```

`src/render/tasklists.ts`:

```ts
// The task_lists core rule (docserver L1; architecture section C, the "Task lists" row; contract sections
// 1 and 6 item 4). A port of the reference's task-list plugin with its defaults (checkboxes disabled, no
// label); markdown-it-task-lists cannot stand in for it, as it writes `checked=""` where the reference
// writes `checked="checked"`. For each list item whose first block is a paragraph whose text starts with
// `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` and then GFM whitespace (space, tab, line feed, \v, \f or \r; not Python's wider
// set), the rule:
// - puts the checkbox before the paragraph's first inline token, as raw HTML of fixed text:
//     <input class="task-list-item-checkbox"{ checked="checked"} disabled="disabled" type="checkbox">
//   checked for `[x] ` and `[X] `, unchecked for `[ ] `. When the marker is followed by whitespace other
//   than a space (`[ ]\tx`, or `[x]` at the end of a line) the reference writes an empty string instead,
//   and so does this rule: the item is still a task item, with no checkbox;
// - drops the marker, the first three code points of that first inline token (Python's `[3:]`), so the
//   whitespace after the marker stays;
// - sets class="task-list-item" on the list item and class="contains-task-list" on the list that holds
//   it (the nearest token before it one level up), so a list that mixes tasks and plain items, and an
//   outer list whose item holds a task list, are marked as the reference marks them.
// It runs right after footnote_tail and before text_join, as the reference's does, so a task item inside
// a footnote is made like any other.
import type { StateCore, Token } from 'markdown-it';
import { cpSlice } from './pyText.js';

/** The task marker at the start of a list item's paragraph text: `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]`, then GFM whitespace. */
export const TASK = /^\[[ xX]\][ \t\n\v\f\r]+/;

/** The checkbox of an open task. */
export const UNCHECKED = '<input class="task-list-item-checkbox" disabled="disabled" type="checkbox">';

/** The checkbox of a done task. */
export const CHECKED =
  '<input class="task-list-item-checkbox" checked="checked" disabled="disabled" type="checkbox">';

/** The checkbox for a task item's text, read by its marker and the space after it; '' as the reference. */
function checkbox(content: string): string {
  if (content.startsWith('[ ] ')) return UNCHECKED;
  if (content.startsWith('[x] ') || content.startsWith('[X] ')) return CHECKED;
  return '';
}

/** Python's `s[3:]`: everything after the first three code points. */
function dropThree(s: string): string {
  return s.substring(cpSlice(s, 3).length);
}

function isTaskItem(tokens: readonly Token[], i: number): boolean {
  return (
    tokens[i]?.type === 'inline' &&
    tokens[i - 1]?.type === 'paragraph_open' &&
    tokens[i - 2]?.type === 'list_item_open' &&
    TASK.test(tokens[i]?.content ?? '')
  );
}

export function taskLists(state: StateCore): void {
  const tokens = state.tokens;
  // For each nesting level, the index of the last token seen at that level. A task item's list is the
  // last token one level above the item. The reference searched backwards from each item instead, which
  // costs a long list quadratic time; this one pass gives the same token. The rule adds children to
  // inline tokens and never adds or removes a token, so the indexes stay valid.
  const last = new Map<number, number>();
  for (const [i, t] of tokens.entries()) {
    last.set(t.level, i);
    // The reference's loop: from the third token to the one before the last.
    if (i < 2 || i >= tokens.length - 1 || !isTaskItem(tokens, i)) continue;
    const item = tokens[i - 2];
    if (item === undefined) continue;
    const children = t.children ?? [];
    const box = new state.Token('html_inline', '', 0);
    box.content = checkbox(t.content);
    const first = children[0];
    if (first !== undefined) first.content = dropThree(first.content);
    children.unshift(box);
    t.children = children;
    t.content = dropThree(t.content);
    item.attrSet('class', 'task-list-item');
    // The reference falls back to tokens[-1], the last token, when no parent is found. A list item always
    // follows its list, so that never happens on a parsed stream; the same fallback is kept all the same.
    tokens.at(last.get(item.level - 1) ?? -1)?.attrSet('class', 'contains-task-list');
  }
}
```

`src/render/engine.ts`:

```ts
// The markdown-it instance behind render() (docserver L1; architecture section C, "Engine"; contract
// section 1). The CommonMark preset with raw HTML off, plus tables and strikethrough, configured once.
// The instance carries no per-document state: everything one render needs lives in its RenderEnv (env.ts).
//
// Pinned on purpose:
// - `html: false` is the raw-HTML wall: markdown-it escapes every tag, and only this library's own rules
//   (the allowlist, allowlist.ts) ever emit markup.
// - `maxNesting` stays the preset's 20, as in the reference: deeper blockquotes and lists stop nesting.
// - `validateLink` and `normalizeLink` are markdown-it's own: javascript:, vbscript:, file: and non-image
//   data: links stay text, and destinations are percent-encoded. Never override them.
//
// markdown-it is 14.3.2, not 15: 15 puts a code span's text into an image's alt (`![a `c`](x)` gives
// alt="a c"), where markdown-it-py, a port of 14, gives alt="a " (decision gate D1, measured on the corpus).
//
// The core chain ends with line_attrs; later rules go `before('line_attrs', …)` so data-line stays last.
// block_strip goes right after block, before inline parsing reads the text it strips (blockStrip.ts).
// The allowlist's rules go right before markdown-it's own raw-HTML rules, which html: false disables:
// safe_block_html with alt paragraph, reference and blockquote (it interrupts those, as in the reference,
// and is not a list terminator), safe_inline_html in the inline chain. balance_details runs after anchors.
// Fences render through this library's own rule (fence.ts), not markdown-it's: a Mermaid figure or a
// highlighted code block, with options.highlight left unset.
// alerts and figcaption follow balance_details. They stand in for the reference's HTML post-passes (its
// caption pass ran first, then its alert pass; the two never touch the same tokens, so their order here
// changes nothing). alerts turns blockquotes into alert_open/alert_close, which render through this
// library's own two rules; figcaption records a caption on its fence token, which renderFence writes.
// Tables, task lists and footnotes, as the reference renders them:
// - the table block rule is this library's port of markdown-it's (tables.ts), set in its place under the
//   same name and with the same alternatives, so it strips the Python way; table_code goes after
//   figcaption, and tables render through this library's two wrapper rules;
// - the footnote plugin is markdown-it-footnote, used as it ships (its output matches the reference's
//   plugin, xhtmlOut included); it adds footnote_def before reference, footnote_inline and footnote_ref
//   after image, and footnote_tail right after inline;
// - task_lists goes before text_join, so after footnote_tail, as the reference's does (tasklists.ts).
import MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it';
import footnote from 'markdown-it-footnote';
import { alerts, renderAlertClose, renderAlertOpen } from './alerts.js';
import { safeBlockHtml, safeInlineHtml } from './allowlist.js';
import { blockStrip } from './blockStrip.js';
import { balanceDetails } from './details.js';
import { renderFence } from './fence.js';
import { figcaption } from './figcaption.js';
import { lineAttrs } from './lineAttrs.js';
import { anchors } from './slug.js';
import { pyTable, renderTableClose, renderTableOpen, tableCode } from './tables.js';
import { taskLists } from './tasklists.js';

export function createEngine(): MarkdownIt {
  const md = new MarkdownIt('commonmark', {
    html: false,
    xhtmlOut: true,
    breaks: false,
    linkify: false,
    typographer: false,
  });
  md.enable(['table', 'strikethrough']);
  md.block.ruler.at('table', pyTable, { alt: ['paragraph', 'reference'] });
  md.use(footnote);
  md.core.ruler.push('line_attrs', lineAttrs);
  md.core.ruler.after('block', 'block_strip', blockStrip);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'anchors', anchors);
  md.block.ruler.before('html_block', 'safe_block_html', safeBlockHtml, {
    alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote'],
  });
  md.inline.ruler.before('html_inline', 'safe_inline_html', safeInlineHtml);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'balance_details', balanceDetails);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'alerts', alerts);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'figcaption', figcaption);
  md.core.ruler.before('text_join', 'task_lists', taskLists);
  md.core.ruler.before('line_attrs', 'table_code', tableCode);
  md.renderer.rules.fence = renderFence;
  md.renderer.rules.alert_open = renderAlertOpen;
  md.renderer.rules.alert_close = renderAlertClose;
  md.renderer.rules.table_open = renderTableOpen;
  md.renderer.rules.table_close = renderTableClose;
  return md;
}
```

`src/render/env.ts`:

```ts
// The per-render state (docserver L1; architecture section C, rule 3 of render(), global constraint 2).
// One RenderEnv is created for each render() call and handed to markdown-it as its `env`; every rule that
// needs state for the length of one document keeps it here, never at module scope, so two renders cannot
// see each other. Later tasks add their fields (the front-matter result) to this interface and to createEnv
// together. The footnote plugin (markdown-it-footnote) keeps its own per-document state on the same object,
// under `footnotes`, which it creates when a document defines a footnote.
import { createCommentScan, type CommentScan } from './allowlist.js';
import { createSlugState, type SlugState } from './slug.js';
import type { Heading } from './types.js';

export interface RenderEnv {
  /** Emit data-line="a-b" on block elements (RenderOptions.lineAttrs, default true). */
  readonly lineAttrs: boolean;
  /** The heading ids this document has handed out (the anchors rule). */
  readonly slugs: SlugState;
  /** Every heading in document order, as the anchors rule set its id (meta.headings). */
  readonly headings: Heading[];
  /** Where the allowlist's comment rules last searched for `-->` (allowlist.ts). */
  readonly comments: CommentScan;
  /** Mermaid figures the fence rule has emitted so far (meta.figures; fence.ts). */
  figures: number;
  /** Their distinct diagram keywords, in document order, at most 32 (meta.mermaidKinds; fence.ts). */
  readonly mermaidKinds: string[];
  /** Code units the fence rule has highlighted so far, at most MAX_HIGHLIGHT_CHARS (fence.ts). */
  highlighted: number;
  /** Tables the table_open rule has emitted so far (meta.tables; tables.ts). */
  tables: number;
  /** Empty cells the table rule has added to short rows in this document, at most 65536 (tables.ts). */
  emptyCells: number;
}

/** A fresh env for one render. */
export function createEnv(o: { lineAttrs: boolean }): RenderEnv {
  return {
    lineAttrs: o.lineAttrs,
    slugs: createSlugState(),
    headings: [],
    comments: createCommentScan(),
    figures: 0,
    mermaidKinds: [],
    highlighted: 0,
    tables: 0,
    emptyCells: 0,
  };
}
```

```ts
// The meta of a rendered document (docserver L1; architecture section C, the "Meta" row; ruling C2).
// Every field is read from what the rules recorded in the document's RenderEnv while it was parsed and
// rendered, so meta and html come from one pass and cannot disagree. Task 4 filled `headings` and `title`,
// Task 6 `figures` and `mermaidKinds` (the fence rule, fence.ts), Task 8 `tables` (the table_open rule,
// tables.ts); Task 9 fills `front` and `frontList`.
import type { RenderEnv } from './env.js';
import type { RenderMeta } from './types.js';

/** The meta of one rendered document. Call it after the env's render has finished. */
export function collectMeta(env: RenderEnv): RenderMeta {
  const headings = env.headings;
  return {
    front: null,
    frontList: null,
    title: headings.find((h) => h.level === 1)?.text ?? null,
    headings,
    figures: env.figures,
    tables: env.tables,
    mermaidKinds: env.mermaidKinds,
  };
}
```

**Decisions this task makes:**
1. **The block rule is the reference's plugin, ported line for line** (mdit-py-plugins 0.6.1's `front_matter`, itself a port of `markdown-it-front-matter`), not the npm plugin. Its quirks are kept, each pinned against the reference: it fires only when `startLine` is 0 and the whole source's first character (`state.src[0]`, not the line's) is `-`, so a bullet item at line 0 whose blockquote holds `---` can carry one and a blockquote at line 0 cannot; three or more dashes open it and the rest of the opening line is not read (`--- x`, `----`); a closer is a line of at least as many dashes followed by spaces only, not indented four or more; a `...` line is seen one turn late, so it closes the block, stays inside the content, and closes nothing when no line follows it; an unclosed block is no front matter. The token is hidden, so markdown-it writes the reference's leading line feed before the next block it renders itself (not before a figure, a details line or indented code, which render through their own rules). It is registered `before('table')` with the plugin's alternatives `paragraph, reference, blockquote, list`, as section C says ("goes first").
2. **YAML is js-yaml 4.3.2's `load(content, { schema: FM_SCHEMA, json: true })`**, and `FM_SCHEMA` is js-yaml's `FAILSAFE_SCHEMA` (strings, sequences and mappings) plus YAML 1.2's null and bool and YAML's merge key `<<` (rulings C15 and C16), with no int or float type. Section C named `CORE_SCHEMA`; ruling C16 replaced it, because the core schema's numbers are JavaScript numbers (`1.0` showed `1`, a 20-digit integer lost precision) and a display library shows what the author wrote. Without the merge key a `<<: *defaults` line, which PyYAML's `safe_load` merges, would render as a `<<` key holding `…`. js-yaml exports its built-in types at run time as `types`, but `@types/js-yaml` 4.0.9 does not declare that export, so `NULL`, `BOOL` and `MERGE` are declared in the file with js-yaml's own definitions. Timestamps, `!!binary`, `!!set`, `!!omap` and `!!pairs` stay out. Measured: the merge cases equal the reference when `<<` comes first in its mapping (decision 10(e) for the other order). `json: true` lets a later duplicate key win, keeping the key's first place, as PyYAML's dict does.
3. **PD2 as ruled (C1, restated by C16), and what follows from it.** `null` (and `~` and an empty value) renders `''`; `true`/`True`/`TRUE` and `false`/`False`/`FALSE` render `true` and `false`; every other scalar renders its source text: `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off`/`y`/`n`, timestamps, `1:30`, `017` (where the core schema read 17), `1.0`, `1.50`, `.inf`, `.nan`, `0o17`, `0x1F`, `1e3`, `-.5`, `1_000` and a 20-digit integer stay exactly as written. Keys are always strings. The explicit tags `!!null`, `!!bool`, `!!str`, `!!seq` and `!!map` load; any other tag (`!!int`, `!!float`, `!!binary`, `!!set`, `!!timestamp`, `!!js/function`, `!!python/...`) fails the load and the block renders nothing. U+0085 is not a YAML 1.2 line break. A list's null item is `''` in the strip and in meta (Python printed `None`); a null value is skipped in meta, as the reference skipped `None`. Against the corpus only `frontmatter-types` moves for PD2: its `flag: yes`, `b: true` and `n: null`, and its `f: 1.50`, which the reference printed as Python's float `1.5`.
4. **The caps follow the reference's slices, which section C's prose words loosely.** The strip takes a list's first 50 items and then skips the nested ones among them (`v[:50]`, then the filter), so `[[n], 1, …, 60]` shows `1` to `49`; meta does the same with 300. Every scalar is cut to 500 code points (300 for a meta list item) with `cpSlice`, never splitting an astral character. The 40-key cut comes before meta skips mappings and nulls. YAML is read only below 20000 code points (`cpLength(content) < 20000`, the strip's own test); the reference's meta pattern allowed exactly 20000, which this library treats as part of PD3 (one block, one cap).
5. **One parse, one mapping (PD3).** The render rule parses the token's content once and records `frontEntries(mapping)` (or `null`) in `RenderEnv.frontList`; `collectMeta` builds `front` from it with `frontRecord`: an `Object.create(null)` object, every key set with `Object.defineProperty`, a list key mapped to its items and a scalar to its one value. So a `__proto__`, `constructor` or `toString` key is an own key, and nothing reaches a prototype. No block, a load error, a list, a scalar or content over the cap gives `front: null, frontList: null`; an empty mapping, or one whose values are all mappings or nulls, gives `frontList: []` and an empty `front` (the reference's meta gave `[]` for `{}` too), while the strip renders nothing for an empty mapping.
6. **The BOM strip (PD4) sits right after the byte gate in `renderWith`.** `bytes` is the input's own UTF-8 length, BOM included (the gate measures the input as given); the strip removes one U+FEFF at index 0 and nothing else, so a second BOM, or one inside the text, stays; the failure fallback escapes the stripped source.
7. **Departures are written by exact edits, not by this renderer.** Step 5's script edits the eight files Task 2 derived from the reference, each edit a literal `old` that must occur exactly once, so each moved byte is named in the plan: four `<dd>` values and three meta values (each in `front` and in `frontList`) for PD2 (`frontmatter-types`: `flag`, `b`, `n` and `f`); one `front`/`frontList` pair for each PD3 case (`dashes4`, `dots`, `space-open`, `crlf`); and for PD4 (`line-endings/bom`) the setext heading the reference made of the BOM and the YAML becomes the strip, its meta gains the pair and loses that heading. `DEPARTURES.json` lists the six cases; Task 2's `expected.test.ts` then checks both directions. The commit names the six ids in `Goldens-moved:` (section D).
8. **The pending hand-over, measured.** Every case labelled `T9` passes after this task and so does `spec-template`, labelled `T10`: its only remaining difference was its front matter. All 16 entries leave and the file is `{}`; the label pattern becomes `T10`-`T12`, because a generated case Task 10 or 11 adds may still need a label. `frontmatter-openers/not-first`, `frontmatter-openers/unclosed` and `line-endings/bom` were passing before this task (no front matter is involved in the first two; Task 4 unpended the third with the reference's output, so this task moves its golden and its code in one change, as Task 4 asked).
9. **Where section F's named reds cannot happen.** M9.6 names `h-frontmatter-hostile/yaml-tags`, but js-yaml 4's `DEFAULT_SCHEMA` has no `js/function` or `python` types either, so that case still renders nothing; row M12 reds through `frontmatter-types` and `frontmatter` (a date becomes a `Date`) and the unit tags case (`!!binary`, `!!set` and `!!timestamp` load). M9.12 names `frontmatter-openers/not-first`, whose first character is `P`, so the `state.src[0]` check refuses it with or without the line-0 check; row M23 reds through the unit case "only at line 0". M9.2, M9.3 and M9.9 each get two rows (strip and meta; `dd` and `dt`).
10. **Loader differences that ruling C17 puts under PD2, found by the differential run (item 5), each pinned by a unit case in the PD2 block (`C17 (a)`-`(e)`, and U+0085):** (a) a key that is an array index (`2:`) is listed before the other keys, because JavaScript orders such keys first: `b: 1` then `2: x` gives `2`, `b` where the reference gave `b`, `2`; (b) a literal or folded block scalar (`|`, `>`) that is the block's last value keeps a trailing line feed (js-yaml appends one to its input; the token content has none, and PyYAML then dropped it): `multi\nline\n` against `multi\nline`; (c) a sequence used as a key (`? [a, b]`) loads as the key `a,b`, where PyYAML refused the whole block; (d) YAML nested deeper than 100 levels fails js-yaml's `maxDepth` and renders nothing, where PyYAML rendered it; (e) a merge key placed after other keys puts the merged keys last, where PyYAML put them first. And U+0085 is not a line break to js-yaml, so `a: x` U+0085 `b: y` fails the load and renders nothing, where PyYAML read two keys. These come from js-yaml and from JavaScript's object order, not from a guard in this library's code, so they have no mutation row; their cases go red if a js-yaml upgrade changes them, which is the point.

```ts
// Front matter (docserver L1, Task 9; architecture section C, the "Front matter" row; contract section 2.12;
// ruling C1's departures PD2, PD3 and PD4). Every expected html string in the first block was produced by
// the reference renderer from the same input and is compared after normaliseForCompare (it only touches
// code blocks). The later blocks pin the three departures, meta.front and meta.frontList, the limits, and
// the rule's place in the engine. Every non-ASCII character is written as a \u escape.
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { normaliseForCompare } from '../src/conformance/normalise.js';
import { checkOutputSafety } from '../src/conformance/oracle.js';
import { createEngine } from '../src/render/engine.js';
import { createEnv } from '../src/render/env.js';
import { FM_MAX_CHARS, frontRecord, parseFrontMatter } from '../src/render/frontMatter.js';
import { render } from '../src/render/index.js';
import type { FrontEntry } from '../src/render/types.js';

type Case = readonly [name: string, src: string, html: string];

function cases(list: readonly Case[]): void {
  for (const [name, src, html] of list) {
    it(name, () => {
      expect(normaliseForCompare(render(src).html)).toBe(html);
    });
  }
}

const dl = (line: string, items: string): string => `<dl class="doc-meta" data-line="${line}">${items}</dl>\n`;
const item = (k: string, v: string): string => `<div><dt>${k}</dt><dd>${v}</dd></div>`;
const scalar = (key: string, v: string): FrontEntry => ({ key, list: false, vals: [v] });
const A1 = dl('1-3', item('a', '1'));

describe('front matter: against the reference', () => {
  cases([
    [
      'a mapping renders the strip; the hidden token puts a line feed before a heading',

        '<ul data-line="8-9">\n<li data-line="8-9">x</li>\n</ul>\n<blockquote data-line="10-10">\n' +
        '<p data-line="10-10">q</p>\n</blockquote>\n',

    [
      'but a list item at line 0 can, inside its own blockquote (the reference reads state.src[0])',
      '- > ---\n  > a: 1\n  > ---\n- b\n',
      '<ul data-line="1-4">\n<li data-line="1-3">\n<blockquote data-line="1-3">' +
        `${A1}</blockquote>\n</li>\n<li data-line="4-4">b</li>\n</ul>\n`,
    ],
    [
      'an empty block, or a block of `...` alone, renders nothing but the line feed',
      '---\n---\n\nx\n',
      '\n<p data-line="4-4">x</p>\n',
    ],
    [
      'a list value joins its items, skipping nested ones; a mapping value is an ellipsis',
      '---\nk: [a, [b], {c: 1}, d]\nm: {x: 1}\n---\n',
      dl('1-4', item('k', 'a, d') + item('m', '\u2026')),
    ],
    [
      'a duplicate key keeps its first place and takes its last value',
      '---\na: 1\nb: 2\na: 3\n---\n',
      dl('1-5', item('a', '3') + item('b', '2')),
    ],
    [
      'the merge key merges, as PyYAML does when it comes first',
      '---\n<<: {z: 1}\nbase: &b {x: 1, y: 2}\nm:\n  <<: *b\n  y: 3\nlist: [*b]\n---\n',
      dl('1-8', item('z', '1') + item('base', '\u2026') + item('m', '\u2026') + item('list', '')),
    ],
    ['an empty mapping renders nothing', '---\n{}\n---\n', ''],
  ]);

  it('meta.frontList equals the reference where its raw-text pattern found the same block', () => {
    expect(render('---\ntitle: T\n---\n# H\n').meta.frontList).toEqual([scalar('title', 'T')]);
    expect(render('---\nk: [a, [b], {c: 1}, d]\nm: {x: 1}\n---\n').meta.frontList).toEqual([
      { key: 'k', list: true, vals: ['a', 'd'] },
    ]);
    expect(render('---\na: 1\nb: 2\na: 3\n---\n').meta.frontList).toEqual([scalar('a', '3'), scalar('b', '2')]);
    expect(render('---\n{}\n---\n').meta.frontList).toEqual([]);
    expect(render('---\nbase: &b {x: 1, y: 2}\nm:\n  <<: *b\n  y: 3\n---\n').meta.frontList).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('PD2: scalars render their source text, without Python (rulings C1 and C16)', () => {
  const SRC =
    '---\nn: null\nt: ~\ne:\nb: true\nB: False\ny: yes\nN: no\non: off\nd: 2026-10-12\n' +
    'dt: 2026-10-12 08:00:00\no: 017\ns: 1:30\nl: [~, false]\n---\n';

  it("null is '', booleans are true/false, yes/no/on/off, timestamps, 017 and 1:30 stay as written", () => {
    expect(render(SRC).html).toBe(
      dl(
        '1-15',
        item('n', '') +
          item('t', '') +
          item('e', '') +
          item('b', 'true') +
          item('B', 'false') +
          item('y', 'yes') +
          item('N', 'no') +
          item('on', 'off') +
          item('d', '2026-10-12') +
          item('dt', '2026-10-12 08:00:00') +
          item('o', '017') +
          item('s', '1:30') +
          item('l', ', false'),
      ),
    );
  });

  it('meta skips null values, as the reference did, and lists a null item as an empty string', () => {
    expect(render(SRC).meta.frontList?.map((e) => `${e.key}=${e.vals.join('|')}`)).toEqual([
      'b=true',
      'B=false',
      'y=yes',
      'N=no',
      'on=off',
      'd=2026-10-12',
      'dt=2026-10-12 08:00:00',
      'o=017',
      's=1:30',
      'l=|false',
    ]);
  });

  it('the schema reads a date, yes and a number as strings', () => {
    const data = parseFrontMatter('d: 2026-10-12\ny: yes\nt: 2026-10-12T08:00:00Z\nv: 1.0');
    expect(data).toEqual({ d: '2026-10-12', y: 'yes', t: '2026-10-12T08:00:00Z', v: '1.0' });
    expect(typeof data?.['d']).toBe('string');
    expect(typeof data?.['v']).toBe('string');
  });

  it('numbers render as written (ruling C16): 1.0, .inf, a 20-digit integer, 0o17; true is true, null is empty', () => {
    const src =
      '---\nversion: 1.0\ninf: .inf\nbig: 12345678901234567890\noct: 0o17\nt: true\nn: null\n' +
      'hex: 0x1F\nexp: 1e3\nneg: -.5\nund: 1_000\nl: [1.50, ~, TRUE, .nan]\n---\n';
    const r = render(src);
    expect(r.html).toBe(
      dl(
        '1-13',
        item('version', '1.0') +
          item('inf', '.inf') +
          item('big', '12345678901234567890') +
          item('oct', '0o17') +
          item('t', 'true') +
          item('n', '') +
          item('hex', '0x1F') +
          item('exp', '1e3') +
          item('neg', '-.5') +
          item('und', '1_000') +
          item('l', '1.50, , true, .nan'),
      ),
    );
    expect({ ...r.meta.front }).toEqual({
      version: '1.0',
      inf: '.inf',
      big: '12345678901234567890',
      oct: '0o17',
      t: 'true',
      hex: '0x1F',
      exp: '1e3',
      neg: '-.5',
      und: '1_000',
      l: ['1.50', '', 'true', '.nan'],
    });
  });

  it('tags outside the schema fail the load: the block renders nothing and meta is null', () => {
    for (const v of ['!!int 3', '!!float 1.5', '!!binary aGVsbG8=', '!!set {a, b}', '!!timestamp 2026-10-12', "!!js/function 'f'"]) {
      const r = render(`---\nk: ${v}\n---\n`);
      expect([r.html, r.meta.frontList, r.meta.front]).toEqual(['', null, null]);
    }
  });

  // Ruling C17: the loader differences PD2 also covers. Each case notes what the reference rendered.
  it('C17 (a): integer-like keys are listed first, where the reference kept document order', () => {
    const r = render('---\na: y\n2: x\n---\n');
    expect(r.html).toBe(dl('1-4', item('2', 'x') + item('a', 'y')));
    expect(r.meta.frontList?.map((e) => e.key)).toEqual(['2', 'a']);
  });

  it('C17 (b): a last block scalar keeps its trailing line feed, where the reference dropped it', () => {
    expect(render('---\nk: v\na: |\n  x\n---\n').html).toBe(dl('1-5', item('k', 'v') + item('a', 'x\n')));
  });

  it('C17 (c): a sequence key loads as its items joined by commas, where the reference rendered nothing', () => {
    expect(render('---\n? [a, b]\n: v\n---\n').html).toBe(dl('1-4', item('a,b', 'v')));
  });

  it('C17 (d): nesting deeper than 100 levels fails the load, where the reference read it', () => {
    const nested = (n: number): string => `---\nk: ${'['.repeat(n)}${']'.repeat(n)}\n---\n`;
    expect(render(nested(99)).html).toBe(dl('1-3', item('k', '')));
    const r = render(nested(100));
    expect([r.html, r.meta.frontList]).toEqual(['', null]);
  });

  it('C17 (e): a late merge key puts the merged keys last, where the reference put them first', () => {
    expect(render('---\na: 1\n<<: {b: 2}\n---\n').html).toBe(dl('1-4', item('a', '1') + item('b', '2')));
    expect(render('---\n<<: {b: 2}\na: 1\n---\n').html).toBe(dl('1-4', item('b', '2') + item('a', '1')));
  });

  it('C17: U+0085 is not a line break, so this value fails the load, where the reference read two keys', () => {
    const r = render('---\na: x\u0085b: y\n---\n');
    expect([r.html, r.meta.frontList]).toEqual(['', null]);
  });
});

describe('PD3: meta comes from the block the strip renders (ruling C1)', () => {
  for (const [name, src] of [
    ['a four-dash opener and closer', '----\na: 1\n----\n'],
    ['a `...` closer', '---\na: 1\n...\n# H\n'],
    ['text after the opening dashes', '--- x\na: 1\n---\n'],
    ['CRLF line endings', '---\r\na: 1\r\n---\r\n'],
    ['CR line endings', '---\ra: 1\r---\r'],
  ] as const) {
    it(`${name}: the strip and meta.frontList both read a: 1`, () => {
      const r = render(src);
      expect(r.html.startsWith(A1)).toBe(true);
      expect(r.meta.frontList).toEqual([scalar('a', '1')]);
      expect({ ...r.meta.front }).toEqual({ a: '1' });
    });
  }

  it('no front matter, or one that is not a mapping, gives null for both', () => {
    for (const src of ['# H\n', '---\na: 1\n', '---\n- a\n- b\n---\n', '---\n: : bad\n---\n', '---\nplain\n---\n']) {
      const r = render(src);
      expect([r.meta.front, r.meta.frontList]).toEqual([null, null]);
    }
  });
});

describe('PD4: one leading byte order mark is removed (ruling C1)', () => {
  it('a BOM file keeps its front matter, and bytes still counts the BOM', () => {
    const r = render('\ufeff---\na: 1\n---\n');
    expect(r.html).toBe(A1);
    expect(r.meta.frontList).toEqual([scalar('a', '1')]);
    expect(r.bytes).toBe(16);
  });

  it('only one is removed, and only at the start', () => {
    expect(render('\ufeff\ufeff---\na: 1\n---\n').html).toBe('<h2 id="---a-1" data-line="1-3">\ufeff---\na: 1</h2>\n');
    expect(render('\ufeffx\ufeff\n').html).toBe('<p data-line="1-1">x\ufeff</p>\n');
  });
});

describe('meta.front and meta.frontList', () => {
  it('front is a null-prototype record of frontList: a list to its items, a scalar to its value', () => {
    const r = render('---\nkey: [1, 2]\none: x\n---\n');
    expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(r.meta.front)).toBe(null);
    expect({ ...r.meta.front }).toEqual({ key: ['1', '2'], one: 'x' });
    expect(r.meta.frontList).toEqual([{ key: 'key', list: true, vals: ['1', '2'] }, scalar('one', 'x')]);
  });

  it('an own __proto__ key stays an own key, round-trips through JSON and pollutes nothing', () => {
    const r = render('---\n__proto__: polluted\nconstructor: built\ntoString: str\n---\n');
    const front = r.meta.front ?? {};
    expect(Object.keys(front)).toEqual(['__proto__', 'constructor', 'toString']);
    expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(front, '__proto__')?.value).toBe('polluted');
    expect(JSON.stringify(front)).toBe('{"__proto__":"polluted","constructor":"built","toString":"str"}');
    const back = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(front)) as Record<string, unknown>;
    expect(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(back, '__proto__')?.value).toBe('polluted');
    expect(({} as Record<string, unknown>)['polluted']).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('frontRecord builds every key with defineProperty on a null-prototype object', () => {
    const rec = frontRecord([scalar('__proto__', 'p'), { key: 'l', list: true, vals: [] }]);
    expect(Object.getPrototypeOf(rec)).toBe(null);
    expect(Object.keys(rec)).toEqual(['__proto__', 'l']);
    expect(rec['l']).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('a mapping with no listable value gives an empty frontList and an empty front', () => {
    const r = render('---\nm: {x: 1}\nn: null\n---\n');
    expect(r.meta.frontList).toEqual([]);
    expect(Object.keys(r.meta.front ?? { x: 1 })).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('the limits', () => {
  const ASTRAL = '\u{1F600}';

  it('40 keys, the first in document order, in the strip and in meta', () => {
    const src = `---\n${Array.from({ length: 41 }, (_, i) => `k${i}: v`).join('\n')}\n---\n`;
    const r = render(src);
    expect(r.html.split('<dt>').length - 1).toBe(40);
    expect(r.html).not.toContain('<dt>k40</dt>');
    expect(r.meta.frontList).toHaveLength(40);
  });

  it('500 code points of a value, never half an astral character', () => {
    const r = render(`---\nv: ${'a'.repeat(499)}${ASTRAL}b\n---\n`);
    expect(r.html).toBe(dl('1-3', item('v', `${'a'.repeat(499)}${ASTRAL}`)));
    expect(r.meta.frontList).toEqual([scalar('v', `${'a'.repeat(499)}${ASTRAL}`)]);
  });

  it('the strip reads the first 50 items of a list, then skips the nested ones among them', () => {
    const items = ['[n]', ...Array.from({ length: 60 }, (_, i) => String(i + 1))];
    const r = render(`---\nk: [${items.join(', ')}]\n---\n`);
    expect(r.html).toBe(dl('1-3', item('k', Array.from({ length: 49 }, (_, i) => String(i + 1)).join(', '))));
  });

  it('meta reads the first 300 items, then skips nested ones; 300 code points of each', () => {
    const items = ['{m: 1}', `${'b'.repeat(299)}${ASTRAL}c`, ...Array.from({ length: 400 }, (_, i) => `w${i}`)];
    const r = render(`---\nk: [${items.join(', ')}]\n---\n`);
    const vals = r.meta.frontList?.[0]?.vals ?? [];
    expect(vals).toHaveLength(299);
    expect(vals[0]).toBe(`${'b'.repeat(299)}${ASTRAL}`);
    expect(vals.at(-1)).toBe('w297');
  });

  it('YAML of FM_MAX_CHARS code points or more is not read; the count is code points', () => {
    expect(FM_MAX_CHARS).toBe(20000);
    const under = `x: ${ASTRAL.repeat(FM_MAX_CHARS - 4)}`;
    const at = `x: ${ASTRAL.repeat(FM_MAX_CHARS - 3)}`;
    expect(Object.keys(parseFrontMatter(under) ?? {})).toEqual(['x']);
    expect(parseFrontMatter(at)).toBe(null);
    expect(render(`---\n${at}\n---\n`).html).toBe('');
  });

  it('a list of aliases to one list stays cheap (the anchors are shared, never expanded)', () => {
    const rows = ['a: &a [x, x, x, x, x, x, x, x, x]'];
    for (let i = 1; i < 12; i += 1) {
      const p = String.fromCharCode(96 + i);
      rows.push(`${String.fromCharCode(97 + i)}: &${String.fromCharCode(97 + i)} [${Array(9).fill(`*${p}`).join(', ')}]`);
    }
    const started = performance.now();
    const r = render(`---\n${rows.join('\n')}\n---\n`);
    expect(performance.now() - started).toBeLessThan(1000);
    expect(r.meta.frontList).toHaveLength(12);
  });
});
```
