```ts
// Front matter (docserver L1; architecture section C, the "Front matter" row; contract section 2.12;
// ruling C1's departures PD2 and PD3). Three parts:
// - frontMatterRule, the block rule. It is the reference's plugin (a port of markdown-it-front-matter),
//   step for step, quirks included: it fires only for line 0 of a block run whose source starts with `-`
//   (state.src[0], not the line's own first character, so a bullet list item that starts the document can
//   hold one); three or more dashes open it and the rest of that line is not read; it closes on a line of
//   at least as many dashes followed by spaces only, or right after a `...` line (which stays inside the
//   content); a document with no closing line has no front matter. So `---` thematic breaks around text
//   at the top of a document make front matter of the text between them, as in the reference.
//   The token is hidden: markdown-it writes a line feed before the next block, as the reference's does.
// - renderFrontMatter, the render rule: the content, when under FM_MAX_CHARS code points, is read as YAML
//   by js-yaml in JSON mode with FM_SCHEMA: the failsafe schema (strings, sequences, mappings) plus YAML
//   1.2's null and bool and the merge key, and no int or float (PD2, ruling C16: `null` renders '',
//   booleans `true`/`false`, and every other scalar renders its source text, so `1.0`, `.inf`, `0o17`, a
//   20-digit integer, `yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` and timestamps stay as the author wrote them; no other tags,
//   so `!!int`, `!!float`, `!!js/function`, `!!python/...`, `!!binary` and `!!set` fail the load). The
//   merge key `<<` is there because PyYAML's safe_load reads it and without it a common
//   `<<: *defaults` would render as a key. JSON mode lets a later duplicate key win, as PyYAML's does.
//   A non-empty mapping renders
//     <dl class="doc-meta"{ data-line}><div><dt>{key}</dt><dd>{value}</dd></div>…</dl>\n
//   for its first FM_MAX_KEYS keys, key and value escaped with Python's html.escape (pyEscape); anything
//   else (a load error, a list, a scalar, an empty mapping) renders ''.
// - frontEntries and frontRecord: meta.frontList and meta.front, read from the SAME parsed mapping
//   (PD3), so the strip and the meta can never disagree; the reference read meta from the raw text with a
//   second, stricter pattern, which missed CRLF files, `----` and `--- x` openers and `...` closers.
// Python's len() and [:n] are cpLength and cpSlice (global constraint 6).
import { FAILSAFE_SCHEMA, load, Type } from 'js-yaml';
import type { StateBlock, Token } from 'markdown-it';
import type { RenderEnv } from './env.js';
import { pyEscape } from './escape.js';
import { lineAttr } from './lineAttrs.js';
import { cpLength, cpSlice } from './pyText.js';
import type { FrontEntry } from './types.js';

/** Content of this many code points or more is not read as YAML at all. */
export const FM_MAX_CHARS = 20000;
/** Keys shown in the strip and listed in meta.frontList, the first in document order. */
export const FM_MAX_KEYS = 40;
/** Code points of a scalar value, in the strip and in meta. */
export const FM_MAX_VALUE = 500;
/** Items of a list value the strip reads (nested lists and mappings among them are then skipped). */
export const FM_MAX_ITEMS = 50;
/** Items of a list value meta.frontList reads, and code points of each item. */
export const FM_LIST_MAX_ITEMS = 300;
export const FM_LIST_MAX_ITEM = 300;

const DASH = 0x2d;
const MIN_MARKERS = 3;

/** YAML 1.2's null, as js-yaml defines it (an empty value is null before any type is asked). */
const NULL = new Type('tag:yaml.org,2002:null', {
  kind: 'scalar',
  resolve: (data: unknown) => data === null || data === '~' || data === 'null' || data === 'Null' || data === 'NULL',
  construct: () => null,
});

const TRUE = new Set(['true', 'True', 'TRUE']);
const FALSE = new Set(['false', 'False', 'FALSE']);

/** YAML 1.2's bool, as js-yaml defines it: three spellings of each value, nothing else (not yes/no/on/off). */
const BOOL = new Type('tag:yaml.org,2002:bool', {
  kind: 'scalar',
  resolve: (data: unknown) => typeof data === 'string' && (TRUE.has(data) || FALSE.has(data)),
  construct: (data: string) => TRUE.has(data),
});

/** YAML's merge key, as js-yaml defines it for its default schema (the loader acts on this tag). */
const MERGE = new Type('tag:yaml.org,2002:merge', {
  kind: 'scalar',
  resolve: (data: unknown) => data === '<<' || data === null,
});

/**
 * The schema front matter is read with (PD2, ruling C16): failsafe plus null, bool and the merge key. It has
 * no int or float type, so a number stays the text the author wrote.
 */
export const FM_SCHEMA = FAILSAFE_SCHEMA.extend({ implicit: [NULL, BOOL, MERGE] });

/** A parsed front-matter block: the mapping, or null when the content is not a mapping. */
export type FrontMapping = Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;

/** The front_matter block rule (the reference's plugin, ported line for line). */
export function frontMatterRule(state: StateBlock, startLine: number, endLine: number, silent: boolean): boolean {
  const src = state.src;
  let start = (state.bMarks[startLine] ?? 0) + (state.tShift[startLine] ?? 0);
  let max = state.eMarks[startLine] ?? 0;

  // Only the first line of a block run, and only when the whole source starts with a dash.
  if (startLine !== 0 || src.charCodeAt(0) !== DASH) return false;

  // The opening run of dashes; the rest of the line is not read.
  let pos = start + 1;
  while (pos <= max && pos < src.length) {
    if (src.charCodeAt(pos) !== DASH) break;
    pos += 1;
  }
  const markerCount = pos - start;
  if (markerCount < MIN_MARKERS) return false;
  if (silent) return true;

  let nextLine = startLine;
  let autoClosed = false;
  for (;;) {
    nextLine += 1;
    // No closing line: not front matter.
    if (nextLine >= endLine) return false;
    // The line read in the previous turn was `...`: close after it, keeping it in the content.
    if (src.slice(start, max) === '...') break;

    start = (state.bMarks[nextLine] ?? 0) + (state.tShift[nextLine] ?? 0);
    max = state.eMarks[nextLine] ?? 0;

    if (start < max && (state.sCount[nextLine] ?? 0) < state.blkIndent) break;
    if (src.charCodeAt(start) !== DASH) continue;
    if ((state.sCount[nextLine] ?? 0) - state.blkIndent >= 4) continue;

    pos = start + 1;
    while (pos < max) {
      if (src.charCodeAt(pos) !== DASH) break;
      pos += 1;
    }
    if (pos - start < markerCount) continue;
    pos = state.skipSpaces(pos);
    if (pos < max) continue;

    autoClosed = true;
    break;
  }

  const oldParent = state.parentType;
  const oldLineMax = state.lineMax;
  state.parentType = 'container' as typeof state.parentType;
  state.lineMax = nextLine;

  const token = state.push('front_matter', '', 0);
  token.hidden = true;
  token.markup = '---';
  token.content = src.slice(state.bMarks[startLine + 1] ?? 0, state.eMarks[nextLine - 1] ?? 0);
  token.block = true;

  state.parentType = oldParent;
  state.lineMax = oldLineMax;
  state.line = nextLine + (autoClosed ? 1 : 0);
  token.map = [startLine, state.line];
  return true;
}

function isNested(v: unknown): boolean {
  return typeof v === 'object' && v !== null;
}

function isMapping(v: unknown): v is FrontMapping {
  return typeof v === 'object' && v !== null && !Array.isArray(v);
}

/** The YAML of a front-matter block as a mapping, or null (too long, a load error, or not a mapping). */
export function parseFrontMatter(content: string): FrontMapping | null {
  if (cpLength(content) >= FM_MAX_CHARS) return null;
  let data: unknown;
  try {
    data = load(content, { schema: FM_SCHEMA, json: true });
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
  return isMapping(data) ? data : null;
}

/** A scalar as text (PD2: null is the empty string, a boolean true or false; the schema reads no numbers). */
function scalarText(v: unknown): string {
  return v === null ? '' : String(v);
}

/** The strip's text for one value: a list's first FM_MAX_ITEMS items, nested ones skipped, joined by `, `. */
export function fmValue(v: unknown): string {
  if (Array.isArray(v)) {
    return v
      .slice(0, FM_MAX_ITEMS)
      .filter((x) => !isNested(x))
      .map(fmValue)
      .join(', ');
  }
  if (isNested(v)) return '\u2026';
  return cpSlice(scalarText(v), FM_MAX_VALUE);
}

/** The first FM_MAX_KEYS keys of a mapping, in document order. */
function firstKeys(data: FrontMapping): string[] {
  return Object.keys(data).slice(0, FM_MAX_KEYS);
}

/** meta.frontList: after the key cut, a list gives its items, a scalar its text; a mapping or null is skipped. */
export function frontEntries(data: FrontMapping): FrontEntry[] {
  const out: FrontEntry[] = [];
  for (const key of firstKeys(data)) {
    const v = data[key];
    if (Array.isArray(v)) {
      const vals = v
        .slice(0, FM_LIST_MAX_ITEMS)
        .filter((x) => !isNested(x))
        .map((x) => cpSlice(scalarText(x), FM_LIST_MAX_ITEM));
      out.push({ key, list: true, vals });
    } else if (!isNested(v) && v !== null) {
      out.push({ key, list: false, vals: [cpSlice(scalarText(v), FM_MAX_VALUE)] });
    }
  }
  return out;
}

/** meta.front: a null-prototype record of frontList, each key to its list or its one value. */
export function frontRecord(list: readonly FrontEntry[]): Readonly<Record<string, string | readonly string[]>> {
  const out = Object.create(null) as Record<string, string | readonly string[]>;
  for (const e of list) {
    Object.defineProperty(out, e.key, {
      value: e.list ? e.vals : (e.vals[0] ?? ''),
      enumerable: true,
      writable: true,
      configurable: true,
    });
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * The front_matter render rule. Its mapping also gives the document's meta (PD3). A document has at most
 * one front_matter token: the rule fires only at line 0, and the first block that takes line 0 consumes it.
 */
export function renderFrontMatter(tokens: Token[], idx: number, _options: unknown, env: RenderEnv): string {
  const token = tokens[idx];
  if (token === undefined) return '';
  const data = parseFrontMatter(token.content);
  env.frontList = data === null ? null : frontEntries(data);
  if (data === null) return '';
  const keys = firstKeys(data);
  if (keys.length === 0) return '';
  const items = keys
    .map((k) => `<div><dt>${pyEscape(k)}</dt><dd>${pyEscape(fmValue(data[k]))}</dd></div>`)
    .join('');
  return `<dl class="doc-meta"${lineAttr(token, env)}>${items}</dl>\n`;
}
```

```js
// Writes the PD2-PD4 departures into conformance/expected/ by exact edits of the files Task 2 derived from
// the reference: each `old` must occur exactly once in its file, or nothing is written.
// usage: node departures.mjs <checkout>
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const root = path.join(path.resolve(process.argv[2] ?? '.'), 'conformance', 'expected');
const NO_FRONT = '"front": null,\n  "frontList": null,';
/** The meta.json text of a front matter with one scalar key, as JSON.stringify(meta, null, 2) writes it. */
const oneKey = (key, value) =>
  `"front": {\n    "${key}": "${value}"\n  },\n  "frontList": [\n    {\n      "key": "${key}",\n` +
  `      "list": false,\n      "vals": [\n        "${value}"\n      ]\n    }\n  ],`;
const listed = (key, value) => `"key": "${key}",\n      "list": false,\n      "vals": [\n        "${value}"`;

const EDITS = [
  // PD2 (rulings C1 and C16): scalars render their source text, without Python's None, True and 1.5.
  ['frontmatter-types.html', '<dt>flag</dt><dd>True</dd>', '<dt>flag</dt><dd>yes</dd>'],
  ['frontmatter-types.html', '<dt>b</dt><dd>True</dd>', '<dt>b</dt><dd>true</dd>'],
  ['frontmatter-types.html', '<dt>n</dt><dd>None</dd>', '<dt>n</dt><dd></dd>'],
  ['frontmatter-types.html', '<dt>f</dt><dd>1.5</dd>', '<dt>f</dt><dd>1.50</dd>'],
  ['frontmatter-types.meta.json', '"flag": "True",', '"flag": "yes",'],
  ['frontmatter-types.meta.json', '"b": "True",', '"b": "true",'],
  ['frontmatter-types.meta.json', listed('flag', 'True'), listed('flag', 'yes')],
  ['frontmatter-types.meta.json', listed('b', 'True'), listed('b', 'true')],
  ['frontmatter-types.meta.json', '"f": "1.5",', '"f": "1.50",'],
  ['frontmatter-types.meta.json', listed('f', '1.5'), listed('f', '1.50')],
  // PD3: meta from the block the strip renders.
  ['frontmatter-openers/dashes4.meta.json', NO_FRONT, oneKey('a', '1')],
  ['frontmatter-openers/dots.meta.json', NO_FRONT, oneKey('a', '1')],
  ['frontmatter-openers/space-open.meta.json', NO_FRONT, oneKey('a', '1')],
  ['line-endings/crlf.meta.json', NO_FRONT, oneKey('title', 'Carriage returns')],
  // PD4: a leading BOM is removed, so the block is front matter and no longer a setext heading.
  [
    'line-endings/bom.html',
    '<h2 id="---title-byte-order-mark" data-line="1-3">\ufeff---\ntitle: Byte order mark</h2>\n',
    '<dl class="doc-meta" data-line="1-3"><div><dt>title</dt><dd>Byte order mark</dd></div></dl>\n\n',
  ],
  ['line-endings/bom.meta.json', NO_FRONT, oneKey('title', 'Byte order mark')],
  [
    'line-endings/bom.meta.json',
    '    {\n      "level": 2,\n      "id": "---title-byte-order-mark",\n' +
      '      "text": "\ufeff---title: Byte order mark"\n    },\n',
    '',
  ],
];

const text = new Map();
for (const [file, old, next] of EDITS) {
  const src = text.get(file) ?? readFileSync(path.join(root, file), 'utf8');
  const hits = src.split(old).length - 1;
  if (hits !== 1) throw new Error(`${file}: expected one ${JSON.stringify(old)}, found ${hits}`);
  text.set(file, src.replace(old, next));
}
for (const [file, src] of text) writeFileSync(path.join(root, file), src, 'utf8');
console.log(`departures: ${EDITS.length} edits in ${text.size} files`);
```

- Produces, for every later task:
  - **`scanRefs` semantics** (Task 11 builds the `x-limits/images-many` verdict on them): `outcome: 'over-limit'` gives `images: []`, `imagesTruncated: false`, `mermaid: { fences: 0, largestBytes: 0, totalBytes: 0 }`; otherwise `'scanned'`, `images` the distinct `<img src>` values `render()` writes (entity-decoded), in document order, at most `maxImages`, and `imagesTruncated` true exactly when another distinct source exists; `mermaid` counts the fences `render()` makes figures with the UTF-8 sizes of their content.
  - **`test/corpus-pending.json` stays `{}`** and a label may only be `T11` or `T12`.
  - **Task 12's browser bundle** picks up `scan.ts` through `src/render/index.ts`; `scan.ts` imports nothing outside `src/render` but `markdown-it` types.

**Decisions this task makes:**
1. **Parse only, render's engine, render's text.** `scanWith` runs `engine.parse(stripBom(markdown), createEnv({ lineAttrs: true }))` and walks the result. markdown-it's `parse` runs the whole core chain (block, inline, footnote_tail, task_lists, anchors, balance_details, alerts, figcaption, table_code, line_attrs), so the token stream is the one `render()` hands to its renderer; nothing is rendered (a unit case swaps in an engine whose renderer throws). `scanRefs` uses `render.ts`'s `ENGINE`, not a second instance, and the same `stripBom` and `checkLimit`, so the two cannot drift apart: the byte gate, the BOM strip (PD4) and the option checks are one code path.
2. **Images are read where `render()` writes them, and only there.** The children of every `inline` token (headings, paragraphs, table cells, list items, alerts, link labels, and footnotes: `footnote_tail` has already moved each referenced note into the stream and dropped every unreferenced definition); and the caption paragraph that the figcaption rule took out of the stream (decision 3). An image token's own children are its alt text, which markdown-it's `renderInlineAsText` writes as text, so an image inside an alt is not read. The value is `attrGet('src')`, which markdown-it's `normalizeLink` has already encoded (`<a b>` is `a%20b`, `é.png` is `%C3%A9.png`, `x&amp;y` is `x&y`): exactly what `render()` writes before `escapeHtml`. A link `validateLink` refuses is never an image token, so it is never read.
3. **A caption's images (found while planning).** The figcaption rule (Task 7) renders the caption paragraph's inline tokens into HTML at core time and drops the paragraph's three tokens, so after `md.parse` an image in `*Figure 1. ![a](cap.png)*` exists only inside `FenceMeta.caption`'s HTML. The reference writes it there too (`<figcaption>Figure 1. <img src="cap.png" alt="a" /> x</figcaption>`, measured on `"$REFERENCE_RENDERER"`). So `FenceMeta` gains `inline`, the dropped paragraph's inline children, and `scanRefs` reads them right after the fence's size, which is where the figcaption sits in the html. Every image among those tokens is inside the caption, because the caption pattern needs the whole paragraph to be one `<em>…</em>`. No html changes.
4. **Distinct, capped, and honest about the cap (C2).** A `Set` keeps the distinct sources in first-seen order and never holds more than `maxImages`; a further distinct source sets `imagesTruncated` and is not stored, so memory is bounded by `maxImages` on any input. A duplicate of a kept source never sets the flag. `maxImages: 0` returns no images and still says whether any exists. An invalid `maxImages` or `maxBytes` (NaN, negative, fractional, infinite) is a `RangeError`, as `render()`'s `maxBytes` already is, never a cap that admits everything.
5. **Mermaid fences are `renderFence`'s own test.** A `fence` token counts when `fenceName(info) === MERMAID` (exact, case-sensitive, first word after Python's strip, split on a space only): `mermaid extra` and `` ``` mermaid`` count, `Mermaid` does not, an indented block is never a fence. `largestBytes` and `totalBytes` are `utf8Length(content)` of the raw content, which the figure writes `pyEscape`d, so the invariant decodes the figure's text and measures it the same way.
6. **`meta` needs no code here.** `figures` and `mermaidKinds` (with its 32 cap, `%%` skip and diagram front-matter skip) landed in Task 6, `tables` in Task 8, and all three are counted at render time (`md.parse` alone counts nothing). This task proves them consistent with the html instead: for every corpus case and every document of the new file, `meta.figures` equals the number of `<figure class="mermaid-figure">` and equals `scanRefs`' `mermaid.fences`; `meta.tables` equals the number of table wrappers; `meta.headings` lists exactly the `<hN id>` of the html, in order and level; `meta.title` is the first level-1 heading's text; `meta.mermaidKinds` is the distinct non-null `mermaidKind` of the figures' sources, in order, cut at 32.
7. **What section F asks for that cannot happen here, and the nearest correct thing.**
   - "Cases unpended: `x-limits/images-many`": the case is a generated one (section E row 40), and generated cases, `conformance/hostile.json` and `buildInput` are Task 11's; `loadCorpus` refuses a `generated` entry until then. Its shape is pinned here as a unit case instead (10000 distinct images give the first 512, truncated) together with the boundary cases (512 distinct plus duplicates are not truncated; 513 are). Task 11 must add the case with a `scanRefs` verdict (`images.length ≤ 512`, `imagesTruncated: true`); `Verdict` today describes a `render()` result only.
   - "Cases unpended: `spec-template`": it already passes since Task 9 (Task 9's decision 8); the pending file is `{}` before and after this task.
   - M10.3 ("keep duplicates" reds the `links-images` invariant): the distinct list is a `Set`, so no one-line mutation keeps duplicates in it. The guard that can be removed is the early `has` return, without which a duplicate of a kept source past the cap sets `imagesTruncated`; row M3 reds that. The invariants still compare `images` with the html's distinct sources (`h-attr-smuggle` shows `b` twice).
   - M10.6 (kinds skip `%%` and fence front matter) is Task 6's L1-T6-M13 and L1-T6-M14, unchanged and still applying at this state; the invariant here cannot see it, because it measures kinds with the same `mermaidKind`. M10.7 (the 32 cap) is L1-T6-M15, and row M17 here reds this file's forty-kind document as well.
8. **Rows on the code this task moves or re-spells.** Only L1-T9-M21/M22 move: their `old`, the BOM line in `renderWith`, becomes the body of `stripBom`, and row M19 stands in for them at this state, red in both `render()`'s tests and `scanRefs`'. L1-T3-M8's anchor, the test inside `checkLimit`, is unchanged when the helper gains its function name and is exported, so M8 still applies once at this task and every later one; row M20 re-measures it at the shared helper, with the same anchor, and is red in `scanRefs`' tests as well as `render()`'s. Every non-ASCII character in it is written as a backslash-u escape, so it holds no non-ASCII byte (check with `grep -nP '[^\x00-\x7e]' test/scan.test.ts; echo "rc=$?"`, which must print only `rc=1`). If your editor turns an escape into the character itself, write the file with a shell heredoc instead.

```ts
// scanRefs and the consistency invariants (docserver L1, Task 10; architecture section C, the "scanRefs" and
// "Meta" rows; section F, T10; rulings C2 and C3). scanRefs parses and never renders, so the first block
// checks it against render() itself: for every corpus case and for this file's own documents, the images
// and Mermaid sizes scanRefs reports are exactly what render()'s html shows, and render()'s meta agrees
// with its own html (figures, tables, heading ids, title, Mermaid kinds). The later blocks pin scanRefs'
// own rules with exact values. Every non-ASCII character is written as a \u escape.
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { loadCorpus } from '../src/conformance/index.js';
import { createEngine } from '../src/render/engine.js';
import { MAX_MERMAID_KINDS, mermaidKind } from '../src/render/fence.js';
import { DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES, DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES, render, scanRefs } from '../src/render/index.js';
import { utf8Length } from '../src/render/pyText.js';
import { scanWith } from '../src/render/scan.js';
import type { ScanRefsResult } from '../src/render/types.js';

const NO_MERMAID = { fences: 0, largestBytes: 0, totalBytes: 0 };
const OVER: ScanRefsResult = { outcome: 'over-limit', images: [], imagesTruncated: false, mermaid: NO_MERMAID };

/** markdown-it's escapeHtml undone: the four entities it writes into an attribute value. */
function unescapeMd(s: string): string {
  return s.replace(/&(?:amp|lt|gt|quot);/g, (e) => ({ '&amp;': '&', '&lt;': '<', '&gt;': '>', '&quot;': '"' })[e] ?? e);
}

/** Python's html.escape undone (pyEscape): the five entities it writes. */
function unescapePy(s: string): string {
  return unescapeMd(s.replaceAll('&#x27;', "'"));
}

/**
 * What render()'s html itself shows. Every `<` that markdown-it or this library's rules escape is `&lt;`, so
 * each pattern below only meets markup the renderer emitted: an image's src, a figure's escaped source
 * (which holds no `<`), a table wrapper, a heading's id.
 */
function fromHtml(html: string): { images: string[]; sources: string[]; tables: number; headings: string[] } {
  const images = [...html.matchAll(/<img src="([^"]*)"/g)].map((m) => unescapeMd(m[1] ?? ''));
  return {
    images: [...new Set(images)],
    sources: [...html.matchAll(/<figure class="mermaid-figure"[^>]*><pre class="mermaid">([^<]*)<\/pre>/g)].map(
      (m) => unescapePy(m[1] ?? ''),
    ),
    tables: html.split('<div class="table-wrapper"><table').length - 1,
    headings: [...html.matchAll(/<h([1-6]) id="([^"]*)"/g)].map((m) => `${m[1] ?? ''}#${m[2] ?? ''}`),
  };
}

/** scanRefs against render() on one document, and render()'s meta against its own html. */
function consistent(markdown: string): void {
  const r = render(markdown);
  const s = scanRefs(markdown);
  expect(r.outcome).toBe('rendered');
  const h = fromHtml(r.html);
  expect(s.outcome).toBe('scanned');
  expect(s.images).toEqual(h.images.slice(0, DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES));
  expect(s.imagesTruncated).toBe(h.images.length > DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES);
  const sizes = h.sources.map((x) => utf8Length(x, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER));
  expect(s.mermaid).toEqual({
    fences: h.sources.length,
    largestBytes: sizes.reduce((a, b) => Math.max(a, b), 0),
    totalBytes: sizes.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0),
  });
  expect(s.mermaid.fences).toBe(r.meta.figures);
  expect(r.meta.tables).toBe(h.tables);
  expect(r.meta.headings.map((x) => `${x.level}#${x.id}`)).toEqual(h.headings);
  expect(r.meta.title).toBe(r.meta.headings.find((x) => x.level === 1)?.text ?? null);
  const kinds = [...new Set(h.sources.map(mermaidKind).filter((k) => k !== null))].slice(0, MAX_MERMAID_KINDS);
  expect(r.meta.mermaidKinds).toEqual(kinds);
  // The byte gate is the same gate: one byte less than the document is over the limit for both.
  if (r.bytes > 0) {
    expect(render(markdown, { maxBytes: r.bytes - 1 }).outcome).toBe('over-limit');
    expect(scanRefs(markdown, { maxBytes: r.bytes - 1 })).toEqual(OVER);
  }
}

describe('scanRefs: images', () => {
  it('each source as render() writes it: normalizeLink applied, entities decoded, in document order, once', () => {
    const md = '![a](<a b>) ![b](x&amp;y) ![c](%41) ![d](\u00e9.png) ![e](2.png) ![f](a%20b)\n';
    expect(scanRefs(md).images).toEqual(['a%20b', 'x&y', '%41', '%C3%A9.png', '2.png']);
  });

  it('a link markdown-it refuses is no image; an allowed data:image is one', () => {
    const md = '![x](javascript:alert(1)) ![y](data:text/html,x) ![z](data:image/png;base64,AA)\n';
    expect(scanRefs(md).images).toEqual(['data:image/png;base64,AA']);
  });

  it('an image inside an alt is not an image; a caption and a footnote are read where render() writes them', () => {
    expect(scanRefs('![![in](inner.png)](outer.png)\n').images).toEqual(['outer.png']);
    expect(scanRefs('```mermaid\nA\n```\n*Figure 1. ![a](cap.png) x*\n\n![b](after.png)\n').images).toEqual([
      'cap.png',
      'after.png',
    ]);
    const notes = 'x[^1] ![m](main.png) ^[![i](inline.png)]\n\n[^1]: ![f](foot.png)\n\n[^2]: ![u](u.png)\n';
    expect(scanRefs(notes).images).toEqual(['main.png', 'foot.png', 'inline.png']);
  });

  it('a leading BOM is removed first, as render() removes it (PD4)', () => {
    expect(scanRefs('\ufeff---\nx: ![a](fm.png)\n---\n![b](body.png)\n').images).toEqual(['body.png']);
    expect(scanRefs('---\nx: ![a](fm.png)\n---\n![b](body.png)\n').images).toEqual(['body.png']);
  });
});

describe('scanRefs: the image cap', () => {
  const doc = (n: number): string => Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => `![i](${String(i)}.png)`).join(' ');

  it(`the default keeps ${String(DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES)} distinct sources and says when more exist`, () => {
    const exact = scanRefs(`${doc(DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES)} ${doc(5)}\n`);
    expect(exact.images).toHaveLength(DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES);
    expect(exact.imagesTruncated).toBe(false);
    const over = scanRefs(`${doc(DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES + 1)}\n`);
    expect(over.images).toEqual(exact.images);
    expect(over.imagesTruncated).toBe(true);
  });

  it('10000 distinct images: the first 512, truncated', () => {
    const s = scanRefs(`${doc(10000)}\n`);
    expect(s.images).toHaveLength(512);
    expect(s.images[511]).toBe('511.png');
    expect(s.imagesTruncated).toBe(true);
  });

  it('maxImages is the host\'s: 2 keeps two; 0 keeps none and still says whether any exists', () => {
    expect(scanRefs(`${doc(3)}\n`, { maxImages: 2 })).toMatchObject({
      images: ['0.png', '1.png'],
      imagesTruncated: true,
    });
    expect(scanRefs(`${doc(2)} ${doc(2)}\n`, { maxImages: 2 })).toMatchObject({ imagesTruncated: false });
    expect(scanRefs(`${doc(1)}\n`, { maxImages: 0 })).toMatchObject({ images: [], imagesTruncated: true });
    expect(scanRefs('no images\n', { maxImages: 0 })).toMatchObject({ images: [], imagesTruncated: false });
  });

  it('an invalid maxImages or maxBytes is a RangeError, not a cap that lets everything through', () => {
    for (const v of [Number.NaN, -1, 1.5, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY]) {
      expect(() => scanRefs('x', { maxImages: v })).toThrow(RangeError);
      expect(() => scanRefs('x', { maxBytes: v })).toThrow(RangeError);
    }
  });
});

    expect(scanRefs('\u00e9![a](a.png)', { maxBytes: 13 })).toMatchObject({ outcome: 'scanned', images: ['a.png'] });
    expect(scanRefs('\u00e9![a](a.png)', { maxBytes: 12 })).toEqual(OVER);

(a) Create `src/render/scan.ts` with exactly this content (ASCII only):

```ts
// scanRefs() (docserver L1; architecture section C, the "scanRefs" row; rulings C2 and C3). What a host
// needs to know about a document before it renders it: the images render() will show and the sizes of the
// Mermaid sources it will turn into figures. It parses with render()'s own engine and renders nothing;
// markdown-it's parse runs the whole core chain, so the token stream is the one render() renders.
// 1. The byte gate, render()'s: over `maxBytes` UTF-8 bytes nothing is parsed and the outcome is
//    'over-limit', with no images and no fences, so an over-limit scan is never read as an empty one.
// 2. One leading U+FEFF is removed (PD4), as render() removes it, so both parse the same text.
// 3. images: the `src` of every image token render() writes, in document order, each source once. The value
//    is the token's attribute, which markdown-it's normalizeLink has already encoded (`<a b>` is `a%20b`),
//    so it is exactly what render() writes before escaping it for HTML. Images are read where render()
//    writes them: in the children of each inline token (a footnote's too: footnote_tail has moved each
//    referenced note into the stream and dropped the others), and in the caption the figcaption rule took
//    out of the stream (FenceMeta.inline). An image's own children are its alt, which render() writes as
//    text, so an image inside an alt is never read. At most `maxImages` distinct sources are kept; when
//    another distinct source exists, `imagesTruncated` is true, so a cut list is never read as a whole one.
// 4. mermaid: the fences render() turns into figures, by renderFence's own test (fenceName(info) is exactly
//    MERMAID), counted with the UTF-8 sizes of their sources (the fence content the figure writes escaped).
import type { MarkdownIt, Token } from 'markdown-it';
import { createEnv } from './env.js';
import { fenceName, MERMAID, type FenceMeta } from './fence.js';
import { utf8Length } from './pyText.js';
import { checkLimit, ENGINE, stripBom } from './render.js';
import { DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES, DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES, type ScanRefsOptions, type ScanRefsResult } from './types.js';

/** What one scan has found so far. */
interface Scan {
  readonly maxImages: number;
  /** The distinct sources kept, at most maxImages; a Set keeps them in the order they were first seen. */
  readonly images: Set<string>;
  imagesTruncated: boolean;
  fences: number;
  largestBytes: number;
  totalBytes: number;
}

/** A fence's size is counted to the end: the whole input is already under maxBytes. */
const UNCAPPED = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;

function addImage(s: Scan, src: string): void {
  if (s.images.has(src)) return;
  if (s.images.size < s.maxImages) s.images.add(src);
  else s.imagesTruncated = true;
}

/** The images among one inline token's children, in order. An image's own children (its alt) are not read. */
function scanInline(children: readonly Token[], s: Scan): void {
  for (const t of children) {
    if (t.type === 'image') addImage(s, t.attrGet('src') ?? '');
  }
}

/** A fence that renders a Mermaid figure: its size, then the images of its caption, which follow its source. */
function scanFence(t: Token, s: Scan): void {
  if (fenceName(t.info) !== MERMAID) return;
  const bytes = utf8Length(t.content, UNCAPPED);
  s.fences += 1;
  s.totalBytes += bytes;
  s.largestBytes = Math.max(s.largestBytes, bytes);
  const caption = (t.meta as FenceMeta | null)?.inline;
  if (caption !== undefined) scanInline(caption, s);
}

/**
 * scanRefs() with an explicit engine. Internal: tests inject an engine here to show the scan renders nothing.
 * Throws RangeError for an invalid `maxBytes` or `maxImages`.
 */
export function scanWith(markdown: string, o: ScanRefsOptions | undefined, engine: MarkdownIt): ScanRefsResult {
  const maxBytes = checkLimit('scanRefs', 'maxBytes', o?.maxBytes ?? DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES);
  const maxImages = checkLimit('scanRefs', 'maxImages', o?.maxImages ?? DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES);
  if (utf8Length(markdown, maxBytes) > maxBytes) {
    return {
      outcome: 'over-limit',
      images: [],
      imagesTruncated: false,
      mermaid: { fences: 0, largestBytes: 0, totalBytes: 0 },
    };
  }
  const s: Scan = { maxImages, images: new Set(), imagesTruncated: false, fences: 0, largestBytes: 0, totalBytes: 0 };
  for (const t of engine.parse(stripBom(markdown), createEnv({ lineAttrs: true }))) {
    if (t.type === 'inline') scanInline(t.children ?? [], s);
    else if (t.type === 'fence') scanFence(t, s);
  }
  return {
    outcome: 'scanned',
    images: [...s.images],
    imagesTruncated: s.imagesTruncated,
    mermaid: { fences: s.fences, largestBytes: s.largestBytes, totalBytes: s.totalBytes },
  };
}

/** The images and Mermaid sizes render() would show for `markdown`, from a parse alone. Pure and deterministic. */
export function scanRefs(markdown: string, o?: ScanRefsOptions): ScanRefsResult {
  return scanWith(markdown, o, ENGINE);
}
```

/** The engine render() and scanRefs() share. Internal: index.ts never exports it. */
export const ENGINE = createEngine();

/** U+FEFF, removed once from the start of the input (PD4). */
const BOM = 0xfeff;

/** The input without one leading U+FEFF (PD4): the text render() and scanRefs() parse. */
export function stripBom(markdown: string): string {
  return markdown.charCodeAt(0) === BOM ? markdown.substring(1) : markdown;
}

/** A limit option, checked: a non-negative safe integer, or a RangeError naming the function and the option. */
export function checkLimit(fn: string, name: string, value: number): number {
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value) || value < 0) {
    throw new RangeError(`${fn}: ${name} must be a non-negative safe integer, got ${String(value)}`);
  }
  return value;
}

**Decisions this task makes:**
1. **What each verdict arm means** (`evaluateVerdict`, all on the raw html `render()` returned, so a consumer's highlighter markup is judged too):
   - `outcome` equal, and an `over-limit` render must have empty html (the render contract, section C rule 1).
   - `maxMs`: the render call's wall-clock time is at most `maxMs × timeScale`.
   - `maxOutputRatio`: UTF-8 bytes of html over UTF-8 bytes of input, an empty input counting as one byte.
   - `maxTagDepth`: per element name, the deepest nesting of that element's own tags; other elements and self-closing tags do not count.
   - `forbid`: no string occurs, compared with ASCII letters folded (`<SCRIPT` is `<script`), never with Unicode case mapping (U+212A is not `k` here). Every `<` and `"` that is text is escaped, so a forbidden `<x` or `x="` only ever matches markup the renderer wrote; that is why the attribute forms read ` onerror="` and not `onerror=`, which the escaped text legitimately holds.
   - `require`: every string occurs exactly as written.
   - `balanced`: per element, as many closers as openers, and no closer before its opener.
   - `headingIds`: the `<hN id>` values of the html, entity-decoded, are exactly `base`, `base-1`, … `base-(count-1)`.
   - `scan` (new, Task 10's hand-over): `scanRefs(input)` returns at most `maxImages` images, `imagesTruncated` exactly as stated, and an outcome matching `render()`'s.
   - `nullPrototypeFront` (new, section E row 31's "`Object.getPrototypeOf(meta.front) === null`"): `meta.front` is a record whose prototype is null; JSON comparison of meta cannot see a prototype.
   - `exact` is bookkeeping: the case also has a golden, which `runCorpus` already compares; `crossCheck` requires it on every hostile case and refuses it on a generated one.
   `parseVerdict` refuses any other key and any malformed value, so a typo in `hostile.json` is a load error, never an arm that silently checks nothing.
2. **`hostile.json` is an array of `{id, input?, verdict}` in manifest order**, one entry per hostile case (no `input`: its input is `conformance/corpus/<id>.md`; `exact: true`; outcome `rendered`) and one per generated case (with `input`, never `exact`). `loadCorpus` refuses a file that disagrees with the manifest (`crossCheck`), so a hostile case cannot lose its verdict by losing its entry. The file is ASCII only (non-ASCII text is a JSON escape) and formatted one key per line, so a diff shows one verdict per line.
3. **A generated input is a spec, built on the consumer's machine.** `{parts: [{text, times?, index?}]}`: each part's text repeated `times` times, and with `index`, every marker in the text replaced by the repetition's number from 0 (`![i](@.png)` × 10000 gives 10000 distinct sources without a 150 KB file). `inputSize` computes the UTF-8 size from the spec alone (the digits of 0 … n-1 counted arithmetically), so a spec over 8 MiB is refused before anything is allocated; a repetition count over 8 MiB is refused before any arithmetic, because every repetition writes at least one byte. `loadCorpus` caps the total of all generated inputs at 8 MiB as well (section E: "The total is capped at 8 MiB"); the shipped total is 8180557 bytes.
4. **The 25 generated cases.** Section E's seven rows expand to 16 cases, ruling C11 adds two, and seven more give a bound of Tasks 3, 5, 6 and 8, or a depth, a verdict a consumer's run checks (the last seven rows):

   Where section E names a family but not its inputs, the inputs are the classic CommonMark pathological shapes (openers without closers, closers without openers, nested brackets, backtick runs). `x-limits/over-limit` uses the default cap, so it also pins `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` for any consumer's render, and its last character straddles the cap.
5. **The hostile cases' verdicts** follow section E's "Pins (verdict)" column, each checked against the case's golden: `forbid` lists for script, style, iframe, svg, img and the `on*` attribute forms; `require` for the escaped text that proves a spoof stayed text (`title="c&quot; onerror=x"`, the `themeCSS` directive inside `<pre class="mermaid">`, the ids of `h-dom-clobber-names`); `balanced` and `maxTagDepth.details ≤ 50` on `h-details-hostile`; on `h-anchor-after-summary-nested` (decision 12), `forbid` of the empty paragraph ruling C13 found and `require` of the anchor after the summary; `maxTagDepth.blockquote ≤ 20` on `h-alert-caption-spoof`; `nullPrototypeFront` on `proto-keys`; `forbid: <dl` where front matter must render nothing (`yaml-tags`, `oversize`); `maxOutputRatio` on `alias-bomb` and `oversize`. Every hostile case has `maxMs: 1000` and `exact: true`.
6. **How the numbers were set (section E, "Timing").** `maxMs = max(1000, 10 × the median of five runs)`, rounded up to 100 ms; `maxOutputRatio` is the smallest integer at least 1.25 × the measured ratio (at least 1). Every small hostile case measured at most 3.1 ms; `alias-bomb` 0.944 (bound 2), `oversize` 0.001 (bound 1). A later machine measures different times; the bounds are backstops, the structural arms are the guard, and a slow runner passes `timeScale`, never a looser `hostile.json` (the ratchet refuses one).
7. **`runCorpus` judges three kinds of case.** A golden case as before (outcome `rendered`, html, meta, oracle). A hostile case by its golden, its verdict (whose `outcome` replaces the golden's own outcome line, so a wrong outcome is reported once) and the oracle. A generated case by its verdict and the oracle alone. `scanRefs` is an option because `runCorpus` judges a render function; a `scanRefs` that throws becomes the scan arm's line (`scan: scanRefs threw: …`), not an exception. `timeScale` must be a positive finite number. Section F T3's `timing` option is not added: a switch that turns `maxMs` off would make a run report ok with an arm unchecked, and `timeScale` already serves a slow machine.
8. **The ratchet.** `compareVerdicts(base, head)` walks base's entries: present in head; `input` deep-equal (a changed input is a weakening in disguise, so a new input is a new case); `outcome` equal; `maxMs`, `maxOutputRatio`, each `maxTagDepth` entry and `scan.maxImages` present and not raised; `forbid`, `require` and `balanced` supersets; `exact` and `nullPrototypeFront` kept; `headingIds` and `scan.imagesTruncated` equal. Any key outside its own `VERDICT_KEYS` copy is refused on every head entry, and a test pins that copy equal to `verdict.ts`'s, so a new arm cannot pass the ratchet unexamined. `checkGoldenMoves(changed, named)` reds an id whose expected files changed and no trailer names, and an id a trailer names whose files did not change. `checkHostileInputs(base, changed)` reds a hostile case of the base whose input file, `conformance/corpus/<id>.md`, changed: a verdict guards its input, so editing the input is a weakened verdict in disguise exactly as a changed input spec is, and the way forward is a new case. The command diffs `<base>...HEAD` (from the merge base, so a golden moved on the base branch after the fork is not the branch's) with `--no-renames`, reads trailers with git's own parser (`%(trailers:key=Goldens-moved,valueonly,unfold)` over `<base>..HEAD`, so a trailer only counts in the final trailer block, exactly where Tasks 2 and 9 put theirs), diffs `conformance/corpus/` the same way for `checkHostileInputs`, reads the working tree's `hostile.json` as head, treats a base without `hostile.json` as an empty one, and fails (exit 1, the parse error) on a base whose `hostile.json` does not parse rather than reading it as empty. `scripts/ratchet.d.mts` types it for the tests, because `tsconfig.json` does not allow JavaScript.
9. **The pending hand-over, measured.** All 25 generated cases and the new hostile case pass when they arrive, so none is pending; `test/corpus-pending.json` stays `{}` and a label may now only be `T12`.
10. **Existing tests touched.** `test/scan.test.ts` skips generated cases: two of them do not render by design (`x-limits/over-limit` is over the byte cap and `x-limits/html-expansion` over `maxHtmlBytes`), and its invariants are for documents that render; `test/fence.test.ts` reads `c?.expected?.meta`; `test/lineattrs.test.ts` is unchanged and now also runs over the 25 generated cases and the new hostile case (26 more passing tests); `test/expected.test.ts` and `test/scan.test.ts` also run over the new hostile case.
11. **What section F asks for that differs here.**
   - M11.6's mutation ("count only opening tags at depth 1") is written as "a closing tag does not decrement" (row M6): that is the one-line way to stop counting nesting, and it reds both `verdict.test.ts` and two shipped verdicts.
   - Section F T3's M3.2 and M3.4 reds arrive here as rows M7 (`maxNesting: 100` reds `x-blockquote-10000`) and M36 (a loosened byte gate reds `x-limits/over-limit`).
   - The wiring of `crossCheck` and `sumInputSizes` into `loadCorpus` is guarded through data (row M33 removes one `exact` from `hostile.json` and `loadCorpus` refuses the corpus); with consistent shipped files, removing the wiring alone reds nothing, and `loadCorpus` takes no injected files. The functions themselves have their own rows (M20, M21).
   - The ratchet's CI step is Task 12's (section F T12, "CI steps added"); `ci.yml` is unchanged.
12. **Ruling C13's corpus case is a hostile case, added here.** Task 5 fixed the bug and pinned it with two unit cases; the corpus case puts ruling C13's own input in front of every consumer's render, and hostile cases get their verdicts in this task. Its id carries the `h-` prefix of every hostile case, and it is listed after `h-alert-caption-spoof` in `manifest.json` and in `hostile.json`, whose orders must agree. Its input is the ruling's four lines and holds no non-ASCII byte; its reference comes from Task 2's generator (`--only`) and its expected files from `UPDATE_EXPECTED=1`, because it departs from nothing. Its verdict pins what C13 is about: the empty paragraph is forbidden, the anchor after the summary is required, and the html is compared exactly. Rows M37-M39 red it through the fix, its golden and its verdict.
13. **Allowlisted tags nest at most 64 deep (ruling C21, departure PD8).** Blockquotes stop at `maxNesting` 20, and Task 5 caps `<details>`, `<sup>`, `<sub>` and `<kbd>` at 64 open levels each: an opener past the cap, and the closer that pairs with it, stay escaped text. Without the cap, 10000 unclosed `<details>` lines became 10000 nested `<details open>` and 100000 `<sup>` nested 100000 deep, which a consumer that walks the fragment recursively, or parses it with a DOM library that has no depth limit, could not survive. `x-details-10000-unclosed` and `x-inline-unclosed/sup-100000` pin the cap in `maxTagDepth` (64) and `require` the first escaped opener, so a raised or lost cap reds the corpus (row M48), and the ratchet lets the bound only tighten.
14. **The html bound gets a generated case (ruling C20, departure PD8).** `x-limits/html-expansion` is the 304 KB input that rendered 200 MB of html as `rendered`. At the default `maxHtmlBytes` (16 MiB) `render()` stops with outcome `output-over-limit` and returns the escaped-source fallback, so the verdict requires that outcome and the fallback's opening and forbids `<a `; its output ratio is 1. `verdict.ts` lists the outcomes a verdict may name in `OUTCOME_WORDS`, typed by `RenderOutcome`, so a later outcome word cannot be left out of `parseVerdict` without a type error. Rows M46 (the word), M47 (the bound) and M48 (the cap) red these through the corpus; Task 3's and Task 5's rows red the code itself.

(a) Create `test/hostile-input.test.ts` with exactly this content:

```ts
// Generated hostile inputs and the hostile.json index (docserver L1, Task 11; architecture sections D, E and F).
// buildInput builds a generated case's input from its spec, deterministically; inputSize measures a spec
// without building it, so a spec over 8 MiB is refused before anything is allocated, and loadCorpus caps the
// total of all generated inputs the same way. parseHostile reads hostile.json and crossCheck ties it to the
// manifest: one verdict per hostile and generated case, an input spec exactly for a generated one.
import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  buildInput,
  crossCheck,
  inputSize,
  MAX_INPUT_BYTES,
  parseHostile,
  sumInputSizes,
  type HostileEntry,
  type InputSpec,
} from '../src/conformance/hostile.js';

const readJson = (rel: string): unknown => JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL(rel, import.meta.url), 'utf8'));
const MiB = 1024 * 1024;
const RENDERED = { outcome: 'rendered' } as const;

describe('buildInput', () => {
  it('concatenates the parts in order, each repeated `times` times (default once)', () => {
    expect(buildInput({ parts: [{ text: 'ab', times: 3 }, { text: '\n' }, { text: '> ', times: 2 }] })).toBe(
      'ababab\n> > ',
    );
  });

  it('replaces every index marker by the repetition number, from 0', () => {
    expect(buildInput({ parts: [{ text: '![i](@.png)\n', times: 3, index: '@' }] })).toBe(
      '![i](0.png)\n![i](1.png)\n![i](2.png)\n',
    );
    expect(buildInput({ parts: [{ text: 'x#y#', times: 2, index: '#' }] })).toBe('x0y0x1y1');
    expect(buildInput({ parts: [{ text: '@', times: 12, index: '@' }] })).toBe('01234567891011');
  });

  it('is deterministic', () => {
    const spec: InputSpec = { parts: [{ text: '[^@] ', times: 500, index: '@' }, { text: '*', times: 99 }] };
    expect(buildInput(spec)).toBe(buildInput(spec));
  });
});

describe('inputSize: the UTF-8 size of a spec, without building it', () => {
  const specs: InputSpec[] = [
    { parts: [{ text: 'a', times: 7 }] },
    { parts: [{ text: '\u00e9\u4e2d', times: 3 }, { text: '\ud83d\ude00' }] },
    { parts: [{ text: '<@>', times: 1001, index: '@' }] },
    { parts: [{ text: '@\u00e9@', times: 10, index: '@' }, { text: 'x', times: 100000 }] },
    { parts: [{ text: '\u00e9 ', times: 120, index: '\u00e9' }] },
  ];
  for (const [i, spec] of specs.entries()) {
    it(`spec ${i}: equals the built input's byte length`, () => {
      expect(inputSize(spec)).toBe(Buffer.byteLength(buildInput(spec), 'utf8'));
    });
  }
});

describe('the 8 MiB cap', () => {
  it('a spec of exactly 8 MiB is built', () => {
    const s = buildInput({ parts: [{ text: 'a', times: MAX_INPUT_BYTES }] });
    expect(MAX_INPUT_BYTES).toBe(8 * MiB);
    expect(s.length).toBe(MAX_INPUT_BYTES);
  });

  it('a 9 MiB spec is refused', () => {
    expect(() => buildInput({ parts: [{ text: 'a', times: 9 * MiB }] })).toThrow(RangeError);
    expect(() => buildInput({ parts: [{ text: 'ab', times: 4 * MiB }, { text: 'c' }] })).toThrow(
      /input spec: 8388609 bytes, over the 8388608-byte cap/,
    );
  });

  it('a repetition count over the cap is refused before any arithmetic', () => {
    expect(() => inputSize({ parts: [{ text: 'a', times: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER }] })).toThrow(
      /parts\[0\]\.times is 9007199254740991, over the 8388608-byte cap/,
    );
  });

  it('the total of several specs is capped too', () => {
    const five: InputSpec = { parts: [{ text: 'a', times: 5 * MiB }] };
    expect(sumInputSizes([five])).toBe(5 * MiB);
    expect(() => sumInputSizes([five, five])).toThrow(/generated inputs total 10485760 bytes, over the 8388608-byte cap/);
  });
});

describe('an invalid spec is refused', () => {
  const bad: [string, unknown, RegExp][] = [
    ['no parts', {}, /must be \{parts/],
    ['empty parts', { parts: [] }, /must be \{parts/],
    ['an extra key', { parts: [{ text: 'a' }], seed: 1 }, /must be \{parts/],
    ['a part that is not an object', { parts: ['a'] }, /parts\[0\] is not an object/],
    ['an unknown part key', { parts: [{ text: 'a', repeat: 2 }] }, /unknown keys: repeat/],
    ['empty text', { parts: [{ text: '' }] }, /text must be a non-empty string/],
    ['zero times', { parts: [{ text: 'a', times: 0 }] }, /times must be a safe integer of at least 1/],
    ['fractional times', { parts: [{ text: 'a', times: 1.5 }] }, /times must be/],
    ['an empty index', { parts: [{ text: 'a', index: '' }] }, /index must be a non-empty string/],
    ['an index not in its text', { parts: [{ text: 'a', times: 2, index: '@' }] }, /does not occur in its text/],
  ];
  for (const [name, spec, message] of bad) {
    it(name, () => {
      expect(() => buildInput(spec as InputSpec)).toThrow(message);
    });
  }
});

describe('parseHostile', () => {
  it('reads entries, with or without an input spec', () => {
    const raw = [
      { id: 'h', verdict: { ...RENDERED, exact: true } },

  const bad: [string, unknown, RegExp][] = [

    ['no id', [{ verdict: RENDERED }], /entry 0 has no id/],
    ['an id twice', [{ id: 'a', verdict: RENDERED }, { id: 'a', verdict: RENDERED }], /a appears twice/],
    ['a bad verdict', [{ id: 'a', verdict: { outcome: 'fine' } }], /hostile\.json: a: outcome must be/],
    ['a bad input', [{ id: 'a', input: { parts: [] }, verdict: RENDERED }], /input spec/],
    ['an input over the cap', [{ id: 'a', input: { parts: [{ text: 'a', times: 9 * MiB }] }, verdict: RENDERED }], /cap/],
  ];
  for (const [name, raw, message] of bad) {

describe('crossCheck: hostile.json against the manifest', () => {
  const spec: InputSpec = { parts: [{ text: 'a' }] };
  const cases = [

  const good: HostileEntry[] = [

  ];

  it('agrees when every hostile and generated case has its entry', () => {
    expect(crossCheck(cases, good)).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('names every disagreement', () => {
    expect(
      crossCheck(cases, [
        { id: 'g0', verdict: RENDERED },
        { id: 'h1', input: spec, verdict: { outcome: 'failed' } },
        { id: 'x1', verdict: { ...RENDERED, exact: true } },
        { id: 'zz', verdict: RENDERED },
      ]),
    ).toEqual([
      'g0: a golden case has no verdict',
      'h1: a hostile case reads its input from corpus/, not from a spec',
      'h1: a hostile case has a golden, so its verdict says exact: true',
      'h1: a hostile case with a golden must render',
      'x1: a generated case needs an input spec',
      'x1: a generated case has no golden, so no exact',
      'zz: in hostile.json but not in the manifest',
    ]);
    expect(crossCheck(cases, [])).toEqual([
      'h1: a hostile case needs a verdict in hostile.json',
      'x1: a generated case needs a verdict in hostile.json',
    ]);
  });
});

describe('the shipped hostile.json', () => {
  const manifest = readJson('../conformance/manifest.json') as { id: string; kind: string }[];
  const entries = parseHostile(readJson('../conformance/hostile.json'));

  it('agrees with the manifest: 15 hostile and 25 generated cases', () => {
    expect(crossCheck(manifest, entries)).toEqual([]);
    expect(entries.filter((e) => e.input === undefined)).toHaveLength(15);
    expect(entries.filter((e) => e.input !== undefined)).toHaveLength(25);
  });

  it('lists its entries in manifest order', () => {
    const order = manifest.filter((c) => c.kind !== 'golden').map((c) => c.id);
    expect(entries.map((e) => e.id)).toEqual(order);
  });

  it('the generated inputs total under the cap', () => {
    const specs = entries.flatMap((e) => (e.input === undefined ? [] : [e.input]));
    const total = sumInputSizes(specs);
    expect(total).toBe(specs.reduce((sum, s) => sum + Buffer.byteLength(buildInput(s), 'utf8'), 0));
    expect(total).toBeLessThanOrEqual(MAX_INPUT_BYTES);
  });

  it('is ASCII only: every other character is written as a \\u escape', () => {
    const text = readFileSync(new URL('../conformance/hostile.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8');
    expect([...text].filter((ch) => ch > '~' || (ch < ' ' && ch !== '\n'))).toEqual([]);
  });
});

(b) Create `test/verdict.test.ts` with exactly this content:

```ts
// Verdicts (docserver L1, Task 11; architecture sections D, E and F). Each arm of evaluateVerdict, passing and
// failing, on hand-written html; parseVerdict's refusals; and the verdict key list, which scripts/ratchet.mjs
// keeps a copy of. Every non-ASCII character is written as a \u escape.
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { VERDICT_KEYS as RATCHET_KEYS } from '../scripts/ratchet.mjs';
import {
  evaluateVerdict,
  imbalance,
  parseVerdict,
  tagDepth,
  VERDICT_KEYS,
  type Verdict,
  type VerdictContext,
} from '../src/conformance/verdict.js';
import type { RenderMeta, RenderResult, ScanRefsResult } from '../src/render/types.js';

const META: RenderMeta = {
  front: null,
  frontList: null,
  title: null,
  headings: [],
  figures: 0,
  tables: 0,
  mermaidKinds: [],
};

function result(html: string, over: Partial<RenderResult> = {}): RenderResult {
  return { html, outcome: 'rendered', bytes: 0, meta: META, ...over };
}

/** The failures of `verdict` on `html` (outcome 'rendered', input 'abcd', 1 ms unless given). */
function judge(verdict: Omit<Verdict, 'outcome'> & { outcome?: Verdict['outcome'] }, html: string, ctx: VerdictContext = { ms: 1 }, input = 'abcd'): string[] {
  return evaluateVerdict(result(html), input, { outcome: 'rendered', ...verdict }, ctx);
}

const SCAN: ScanRefsResult = {
  outcome: 'scanned',
  images: Array.from({ length: 512 }, (_, i) => `${i}.png`),
  imagesTruncated: true,
  mermaid: { fences: 0, largestBytes: 0, totalBytes: 0 },
};

describe('outcome', () => {
  it('must equal the render outcome', () => {
    expect(judge({}, '<p>a</p>')).toEqual([]);
    expect(judge({ outcome: 'failed' }, '<p>a</p>')).toEqual(['outcome: expected "failed", got "rendered"']);
  });

  it('an over-limit render has empty html', () => {
    const over = (html: string): string[] =>
      evaluateVerdict(result(html, { outcome: 'over-limit' }), 'x', { outcome: 'over-limit' }, { ms: 1 });
    expect(over('')).toEqual([]);
    expect(over('<p>')).toEqual(['outcome: an over-limit render has empty html, got 3 characters']);
  });
});

describe('maxMs', () => {
  it('bounds the render time, the bound included', () => {
    expect(judge({ maxMs: 1000 }, '', { ms: 1000 })).toEqual([]);
    expect(judge({ maxMs: 1000 }, '', { ms: 1000.5 })).toEqual(['maxMs: took 1000.5 ms, bound 1000 ms']);
    expect(judge({ maxMs: 1000 }, '', { ms: Number.NaN })).toEqual(['maxMs: took NaN ms, bound 1000 ms']);
  });

  it('timeScale multiplies the bound, never the verdict', () => {
    expect(judge({ maxMs: 1000 }, '', { ms: 1500, timeScale: 2 })).toEqual([]);
    expect(judge({ maxMs: 1000 }, '', { ms: 600, timeScale: 0.5 })).toEqual(['maxMs: took 600.0 ms, bound 500 ms']);
  });
});

describe('maxOutputRatio', () => {
  it('bounds UTF-8 output bytes over UTF-8 input bytes', () => {
    expect(judge({ maxOutputRatio: 2 }, 'x'.repeat(8))).toEqual([]);
    expect(judge({ maxOutputRatio: 2 }, 'x'.repeat(9))).toEqual([
      'maxOutputRatio: output is 2.250 times the input, bound 2',
    ]);
    expect(judge({ maxOutputRatio: 2 }, '\u00e9\u00e9', { ms: 1 }, '\u00e9')).toEqual([]);
    expect(judge({ maxOutputRatio: 2 }, '\u00e9\u00e9a', { ms: 1 }, '\u00e9')).toEqual([
      'maxOutputRatio: output is 2.500 times the input, bound 2',
    ]);
  });

  it('an empty input counts as one byte', () => {
    expect(judge({ maxOutputRatio: 3 }, 'abc', { ms: 1 }, '')).toEqual([]);
    expect(judge({ maxOutputRatio: 3 }, 'abcd', { ms: 1 }, '')).toEqual([
      'maxOutputRatio: output is 4.000 times the input, bound 3',
    ]);
  });
});

describe('maxTagDepth', () => {
  it('is the deepest nesting of one element, siblings and other elements apart', () => {
    expect(tagDepth('<blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n</blockquote>\n</blockquote>\n<blockquote>\n</blockquote>', 'blockquote')).toBe(2);
    expect(tagDepth('<em>a</em><em>b</em><em>c</em>', 'em')).toBe(1);
    expect(tagDepth('<div><p><div data-line="1-1"></div></p></div>', 'div')).toBe(2);
    expect(tagDepth('<details open>\n<details>\n', 'details')).toBe(2);
    expect(tagDepth('<br /><br /><br />', 'br')).toBe(0);
    expect(tagDepth('<p>&lt;em&gt;&lt;em&gt;</p>', 'em')).toBe(0);
    expect(tagDepth('<emph><em></em></emph>', 'em')).toBe(1);
  });

  it('fails each element over its bound', () => {
    const html = '<blockquote><blockquote><em><em>x</em></em></blockquote></blockquote>';
    expect(judge({ maxTagDepth: { blockquote: 2, em: 2 } }, html)).toEqual([]);
    expect(judge({ maxTagDepth: { blockquote: 1, em: 1 } }, html)).toEqual([
      'maxTagDepth: blockquote nests 2 deep, bound 1',
      'maxTagDepth: em nests 2 deep, bound 1',
    ]);
  });
});

describe('forbid', () => {
  it('fails on a forbidden string in any ASCII case', () => {
    expect(judge({ forbid: ['<script'] }, '<p>&lt;script&gt;</p>')).toEqual([]);
    expect(judge({ forbid: ['<script'] }, '<p><SCRIPT>')).toEqual(['forbid: the html contains "<script"']);
    expect(judge({ forbid: ['<SCRIPT', ' onerror="'] }, '<script> <img onError="x">')).toEqual([
      'forbid: the html contains "<SCRIPT"',
      'forbid: the html contains " onerror=\\""',
    ]);
  });

  it('folds ASCII letters only', () => {
    // U+212A KELVIN SIGN lower-cases to k in Unicode, but it is not markup.
    expect(judge({ forbid: ['<kbd'] }, '<p>&lt;\u212abd&gt;</p><\u212abd')).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('require', () => {
  it('fails on a missing string, compared exactly', () => {
    expect(judge({ require: ['<p>A</p>'] }, '<p>A</p>')).toEqual([]);
    expect(judge({ require: ['<p>a</p>', '<p>A'] }, '<p>A</p>')).toEqual(['require: the html lacks "<p>a</p>"']);
  });
});

describe('balanced', () => {
  it('passes when every opening tag has its closer, in order', () => {
    expect(imbalance('<details open>\n<details>\n</details>\n</details>\n', 'details')).toBeNull();
    expect(judge({ balanced: ['details', 'div'] }, '<div><details></details></div>')).toEqual([]);

  it('fails on a missing closer and on a closer before its opener', () => {

    ]);

describe('headingIds', () => {
  const html = '<h1 id="a">a</h1>\n<h2 id="a-1" data-line="3-3">a</h2>\n<h6 id="a-2">a</h6>\n';

  it('the ids are base, base-1, base-2, in order', () => {

  });

    expect(judge({ headingIds: { base: 'a', count: 3 } }, html.replace('a-1', 'a-9'))).toEqual([
      'headingIds: heading 1 has id "a-9", expected "a-1"',
    ]);
    expect(judge({ headingIds: { base: 'b', count: 3 } }, html)).toEqual([
      'headingIds: heading 0 has id "a", expected "b"',
    ]);
  });
});

describe('scan', () => {
  const want = { maxImages: 512, imagesTruncated: true };

  it('passes when scanRefs reports at most maxImages and the stated truncation', () => {
    expect(judge({ scan: want }, '', { ms: 1, scan: SCAN })).toEqual([]);

    ]);
  });
});

```ts
// The verdict ratchet and the golden-move rule (docserver L1, Task 11; architecture section D). The pure
// functions of scripts/ratchet.mjs, one case per kind of weakening and the tightenings that pass; then the
// command itself, run with this Node against throwaway git repositories made in the system temp directory
// (git's global and system configuration are ignored there, and nothing is pushed or fetched).
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { afterAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  checkGoldenMoves,
  checkHostileInputs,
  compareVerdicts,
  expectedIds,
  parseTrailerIds,
  type RatchetEntry,
} from '../scripts/ratchet.mjs';

const BASE: RatchetEntry[] = [
  {
    id: 'h-case',
    verdict: { outcome: 'rendered', maxMs: 1000, forbid: ['<script', '<img'], require: ['<p>'], balanced: ['details'], exact: true },
  },
  {
    id: 'x-case',
    input: { parts: [{ text: '> ', times: 10 }] },
    verdict: {
      outcome: 'rendered',
      maxMs: 2000,
      maxOutputRatio: 4,
      maxTagDepth: { blockquote: 20, em: 5 },
      headingIds: { base: 'a', count: 3 },
      scan: { maxImages: 512, imagesTruncated: true },
      nullPrototypeFront: true,
    },
  },
];

/** BASE with one entry's verdict changed: `set` merged in, `drop` keys removed. */
function edit(id: string, set: Record<string, unknown>, drop: string[] = []): RatchetEntry[] {
  return BASE.map((e) => {
    if (e.id !== id) return e;
    const verdict: Record<string, unknown> = { ...e.verdict, ...set };
    for (const k of drop) delete verdict[k];
    return { ...e, verdict };
  });
}

describe('compareVerdicts: every weakening is refused', () => {
  const cases: [string, RatchetEntry[], string][] = [
    ['removed case', BASE.slice(0, 1), 'x-case: removed (a hostile or generated case is never removed)'],
    ['raised maxMs', edit('x-case', { maxMs: 2001 }), 'x-case: maxMs raised from 2000 to 2001'],
    ['removed maxMs', edit('h-case', {}, ['maxMs']), 'h-case: maxMs removed'],
    ['raised maxOutputRatio', edit('x-case', { maxOutputRatio: 4.5 }), 'x-case: maxOutputRatio raised from 4 to 4.5'],
    ['raised maxTagDepth', edit('x-case', { maxTagDepth: { blockquote: 21, em: 5 } }), 'x-case: maxTagDepth.blockquote raised from 20 to 21'],
    ['removed maxTagDepth entry', edit('x-case', { maxTagDepth: { blockquote: 20 } }), 'x-case: maxTagDepth.em removed'],
    ['shrunk forbid', edit('h-case', { forbid: ['<script'] }), 'h-case: forbid lost "<img"'],
    ['shrunk require', edit('h-case', {}, ['require']), 'h-case: require lost "<p>"'],
    ['shrunk balanced', edit('h-case', { balanced: [] }), 'h-case: balanced lost "details"'],
    ['changed outcome', edit('h-case', { outcome: 'failed' }), 'h-case: outcome changed from rendered to failed'],
    ['dropped exact', edit('h-case', {}, ['exact']), 'h-case: exact dropped'],
    ['dropped nullPrototypeFront', edit('x-case', {}, ['nullPrototypeFront']), 'x-case: nullPrototypeFront dropped'],
    ['changed headingIds', edit('x-case', { headingIds: { base: 'a', count: 2 } }), 'x-case: headingIds changed'],
    ['removed scan', edit('x-case', {}, ['scan']), 'x-case: scan removed'],
    ['raised scan.maxImages', edit('x-case', { scan: { maxImages: 513, imagesTruncated: true } }), 'x-case: scan.maxImages raised from 512 to 513'],
    ['changed scan.imagesTruncated', edit('x-case', { scan: { maxImages: 512, imagesTruncated: false } }), 'x-case: scan.imagesTruncated changed'],
    ['changed input', BASE.map((e) => (e.input === undefined ? e : { ...e, input: { parts: [{ text: '> ', times: 9 }] } })), 'x-case: input changed (add a new case instead)'],
    ['unknown key', edit('h-case', { maxDepth: 3 }), 'h-case: unknown verdict key "maxDepth" (teach scripts/ratchet.mjs first)'],
  ];
  for (const [name, head, line] of cases) {
    it(name, () => {
      expect(compareVerdicts(BASE, head)).toEqual([line]);
    });
  }

  it('an unknown key is refused on a new case too', () => {
    const head = [...BASE, { id: 'x-new', input: { parts: [{ text: 'a' }] }, verdict: { outcome: 'rendered', fast: true } }];
    expect(compareVerdicts(BASE, head)).toEqual(['x-new: unknown verdict key "fast" (teach scripts/ratchet.mjs first)']);
  });
});

describe('the shipped hostile.json', () => {

describe('the ratchet command', () => {
  const RATCHET = fileURLToPath(new URL('../scripts/ratchet.mjs', import.meta.url));
  const dirs: string[] = [];
  // Git sees no global or system configuration and none of this process's GIT_* variables.
  const env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {
    ...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(process.env).filter(([k]) => !k.startsWith('GIT_'))),
    GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: '/dev/null',
    GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1',
    GIT_AUTHOR_NAME: 'Test',
    GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL: 'noreply@example.invalid',
    GIT_COMMITTER_NAME: 'Test',
    GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL: 'noreply@example.invalid',
  };

  function git(dir: string, ...args: string[]): string {
    const r = spawnSync('git', args, { cwd: dir, env, encoding: 'utf8' });
    if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')}: ${r.stderr}`);
    return r.stdout;
  }

  function repo(): string {
    const dir = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), 'docserver-ratchet-'));
    dirs.push(dir);
    git(dir, 'init', '-q', '-b', 'main');
    return dir;
  }

  function commit(dir: string, files: Record<string, string>, message: string): void {
    for (const [rel, text] of Object.entries(files)) {
      mkdirSync(path.dirname(path.join(dir, rel)), { recursive: true });
      writeFileSync(path.join(dir, rel), text);
    }
    git(dir, 'add', '-A');
    git(dir, 'commit', '-q', '-m', message);
  }

  function ratchet(dir: string, ...args: string[]): { status: number | null; out: string; err: string } {
    const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, [RATCHET, ...args], { cwd: dir, env, encoding: 'utf8' });
    return { status: r.status, out: r.stdout, err: r.stderr };
  }

  const hostile = (maxMs: number): string =>
    `${JSON.stringify([{ id: 'x-case', input: { parts: [{ text: 'a' }] }, verdict: { outcome: 'rendered', maxMs } }])}\n`;

  afterAll(() => {
    for (const dir of dirs) rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  });

  it('a first hostile.json has nothing to keep; an unchanged one keeps every verdict', () => {
    const dir = repo();
    commit(dir, { 'README.md': 'x\n' }, 'start');
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/hostile.json': hostile(1000) }, 'verdicts');
    expect(ratchet(dir, '--base', 'HEAD^')).toEqual({ status: 0, out: 'ratchet: 0 verdicts kept, 0 golden moves named\n', err: '' });
    commit(dir, { 'README.md': 'y\n' }, 'readme');
    expect(ratchet(dir, '--base', 'HEAD^')).toEqual({ status: 0, out: 'ratchet: 1 verdicts kept, 0 golden moves named\n', err: '' });
  });

  it('a weaker verdict exits 1 and names it; a tighter one passes', () => {
    const dir = repo();
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/hostile.json': hostile(1000) }, 'verdicts');
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/hostile.json': hostile(2000) }, 'looser');
    expect(ratchet(dir, '--base', 'HEAD^')).toEqual({ status: 1, out: '', err: 'ratchet: x-case: maxMs raised from 1000 to 2000\n' });
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/hostile.json': hostile(900) }, 'tighter');
    expect(ratchet(dir, '--base', 'HEAD^').status).toBe(0);
  });

  it('a moved golden needs a Goldens-moved trailer naming exactly its id', () => {
    const dir = repo();
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/hostile.json': '[]\n', 'conformance/expected/a.html': '<p>1</p>\n' }, 'start');
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/expected/a.html': '<p>2</p>\n' }, 'move a golden');
    expect(ratchet(dir, '--base', 'HEAD^')).toEqual({
      status: 1,
      out: '',
      err: 'ratchet: a: its expected files changed, and no Goldens-moved trailer names it\n',
    });
    git(dir, 'commit', '-q', '--amend', '-m', 'move a golden\n\nGoldens-moved: a, b\nCo-Authored-By: Test <noreply@example.invalid>');
    expect(ratchet(dir, '--base', 'HEAD^')).toEqual({
      status: 1,
      out: '',
      err: 'ratchet: b: a Goldens-moved trailer names it, and its expected files did not change\n',
    });
    git(dir, 'commit', '-q', '--amend', '-m', 'move a golden\n\nGoldens-moved: a\nCo-Authored-By: Test <noreply@example.invalid>');
    expect(ratchet(dir, '--base', 'HEAD^')).toEqual({ status: 0, out: 'ratchet: 0 verdicts kept, 1 golden moves named\n', err: '' });
  });

  it('on a branch, only the branch is read: a move on the base after the fork is not the branch\'s', () => {
    const dir = repo();
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/hostile.json': '[]\n', 'conformance/expected/a.html': '<p>1</p>\n' }, 'start');
    git(dir, 'checkout', '-q', '-b', 'topic');
    commit(dir, { 'README.md': 'x\n' }, 'topic work');
    git(dir, 'checkout', '-q', 'main');
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/expected/a.html': '<p>2</p>\n' }, 'move on main\n\nGoldens-moved: a');
    git(dir, 'checkout', '-q', 'topic');
    expect(ratchet(dir, '--base', 'main')).toEqual({ status: 0, out: 'ratchet: 0 verdicts kept, 0 golden moves named\n', err: '' });
  });

  it('an edited input of a hostile case exits 1 and names it; a new case beside it passes', () => {
    const dir = repo();
    const verdicts = `${JSON.stringify([{ id: 'h-case', verdict: { outcome: 'rendered', exact: true } }])}\n`;
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/hostile.json': verdicts, 'conformance/corpus/h-case.md': '<script>x</script>\n' }, 'start');
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/corpus/h-case-2.md': 'more\n' }, 'a new input');
    expect(ratchet(dir, '--base', 'HEAD^')).toEqual({ status: 0, out: 'ratchet: 1 verdicts kept, 0 golden moves named\n', err: '' });
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/corpus/h-case.md': 'x\n' }, 'weaken the input');
    expect(ratchet(dir, '--base', 'HEAD^')).toEqual({
      status: 1,
      out: '',
      err: 'ratchet: h-case: its input changed (add a new case instead)\n',
    });
  });

  it('a base hostile.json that does not parse is an error, not an empty base', () => {
    const dir = repo();
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/hostile.json': '[{' }, 'broken');
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/hostile.json': '[]\n' }, 'fixed');
    const r = ratchet(dir, '--base', 'HEAD^');
    expect(r.status).toBe(1);
    expect(r.err).toContain('SyntaxError');
  });

  it('usage errors exit 2', () => {
    const dir = repo();
    commit(dir, { 'conformance/hostile.json': '[]\n' }, 'start');
    expect(ratchet(dir)).toEqual({ status: 2, out: '', err: 'usage: node scripts/ratchet.mjs --base <git ref>\n' });
    expect(ratchet(dir, '--base', 'no-such-ref')).toEqual({ status: 2, out: '', err: 'ratchet: unknown base "no-such-ref"\n' });
  });
});

// The conformance corpus against this library's render() (docserver L1, Task 3; architecture section F,
// "How tasks hand over"). test/corpus-pending.json names the cases a later task makes pass, each with that
// task (`"T<n>"`): a pending case must FAIL, so a case that starts passing is removed from the list in the
// same change, and every other case must pass. Each task removes its own cases; Task 12 asserts the list
// is empty. The first blocks test runCorpus and loadCorpus themselves with stand-in render functions.
// Task 11 adds the verdicts of conformance/hostile.json: a hostile case is judged by its golden and its
// verdict, a generated case (built from a spec, with no golden) by its verdict alone, and the oracle runs
// on every case. Every non-ASCII character is written as a \u escape.
import { Buffer } from 'node:buffer';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

>;

/** A stand-in renderer that returns one case's expected output, plus `extra` appended to the HTML. */
function replay(id: string, extra = ''): RenderFn {
  const expected = cases.find((x) => x.id === id)?.expected;
  if (expected === undefined || expected === null) throw new Error(`no golden case ${id}`);
  return () => ({
    html: expected.html + extra,
    outcome: 'rendered',
    bytes: 0,
    meta: JSON.parse(expected.meta) as RenderMeta,
  });
}

/** A stand-in renderer that returns `html` for any input. */
function fixed(html: string): RenderFn {
  const meta = JSON.parse(cases.find((x) => x.id === 'empty-docs/empty')?.expected?.meta ?? '') as RenderMeta;
  return (): RenderResult => ({ html, outcome: 'rendered', bytes: 0, meta });
}
