(d) Create `test/pack.test.ts` with exactly this content:

```ts
// The packed package (docserver L1, Task 12; architecture section F T12). A clean copy of the checkout is built
// and packed in a temporary directory, as CI's `npm run build` and `npm pack` would, so this test never writes
// the checkout's own dist/. The tarball must hold the two entries, their types and the whole corpus a consumer's
// runCorpus reads, and nothing else: no Python references, no scripts, no sources, tests or working papers.
// Then scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs installs the tarball offline (its dependencies linked from this checkout's
// node_modules) and imports it by package name, exactly as CI's registry-installed smoke does; a second tarball
// whose packed golden was changed must fail it, naming the case. npm runs offline here, with its update check off
// and a throwaway cache, so the test touches no network. The smoke runs with --time-scale 10: test/corpus.test.ts
// holds every maxMs at scale 1, and this run judges the package, not the machine.
import { spawnSync, type SpawnSyncReturns } from 'node:child_process';
import { appendFileSync, cpSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, realpathSync, rmSync, symlinkSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('../', import.meta.url));
const TSC = path.join(ROOT, 'node_modules', 'typescript', 'bin', 'tsc');
const SMOKE = path.join(ROOT, 'scripts', 'consumer-smoke.mjs');

const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'package.json'), 'utf8')) as { name: string; version: string };
const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, 'conformance', 'manifest.json'), 'utf8')) as {
  id: string;
  kind: string;
}[];

/** The file name npm gives the tarball: the scope's @ dropped, its slash a dash, then the version. */
const TARBALL = `${pkg.name.replace(/^@/, '').replace('/', '-')}-${pkg.version}.tgz`;

/** The only places a packed file may live. */
const ALLOWED = [
  /^dist\/(?:render|conformance)\/[A-Za-z]+\.(?:js|d\.ts)$/,
  /^conformance\/(?:manifest|hostile|DEPARTURES)\.json$/,
  /^conformance\/(?:corpus|expected)\/[A-Za-z0-9/_-]+\.(?:md|html|meta\.json)$/,
  /^(?:package\.json|README\.md|LICENSE)$/,
];

interface Packed {
  filename: string;
  files: string[];
}

let work = '';
let packed: Packed = { filename: '', files: [] };
let smoke: SpawnSyncReturns<string> | null = null;
let brokenSmoke: SpawnSyncReturns<string> | null = null;

/** Run scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs with these arguments. */
function runSmoke(args: readonly string[]): SpawnSyncReturns<string> {
  return spawnSync(process.execPath, [SMOKE, ...args], { cwd: work, encoding: 'utf8' });
}

/** npm with no network: offline, no update check, no audit or funding calls, a throwaway cache. */
function npm(args: readonly string[], cwd: string): SpawnSyncReturns<string> {
  return spawnSync('npm', [...args], {
    cwd,
    encoding: 'utf8',
    env: {
      ...process.env,
      npm_config_offline: 'true',
      npm_config_update_notifier: 'false',
      npm_config_audit: 'false',
      npm_config_fund: 'false',
      npm_config_cache: path.join(work, 'npm-cache'),
    },
  });
}

beforeAll(() => {
  work = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), 'docserver-pack-'));
  const stage = path.join(work, 'stage');
  // A clean checkout: everything but git's own files, installs, build output and earlier tarballs.
  cpSync(ROOT, stage, {
    recursive: true,
    filter: (src) => !/(?:^|[\\/])(?:\.git|node_modules|dist|coverage)$|\.tgz$/.test(path.relative(ROOT, src)),
  });
  symlinkSync(realpathSync(path.join(ROOT, 'node_modules')), path.join(stage, 'node_modules'), 'dir');
  const build = spawnSync(process.execPath, [TSC, '-p', 'tsconfig.build.json'], { cwd: stage, encoding: 'utf8' });
  if (build.status !== 0) throw new Error(`build failed: ${build.stdout}${build.stderr}`);
  const pack = npm(['pack', '--json', '--ignore-scripts', '--pack-destination', work], stage);
  if (pack.status !== 0) throw new Error(`npm pack failed: ${pack.stderr}`);
  const [first] = JSON.parse(pack.stdout) as { filename: string; files: { path: string }[] }[];
  packed = { filename: first?.filename ?? '', files: (first?.files ?? []).map((f) => f.path).sort() };
  const deps = realpathSync(path.join(ROOT, 'node_modules'));
  smoke = runSmoke([path.join(work, packed.filename), '--deps-from', deps, '--time-scale', '10']);
  // The same package with one packed golden changed: its own corpus no longer passes.
  const broken = path.join(work, 'broken');
  mkdirSync(broken);
  appendFileSync(path.join(stage, 'conformance', 'expected', 'headings.html'), 'x');
  const repack = npm(['pack', '--json', '--ignore-scripts', '--pack-destination', broken], stage);
  if (repack.status !== 0) throw new Error(`npm pack failed: ${repack.stderr}`);
  brokenSmoke = runSmoke([path.join(broken, packed.filename), '--deps-from', deps, '--time-scale', '10']);
}, 300_000);

afterAll(() => {
  if (work !== '') rmSync(work, { recursive: true, force: true });
});

describe('npm pack', () => {
  it('names the tarball as CI expects it', () => {
    expect(packed.filename).toBe(TARBALL);
    expect(TARBALL).toBe('synapsium-labs-docserver-0.1.0.tgz');
  });

  it('holds both entries with their types, the corpus files, the licence and the readme', () => {
    for (const must of [
      'dist/render/index.js',
      'dist/render/index.d.ts',
      'dist/conformance/index.js',
      'dist/conformance/index.d.ts',
      'conformance/manifest.json',
      'conformance/hostile.json',
      'conformance/DEPARTURES.json',
      'conformance/expected/headings.html',
      'LICENSE',
      'README.md',
      'package.json',
    ]) {
      expect(packed.files).toContain(must);
    }
  });

  it('holds every file runCorpus reads: each case input and its expected html and meta', () => {
    const needed = manifest
      .filter((m) => m.kind !== 'generated')
      .flatMap((m) => [`conformance/corpus/${m.id}.md`, `conformance/expected/${m.id}.html`, `conformance/expected/${m.id}.meta.json`]);
    expect(needed.length).toBe(156);
    expect(needed.filter((f) => !packed.files.includes(f))).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('holds nothing else: no references, scripts, sources, tests, CI files or working papers', () => {
    expect(packed.files.filter((f) => !ALLOWED.some((re) => re.test(f)))).toEqual([]);
    expect(packed.files.filter((f) => /^(?:conformance\/reference|scripts|src|test|docs|\.github)\//.test(f))).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('the packed package, imported by name', () => {
  it('passes the whole corpus through the consumer smoke', () => {
    expect(smoke?.stderr).toBe('');
    expect(smoke?.stdout).toBe(
      [
        'consumer-smoke: installed the tarball offline',
        'consumer-smoke: @synapsium-labs/docserver/render resolves into node_modules',
        'consumer-smoke: a deep import is refused (ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED)',
        'consumer-smoke: 77 of 77 cases passed',
        '',
      ].join('\n'),
    );
    expect(smoke?.status).toBe(0);
  });

  it('fails, naming the case, when the packed corpus does not pass', () => {
    const lines = brokenSmoke?.stdout.split('\n') ?? [];
    expect(lines.slice(0, 4)).toEqual([
      'consumer-smoke: installed the tarball offline',
      'consumer-smoke: @synapsium-labs/docserver/render resolves into node_modules',
      'consumer-smoke: a deep import is refused (ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED)',
      'consumer-smoke: 76 of 77 cases passed',
    ]);
    expect(lines[4]).toMatch(/^consumer-smoke: headings: html differs at offset \d+/);
    expect(brokenSmoke?.status).toBe(1);
  });
});

describe('scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs: refusals', () => {
  const USAGE = 'usage: node scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs <tarball> [--deps-from <node_modules>] [--time-scale <n>]\n';

  it('a bad command line exits 2 with the usage line', () => {
    const bad = [
      [],
      ['--deps-from', 'x'],
      ['a.tgz', '--deps-from'],
      ['a.tgz', '--other', 'x'],
      ['a.tgz', '--deps-from', 'x', 'y'],
      ['a.tgz', '--deps-from', 'x', '--deps-from', 'y'],
      ['a.tgz', '--time-scale', '0'],
      ['a.tgz', '--time-scale', 'fast'],
    ];
    for (const args of bad) expect(runSmoke(args)).toMatchObject({ status: 2, stdout: '', stderr: USAGE });
  });

  it('a tarball that cannot be unpacked exits 1 and says which command failed', () => {
    const r = runSmoke([path.join(work, 'no-such.tgz'), '--deps-from', path.join(ROOT, 'node_modules')]);
    expect(r.status).toBe(1);
    expect(r.stdout).toBe('');
    expect(r.stderr).toMatch(/^consumer-smoke: tar -xzf \S+no-such\.tgz -C \S+ exited \d+$/m);
  });
});
```

```ts
// The README documents what ships (docserver L1, Task 12; architecture section F T12). Each runtime export of
// both entries, the three default limits, the allowlist, every departure category, the warning that ids may
// collide (ruling C22) and the consumer's corpus call is named there, so a new export or a new departure cannot
// ship undocumented. The words around them are not pinned; the names are.

import * as render from '../src/render/index.js';

  category: string;
}[];

/** The categories with no file to move (PD1 compares code as text; PD5-PD8 move no golden), then those that do. */
const CATEGORIES = [...new Set(['PD1', 'PD5', 'PD6', 'PD7', 'PD8', ...departures.map((d) => d.category)])].sort();

describe('README', () => {
  it('names every runtime export of ./render and ./conformance', () => {
    const names = [...Object.keys(render), ...Object.keys(conformance)].sort();
    expect(names).toHaveLength(13);
    expect(names.filter((n) => !README.includes(`\`${n}\``) && !README.includes(`\`${n}(`))).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('states the default limits with their values, the html bound among them', () => {
```

(b) Create `scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs` with exactly this content:

```js
// The packed-consumer smoke (docserver L1; architecture section F, Task 12).
//
//   node scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs <tarball>                            install from the registry (CI)
//   node scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs <tarball> --deps-from <node_modules>  offline (test/pack.test.ts)
//   ... [--time-scale <n>]                                               runCorpus's timeScale (default 1)
//
// It makes a throwaway consumer project, installs the packed tarball there, and runs a check from inside that
// project, so every import resolves by package name through the tarball's own exports map, never through this
// checkout. The check imports `@synapsium-labs/docserver/render` and `/conformance`, confirms the entry
// resolved into the consumer's node_modules and that a deep import past the exports map is refused, and runs
// runCorpus(render, { scanRefs }). It exits 0 only when every case passes, 1 when the check fails, 2 on a usage
// error. Without --deps-from, `npm install` fetches the package's dependencies from the registry, as a real
// consumer would; with it, the tarball is unpacked as the package and its dependencies are linked from an
// installed tree, and nothing touches the network. --time-scale multiplies every verdict's maxMs, for a busy
// machine (the test passes one; CI does not). Node built-ins only; dev tooling, never shipped.
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, renameSync, rmSync, symlinkSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';

const PACKAGE = '@synapsium-labs/docserver';

/** Runs inside the consumer project; every specifier resolves from there. */
const check = (timeScale) => `import { render, scanRefs } from '${PACKAGE}/render';
import { runCorpus } from '${PACKAGE}/conformance';

const say = (line) => console.log(\`consumer-smoke: \${line}\`);
let ok = true;

const resolved = import.meta.resolve('${PACKAGE}/render');
if (resolved.endsWith('/node_modules/${PACKAGE}/dist/render/index.js')) {
  say('${PACKAGE}/render resolves into node_modules');
} else {
  ok = false;
  say(\`${PACKAGE}/render resolves outside the installed package: \${resolved}\`);
}

try {
  await import('${PACKAGE}/dist/render/index.js');
  ok = false;
  say('a deep import resolved: the exports map must be the whole public surface');
} catch (e) {
  if (e?.code === 'ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED') say('a deep import is refused (ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED)');
  else {
    ok = false;
    say(\`a deep import failed for another reason: \${String(e)}\`);
  }
}

const run = runCorpus(render, { scanRefs, timeScale: ${timeScale} });
say(\`\${run.passed} of \${run.total} cases passed\`);
for (const r of run.results) if (!r.ok) say(\`\${r.id}: \${r.failures.join(' | ')}\`);
process.exitCode = ok && run.ok ? 0 : 1;
`;

function usage() {
  console.error('usage: node scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs <tarball> [--deps-from <node_modules>] [--time-scale <n>]');
  return 2;
}

/** Run a command to completion; its output goes to stderr, so stdout carries only the smoke's own lines. */
function run(cmd, args, cwd) {
  const r = spawnSync(cmd, args, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8' });
  if (r.status !== 0) {
    process.stderr.write(`${r.stdout ?? ''}${r.stderr ?? ''}`);
    throw new Error(`consumer-smoke: ${cmd} ${args.join(' ')} exited ${String(r.status)}`);
  }
}

/** Unpack the tarball as node_modules/<PACKAGE> and link each of its dependencies from `depsFrom`. */
function installOffline(tarball, depsFrom, dir) {
  const scope = path.join(dir, 'node_modules', path.dirname(PACKAGE));
  mkdirSync(scope, { recursive: true });
  run('tar', ['-xzf', tarball, '-C', scope], dir);
  const target = path.join(dir, 'node_modules', PACKAGE);
  renameSync(path.join(scope, 'package'), target);
  const { dependencies = {} } = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(target, 'package.json'), 'utf8'));
  for (const name of Object.keys(dependencies)) {
    const link = path.join(dir, 'node_modules', name);
    mkdirSync(path.dirname(link), { recursive: true });
    symlinkSync(path.join(depsFrom, name), link, 'dir');
  }
}

/** The command line: the tarball, then each option at most once, each with its value; null when malformed. */
function parseArgs(argv) {
  const [tarball, ...rest] = argv;
  if (tarball === undefined || tarball.startsWith('--') || rest.length % 2 !== 0) return null;
  const options = new Map();
  for (let i = 0; i < rest.length; i += 2) {
    const [flag, value] = [rest[i], rest[i + 1]];
    if (!['--deps-from', '--time-scale'].includes(flag) || options.has(flag)) return null;
    options.set(flag, value);
  }
  const timeScale = Number(options.get('--time-scale') ?? '1');
  if (!(Number.isFinite(timeScale) && timeScale > 0)) return null;
  const deps = options.get('--deps-from');
  return { tarball: path.resolve(tarball), depsFrom: deps === undefined ? null : path.resolve(deps), timeScale };
}

function main(argv) {
  const args = parseArgs(argv);
  if (args === null) return usage();
  const { tarball, depsFrom, timeScale } = args;
  const dir = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), 'docserver-consumer-'));
  try {
    const project = { name: 'docserver-consumer-smoke', version: '0.0.0', private: true, type: 'module' };
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'package.json'), `${JSON.stringify(project, null, 2)}\n`);
    if (depsFrom === null) {
      run('npm', ['install', '--no-save', '--no-audit', '--no-fund', '--ignore-scripts', tarball], dir);
      console.log('consumer-smoke: installed the tarball from the registry');
    } else {
      installOffline(tarball, depsFrom, dir);
      console.log('consumer-smoke: installed the tarball offline');
    }
    writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'check.mjs'), check(timeScale));
    const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, ['check.mjs'], { cwd: dir, stdio: 'inherit' });
    return r.status === 0 ? 0 : 1;
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(String(e instanceof Error ? e.message : e));
    return 1;
  } finally {
    rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

process.exitCode = main(process.argv.slice(2));
```

(c) Replace `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with exactly this content (the header's first lines and the last three steps are new):

```yaml
name: ci

# Typecheck, test and build on every pull request and every push to main, on Node 22 and 24; then refuse a
# weakened hostile verdict or an unnamed golden move (the ratchet), and install the packed tarball in a
# throwaway project and run the corpus through its public entries (the consumer smoke). The ratchet's base is
# the pull request's base branch; on a push, main's tip before the push, so every commit the push adds is read
# (HEAD^ only for a push that has no previous tip); by hand, origin/main.
# The token is read-only; a later job that needs more asks for it in its own diff.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  test:
    name: test (${{ matrix.node }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: [22, 24]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run
      - run: npm run build
      - name: ratchet
        env:
          BASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('origin/{0}', github.base_ref) || github.event_name == 'push' && github.event.before != '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' && github.event.before || github.event_name == 'push' && 'HEAD^' || 'origin/main' }}
        run: node scripts/ratchet.mjs --base "${BASE}"
      - run: npm pack
      - run: node scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs ./synapsium-labs-docserver-0.1.0.tgz
```

(e) Replace `README.md` with exactly this content:

````markdown
# docserver

One shared renderer for spec and plan documents written in Markdown. It turns Markdown into the rich reading layout: a contents sidebar, "In short" and "Where things stand" boxes, status labels, figure cards for Mermaid diagrams, quick jump, a glossary on hover, an Index of defined IDs, "Changes since", read marks, and light and dark themes.

It is pure. It does no network, storage, auth, git or hosting. Each product that uses it brings its own transport, login, content source and hosting, and pins one exact version.

**Status:** pre-release and private until v1, which goes public under the MIT licence as `@synapsium-labs/docserver`.

## What it holds

| Part | Entry point | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Markdown rules (markdown-it, TypeScript): GitHub-style Markdown, alerts, figure captions, front matter, heading ids, a short raw-HTML allowlist | `@synapsium-labs/docserver/render`: `render()`, `scanRefs()` | Built |
| The conformance corpus: Markdown in, expected HTML out, plus hostile cases | `@synapsium-labs/docserver/conformance`: `runCorpus()`, `loadCorpus()` | Built |
| The rich layout | `enhance(root, options)` | Planned |
| Fonts, a self-hosted Mermaid, and an asset manifest with hashes | `assets/` | Planned |
| A sandboxed-frame document builder, and a host helper | `frameDocument()`, `mountDocFrame()` | Planned |

The package exports exactly `./render`, `./conformance` and `./package.json`; nothing else is importable.

## Rendering: `./render`

```ts
import { render, scanRefs } from '@synapsium-labs/docserver/render';

const r = render(markdown, { maxBytes: 1_048_576, lineAttrs: true });
if (r.outcome === 'rendered') {
  showFragment(r.html); // the html is safe markup by the allowlist below
  for (const h of r.meta.headings) {
    const link = document.createElement('a');
    link.href = `#${h.id}`;
    link.textContent = h.text; // meta holds the author's plain text, never markup
    contents.append(link);
  }
}
```

`./render` runs unchanged in Node, browsers and workers. It imports no host API: no network, storage, DOM, Node built-in, clock or randomness, and it keeps no state between calls, so one input and one set of options always give the same output. The tests prove this by bundling it for the browser and running the whole corpus in an empty JavaScript context, where its output must equal Node's byte for byte.

**`render(markdown, options?)`** returns `{ html, outcome, bytes, meta }`.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `outcome` | `'rendered'`; `'over-limit'` when the input is over `maxBytes` UTF-8 bytes (nothing is parsed and `html` is `''`); `'output-over-limit'` when the html would pass `maxHtmlBytes` (rendering stops there); or `'failed'` after an internal error. For the last two, `html` is the escaped source in a `<pre>` under one line saying so, cut to `maxHtmlBytes`. Never raw input HTML. |
| `html` | An HTML fragment. |
| `bytes` | The input's UTF-8 length; when over the limit, the count at which counting stopped (`maxBytes + 1`). |
| `meta.title` | The text of the first level-1 heading, or `null`. |
| `meta.headings` | Every heading: `{ level, id, text }`, in document order. |
| `meta.front`, `meta.frontList` | The front matter as a record with a null prototype (a list value stays a list) and as `{ key, list, vals }` entries in source order; both `null` when there is none. |
| `meta.figures`, `meta.tables` | How many Mermaid figures and tables were rendered. |
| `meta.mermaidKinds` | The distinct diagram keywords of the rendered Mermaid fences, in order, at most 32. |

Unless the outcome is `'rendered'`, `meta` is a frozen empty meta. Every string in `meta` (a heading's `text`, `title`, front-matter keys and values) is the author's plain text, not escaped: `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` in a heading arrives as those characters. Insert it with `textContent`, or escape it; never build markup from it. Only `html` is safe to insert as markup.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `maxBytes` | `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES`, 4194304 (4 MiB) | UTF-8 byte cap on the input. Counting stops at the cap, so measuring an oversized input costs no more than the cap. It bounds the input only; `maxHtmlBytes` bounds the html. |
| `maxHtmlBytes` | 16777216 (16 MiB, four times `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES`) | UTF-8 byte cap on the html. An input under `maxBytes` can still expand far past it (a reference definition with a long URL, used many times, repeats the URL at each use), so the html is counted as it is rendered and the render stops at the first piece that would pass the cap, with outcome `'output-over-limit'`. No ordinary document comes near the default. |
| `lineAttrs` | `true` | Put `data-line="a-b"` (the block's source lines) on block elements. |

**`scanRefs(markdown, options?)`** parses without rendering and returns `{ outcome, images, imagesTruncated, mermaid }`: the distinct image sources `render()` would emit, in order and at most `maxImages` (default `DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGES`, 512) with `imagesTruncated` saying whether more exist, and the count and UTF-8 sizes (largest and total) of the Mermaid fences `render()` would turn into figures. It takes the same `maxBytes`, and its `outcome` is `'over-limit'` exactly when `render()`'s would be.

### What it renders

- CommonMark with GitHub tables (wrapped in `<div class="table-wrapper">`; short rows are padded with at most 65536 empty cells in the whole document), strikethrough, task lists and footnotes. Raw HTML is off; only the allowlist below is recognised.
- Heading ids on every level: the heading's text lower-cased, spaces turned into `-`, and everything but letters, digits, `_`, `-` and CJK ideographs removed, with `-1`, `-2` and so on for repeats. Heading ids, `<!-- id:X -->` anchors and the footnotes' `fn1` and `fnref1` ids share one namespace with no prefix, so an author can write an id that another element also has, and ids may collide. A host must never look up an element of a rendered document by a document id (`getElementById`, `querySelector('#...')`, or a named property of `window` or `document`); it walks the fragment it inserted instead.
- Fenced code highlighted by highlight.js, in `<div class="codehilite"><pre><code class="hljs language-NAME">`. The language comes only from a fixed list (bash, shell, css, diff, dockerfile, go, ini, java, javascript, json, markdown, python, rust, sql, typescript, xml, yaml, plaintext, and their usual aliases); any other fence is escaped plain text, and the language is never guessed. Highlighting is bounded: a fence with a line over 256 characters, or one that would take a document past 256 KiB of highlighted code, keeps its language class and shows escaped plain text.
- A `mermaid` fence becomes `<figure class="mermaid-figure"><pre class="mermaid">` with its source escaped as text. A paragraph right after it that is wholly `*Figure N. ...*` becomes its `<figcaption>`.
- `> [!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]` and `[!CAUTION]` blockquotes become `<div class="gh-alert gh-note">` callouts (uppercase markers only).
- YAML front matter at the very start, between `---` lines, becomes a `<dl class="doc-meta">` strip: at most 40 keys, values cut at 500 characters, lists at 50 items, and nothing at all for a block of 20000 characters or more. Scalars show the text the author wrote (`1.0`, `.inf`, `0o17`, `yes` and dates stay as written), except that `null` shows empty and booleans show `true` or `false`: the schema is YAML's failsafe one plus null, bool and the merge key `<<`, with no number types and no other tags.
- Links keep markdown-it's own check: `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` and non-image `data:` URLs stay text.

### The raw-HTML allowlist

The same list in every environment, exported as `ALLOWLIST`. Each form is matched exactly and emitted from fixed markup; everything else is escaped and shown as text.

| Input | Where | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `<br>`, `<br/>`, `<br />` | inline | `<br />` |
| `<sup>`, `<sub>`, `<kbd>` and their closers, with no attributes | inline | the same tag, lower case; past 64 open levels of one tag in a document, the opener and the closer that pairs with it stay text |
| `<!-- any comment -->` | inline, or a block of its own | nothing |
| `<!-- id:X -->` alone on its line, `X` matching `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}` | block | `<span class="doc-anchor" id="X"></span>` |
| `<details>`, `<details open>`, `</details>` alone on a line | block | the same tag; a stray closer is dropped, a details left open is closed at the end of the document, and past 64 open levels the opener and the closer that pairs with it stay text |
| `<summary>text</summary>` alone on a line | block | the same, with the text escaped |

## The conformance corpus: `./conformance`

The corpus is the contract: what `render()` must produce, shipped with the package so any host can check its own renderer or build against it.

| Kind | Cases | Judged by |
|---|---|---|
| golden | 37 | `conformance/corpus/<id>.md` in, `conformance/expected/<id>.html` and `.meta.json` out, compared exactly |
| hostile | 15 | a golden, plus a verdict in `conformance/hostile.json` (strings that must never appear, bounds on depth and time) |
| generated | 25 | a verdict only; the input is built from a small spec on the consumer's machine (deep nesting, long delimiter runs, huge tables, comment and heading floods, pathological code, an over-limit input, an html expansion past `maxHtmlBytes`) |

Every case is also checked by an output-safety oracle: only known tags, attributes, classes and URL schemes may appear. Code inside a highlighted block is compared as text, so a host may use another highlighter's markup.

To run it in your own CI against the renderer you ship:

```js
import { render, scanRefs } from '@synapsium-labs/docserver/render';
import { runCorpus } from '@synapsium-labs/docserver/conformance';

const run = runCorpus(render, { scanRefs });
for (const r of run.results) if (!r.ok) console.error(r.id, r.failures.join('\n  '));
if (!run.ok) process.exit(1);
```

`runCorpus(renderFn, { only, scanRefs, timeScale })` returns `{ ok, total, passed, results }`, one result per case with its failures. Pass `scanRefs`, or the case that bounds image scanning fails and says so. `timeScale` multiplies every time bound for a slow machine; it never changes a verdict. `loadCorpus()` returns the cases themselves, and `normaliseForCompare`, `checkOutputSafety`, `evaluateVerdict`, `buildInput`, `inputSize` and `MAX_INPUT_BYTES` are exported for hosts that judge cases their own way.

### Departures from the reference renderer

The goldens were produced by the Python renderer these rules were ported from. The port matches it byte for byte except in these categories, each listed per case in `conformance/DEPARTURES.json` where it moves a file:

| Category | Departure |
|---|---|
| PD1 | Code highlighting: highlight.js replaces Pygments, so code inside `div.codehilite` is compared as text (no file moves). |
| PD2 | Front matter scalars render their source text: `null` renders empty, booleans render `true` and `false`, and every other scalar (`1.50`, `.inf`, `017`, `yes`, `on`, dates) stays as written, where the reference printed Python's values. |
| PD3 | `meta.front` and `meta.frontList` come from the same front-matter block the strip renders, so CRLF files, `----` and `...` fences agree. |
| PD4 | One leading byte order mark is removed before parsing. |
| PD5 | Allowlisted tag names fold ASCII letters only; look-alike letters that only Unicode case folding equates stay text (no file moves). |
| PD6 | Reference labels: markdown-it normalises a link's label with JavaScript's whitespace and the reference with Python's, so a label holding U+001C-U+001F, U+0085 or U+FEFF can match a different definition, or none (no file moves). |
| PD7 | A figure caption never comes from a tight list's hidden paragraph and never reaches past the block after its figure, so the output stays balanced (no file moves). |
| PD8 | Bounds that only hostile documents reach: short table rows add at most 65536 empty cells in the whole document; html past `maxHtmlBytes` stops with `'output-over-limit'`; and `details`, `sup`, `sub` and `kbd` nest at most 64 open levels each, a deeper opener and the closer that pairs with it staying text (no file moves). |

A change that moves any file under `conformance/expected/` names the moved case ids in a `Goldens-moved: <id>, <id>` commit trailer, and a hostile verdict may only tighten: `node scripts/ratchet.mjs --base <ref>` refuses anything else, and CI runs it on every change.

## Build and test

Node 22 or later. Every dependency is pinned to an exact version and installed from the committed lockfile.

```sh
npm ci                            # install exactly what package-lock.json records
npm run typecheck                 # the whole tree, then src/render alone with no host types
./node_modules/.bin/vitest run    # every test; one file: ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/package.test.ts
npm run build                     # dist/ from src/
```

- Run the local `vitest` binary, never a bare `npx vitest`, which can resolve a different global copy.
- Tests never reach a network: `test/setup/no-network.ts` makes `fetch` and every socket connect throw, and the packing test runs npm offline.
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs those four steps on Node 22 and 24, on pull requests and on `main`, then the verdict ratchet against the base branch (on a push, against `main` before the push), then `npm pack` and `scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs`, which installs the tarball in a throwaway project from the registry and runs the corpus through the package's public entries.
- A new or bumped dependency is an exact version at least 14 days old. Add it with
  `npm install --save-exact --before=<a date 14 days back> <name>@<x.y.z>`; npm then refuses a younger version.

## Design

The design lives in ccrc's spec: [Rich Docs reader and a shared renderer](https://github.com/Synapsium-Labs/ccrc-pwa/blob/main/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-rich-docs-reader-and-shared-renderer-design.md), §3. The programme ledger is [`docs/superpowers/programs/docserver.md`](docs/superpowers/programs/docserver.md).

## Licence

MIT. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). Bundled third-party files keep their own licences, listed in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES` once they ship.
````

```
ci: purity, browser parity, public-readiness and the packed-consumer smoke (docserver L1)

./render is proven pure three ways from its source (the purity
typecheck, which loads no DOM library; its import graph; its
identifiers) and once by running:
an esbuild browser bundle in an empty VM context passes the whole
corpus and matches Node's output byte for byte. A scanner keeps
home paths, private hosts and addresses, personal e-mail and
credentials out of the tree. The packed tarball holds the entries
and the corpus and nothing else, and scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs
installs it and runs the corpus through its public entries, offline
in the tests and from the registry in CI, after the verdict ratchet.
The README documents the API, that meta holds plain text and that ids
may collide, the allowlist, the corpus and the departures; the ratchet
on a push reads every commit the push adds; and the build tests run
alone after the rest.
```
